specs.title: SUPPRESS WHEN literal phrase on the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause (indexed files)

spec.construct: C6B-suppress-when-altkey — SUPPRESS WHEN literal-1 phrase on the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause (indexed files, COBOL-2023)

specCitations.what: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause general format — the SUPPRESS WHEN phrase's position (after WITH DUPLICATES, both optional/independent)
specCitations.quote: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY IS  { data-name-1 } / { record-key-name-1 SOURCE IS { data-name-2 } ... }   [ WITH DUPLICATES ]     [ SUPPRESS WHEN literal-1 ]

specCitations.what: literal-1 category / ALL-literal length constraint
specCitations.quote: Literal-1 shall be an alphanumeric literal, a national literal, or a figurative constant, and shall be of the same category as data-name-1 or data-name-2. If ALL literal is specified, the literal shall be one character long.

specCitations.what: the alternate key's own category (fixes what 'same category as data-name-1' can be)
specCitations.quote: Data-name-1 and data-name-2 shall be defined as a data item of category alphanumeric or national within a record description entry associated with the file-name to which the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause is subordinate.

specCitations.what: THE governing general rule: suppression establishes a WRITE/REWRITE-time key value that withholds the alternate access path
specCitations.quote: Literal-1 establishes the key suppression value for this alternate record key for WRITE and REWRITE statements. Alternate record key suppression specifies that an alternate record key access path to a particular record shall not be provided when the value of data-name-1 or record-key-name-1 in that record is equal to literal-1.

specCitations.what: the READ/START consequence — suppressed records are invisible under that key of reference
specCitations.quote: The suppression does not impact READ and START although the suppressed records will not be processed by these statements. It is as if they did not exist.

specCitations.what: WRITE-time suppression + the no-duplicate-condition tail
specCitations.quote: For each alternate record key for which alternate record key suppression is specified and for which the value of the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY phrase is equal to the literal specified in that phrase: a) the access path to the record using this alternate record key shall not be provided, and b) the record shall be logically positioned so that it will not be found when accessed using the alternate record key. Any number of records may have the same alternate key value equal to its key suppression value without requiring the DUPLICATES phrase to be specified for that key. Key entries that are suppressed shall not cause a duplicate key condition to exist.

specCitations.what: dynamic maintenance of the path in BOTH directions on REWRITE
specCitations.quote: If the SUPPRESS WHEN phrase is specified in the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause and the value of the alternate record key is no longer equal to the literal specified in that phrase: 1. an access path to this record using this key of reference shall be provided, and 2. the record shall be logically positioned so that it will be found when accessed using the alternate record key. If alternate record key suppression is specified for this alternate record key and the value of this alternate record key is now equal to its key suppression value: 1. the access path to the record using this alternate record key shall no longer be provided, and 2. the record shall be logically repositioned so that it will not be found when accessed using this alternate record key.

specCitations.what: the comparison basis + the duplicate exemption on REWRITE
specCitations.quote: The comparison used for determining changes to the key is based on the collating sequence for the file according to the rules for a relation condition. Any number of records may have the same alternate key value equal to its key suppression value without requiring the DUPLICATES phrase to be specified for that key. Key entries that are suppressed shall not cause a duplicate key condition to exist.

specCitations.what: sequential READ NEXT/PREVIOUS must skip suppressed records under an alternate key of reference
specCitations.quote: If the key of reference is an alternate key, any record identified as being suppressed by the SUPPRESS WHEN phrase of the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause is not considered to exist.

specCitations.what: random READ finds the FIRST record having an equal key value — combined with §12.4.5.6.4 GR6 NOTE ('as if they did not exist') a suppressed record is not a candidate, so an all-suppressed match is '23'
specCitations.quote: execution of a READ statement sets the file position indicator to the value in the key of reference. This value is compared with the value contained in the corresponding data item of the stored records in the file until the first record having an equal value is found. … If no record is so identified, the invalid key condition exists and execution of the READ statement is unsuccessful.

specCitations.what: START ignores suppressed records under an alternate key of reference; unsatisfied ⇒ invalid key
specCitations.quote: If the key of reference is an alternate key, any record identified as being suppressed by the SUPPRESS WHEN phrase of the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause is ignored. Then, either: 1. The file position indicator is set to the value of the key of reference in the first logical record whose key satisfies the comparison, or 2. If the comparison is not satisfied by any record in the file, the invalid key condition exists and the execution of the START statement is unsuccessful.

specCitations.what: EXTERNAL file connectors must agree on the SUPPRESS WHEN phrase — extends the existing SELECT fingerprint
specCitations.quote: The same data description entry for data-name-2 and each data-name-3 as well as their relative location within the associated record, the same number of alternate record keys, the same SUPPRESS WHEN phrase, and the same DUPLICATES phrase.

specCitations.what: the SUPPRESS WHEN attribute is a FIXED file attribute of the physical file
specCitations.quote: Other fixed attributes of the physical file provided through COBOL are prime record key, alternate record keys, SUPPRESS WHEN attribute, code set, …

specCitations.what: edition provenance — a COBOL-2023 addition
specCitations.quote: — Alternate key suppression on indexed files using the SUPPRESS WHEN phrase of the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause … 42) SUPPRESS WHEN phrase. The SUPPRESS WHEN phrase may be specified as part of the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause to suppress access to a record via a particular alternate record key when the value of this key equals the value specified in this phrase.

superseded_by.why: REFUTED — the two C6-A claims in this object only. `summary` says C6-A (WRITE BEFORE AND AFTER ADVANCING) IS FULLY LANDED end-to-end with the grammar reading `writeBeforeAfter : writeAdvancePhrase writeAdvancePhrase?` and MUST NOT be re-implemented, and `evidence` names src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolIO.g4:357-366 for it. kb/Work/PB712 measured the phrase off the RENDERED PDF page (printed folio 785), as CLAUDE.md rule 1 requires: §14.9.51.2 Format 1's choice indicators enclose only the two WORDS BEFORE and AFTER, with ONE ADVANCING and ONE operand outside them (§5.2.6.4). The repeated-phrase rule therefore REJECTED the only printed spelling of the 2023 combination, `WRITE R BEFORE AFTER ADVANCING 4 LINES`, and ACCEPTED a two-operand form the standard never prints, which advanced the linage counter twice and silently lost an end-of-page condition. The rule now reads `(BEFORE AFTER? | AFTER BEFORE?) ADVANCING? (PAGE | operand (LINE|LINES)?)`, `writeAdvancePhrase` is DELETED, and SR17 moved to StatementValidation.CheckWriteBeforeAfterPage as COBOLNET1910. So C6-A was not fully landed and DID need re-implementing — and this artefact is what told the implementer not to look, which is the harm kb/Work/PB785 records. The C6-B findings in this object (the SUPPRESS WHEN phrase on ALTERNATE RECORD KEY, unlanded) are untouched by this refutation; the path:line coordinates throughout are as of 2026-07-20 and several now land on different code.

grammarChanges.change: extend rule — append an optional trailing SUPPRESS WHEN phrase as its own sub-rule reference
grammarChanges.orderingNote: No alternative-ordering change is required. The new phrase is a TRAILING optional suffix of an existing rule, keyword-led by the hard-reserved SUPPRESS. It cannot be confused with any other fileControlClauses alternative (none begins with SUPPRESS) and cannot be swallowed by the preceding `dataReference` (SUPPRESS is a reserved token, so cobolWord cannot match it). The rule is NOT shared across sections (alternateKeyClause is referenced only from fileControlClauses), so the DEVLOG-736 shared-rule over-fire hazard does not apply. Keep `alternateKeySuppressWhen` as a SEPARATE rule (not inlined) so the parse-arm gate has a dedicated Visit method and fires exactly once per phrase.

Add `private string? SuppressValue(Core.AlternateKeySuppressWhenContext ctx, DataItem key)` implementing §12.4.5.6.3 SR7 COMPLETELY:
- `var lit = ctx.literal();`
- If `lit.numericLiteral() is not null` ⇒ Error COBOLNET1578 (literal-1 shall be alphanumeric, national, or a figurative constant), return null.
- Let `nn = lit.nonNumericLiteral()`. If `nn.BOOLLIT() is not null` ⇒ COBOLNET1578 (boolean is not an admitted class). If `nn.concatenationExpression() is not null` ⇒ fold via the existing ConcatFolder and treat the folded literal as the operand (§8.8.3.3 GR3 makes a concatenation usable anywhere a literal may be).
- CATEGORY match (SR7 'shall be of the same category as data-name-1'): the key's category is alphanumeric or national (SR2). If `key.Pic?.Category is PicCategory.National` the literal must be NATLIT or a national-usable figurative; otherwise it must be STRINGLIT/HEXLIT or an alphanumeric figurative. Mismatch ⇒ COBOLNET1578.
- ALL-literal length (SR7 sentence 2): `if (nn.figurativeConstant() is { } fg && fg.ALL() is not null)` decode the ALL operand; if its decoded length != 1 ⇒ Error COBOLNET1579, return null.
- VALUE COMPUTATION: a FIGURATIVE constant (ZERO/SPACE/QUOTE/HIGH-VALUE/LOW-VALUE, with or without ALL) has 'the length required by the context' — the context here is the KEY ITEM, so expand it to exactly `key.ImageWidth` characters using `CobolNet.CodeGen.FigurativeConstants.KindOf` + `FillChar` (the ONE figurative service, DESIGN-codegen-backend §2.5 rationale #6). An `ALL "x"` figurative expands its single character to key.ImageWidth. A PLAIN alphanumeric/national/hex literal is returned AS WRITTEN (decoded via CobolLiteral.Decode / DecodeHex) with NO padding or truncation — the runtime performs the §14.9.51 GR35 relation-condition comparison, which space-extends the shorter operand; padding here would be correct but truncation would be WRONG (a literal longer than the key can never compare equal, and the runtime comparison expresses that faithfully).

diagnostics.message: SUPPRESS WHEN literal-1 on the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause shall be an alphanumeric literal, a national literal, or a figurative constant, and shall be of the same category as the alternate record key (ISO §12.4.5.6.3 SR7; the key itself is category alphanumeric or national per SR2) — a numeric or boolean literal, or a literal whose category differs from the key's, is rejected.
When the SUPPRESS WHEN literal on the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause is specified as ALL literal, the literal shall be one character long (ISO §12.4.5.6.3 SR7).

editionGating.behaviorByEdition: COBOL-85: REJECT — COBOLNET0900 via the ParseArm gate on alternateKeySuppressWhen (the clause parses at every --std; the superset grammar carries no {isXXXX()}? gate). COBOL-2002: REJECT — COBOLNET0900. COBOL-2014: REJECT — COBOLNET0900. COBOL-2023 (the default --std): ACCEPT — full bind/emit/runtime suppression semantics per §12.4.5.6.4 GR6, §14.9.51 GR41, §14.9.35 GR24, §14.9.30 GR21c/GR32, §14.9.41 GR17e. The bare ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause and its WITH DUPLICATES phrase are edition-invariant (85+) and MUST NOT be affected — the gate fires only on the presence of the SUPPRESS WHEN phrase's own parse rule. COBOLNET1578/1579 (SR7 violations) are EDITION-INVARIANT within the accepting edition: they fire at 2023; below 2023 the 0900 introduction gate fires first and the SR7 checks are additionally reported (both accumulate — the pass runs after bind so semantic errors also collect, DESIGN-version-conformance-pipeline §2).

OPEN OUTPUT; WRITE four records: (P001,'AAAA'), (P002,'    ')[suppressed], (P003,'BBBB'), (P004,'    ')[suppressed, and a SECOND record with the suppression value under a NO-DUPLICATES-needed key]. CLOSE; OPEN INPUT; START IXF KEY NOT LESS THAN IX-ALT with IX-ALT = LOW-VALUES; then READ IXF NEXT repeatedly until AT END, DISPLAYing IX-PRIME. Expected stdout: exactly `P001` then `P003` then `END` — the two space-keyed records are invisible under the alternate key of reference. Then a second leg: READ IXF KEY IS IX-PRIME with IX-PRIME='P002' succeeds and DISPLAYs its IX-ALT — proving the record is fully intact via the prime path (the record is suppressed only under that ALT key).

tests.covers: §14.9.35 GR24 — dynamic maintenance in BOTH directions on REWRITE (path withdrawn when the value becomes the suppression value; path (re)provided + repositioned when it moves away)

(a) READ P002 by prime, MOVE SPACES TO IX-ALT, REWRITE ⇒ FS `00`; then START on IX-ALT LOW-VALUES + READ NEXT loop ⇒ only P001, P003 appear. (b) READ P002 by prime, MOVE 'ZZZZ' TO IX-ALT, REWRITE ⇒ FS `00`; re-run the alternate walk ⇒ P001, P003, P002 (ZZZZ collates last) — the path was re-provided. (c) With DUPLICATES on the key, REWRITE a record's IX-ALT from a suppressed value to an EXISTING duplicate value ⇒ FS `02` and the record is positioned LAST in the duplicate set (GR24b) — assert the READ NEXT order.

designDefects: ⛔ PRIMARY DEFECT — THE FIGURATIVE-CONSTANT LENGTH PRESCRIPTION CONTRADICTS THE SPEC IT NEVER CITES. The design instructs: 'a FIGURATIVE constant … has "the length required by the context" — the context here is the KEY ITEM, so expand it to exactly key.ImageWidth characters', and pins it with a unit test asserting SUPPRESS WHEN SPACE on a PIC X(6) key yields six spaces and HIGH-VALUE yields six U+00FF, and that ALL "x" expands to key width. **§8.3.3.6.4 is never cited anywhere in the spec.** Its GR3 (ISO_COBOL.md:6376ff) reads: 'When a figurative constant represents a string of one or more characters and the length of the string is **not specified in the rules for the context** in which the figurative constant is used, the length of the string is determined from context by applying the following rules in order: a) … concatenation expression … one character. b) When a figurative constant is other than ALL literal-1, the length of the string is **one character**. c) The length of the string is the length of literal-1.' §12.4.5.6 states NO length for literal-1, so on a plain reading GR3b gives bare SPACE/ZERO/QUOTE/HIGH-VALUE/LOW-VALUE a length of ONE, and GR3c gives ALL "x" a length of ONE (the length of literal-1, which SR7 forces to 1). GR2 (the key-width reading) is reachable only via NOTE 1 ('A figurative constant is associated with a data item … when, for example, the figurative constant is … compared with it'), but GR2's own precondition — 'the length of the string **is** specified in the rules for the context' — is not met. THIS IS DECISION-CHANGING, NOT COSMETIC: on a PIC X(4) key, SUPPRESS WHEN HIGH-VALUE under GR3b suppresses records whose key is 0xFF+3 spaces, whereas under GR2 it suppresses 0xFF×4 — disjoint record sets. Same for ZERO ('0   ' vs '0000') and ALL "*" ('*   ' vs '****'). The design asserts one branch with 'high' confidence and no citation.

THE SAME PRESCRIPTION IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT, WHICH EXPOSES IT AS AD HOC. The design pads figuratives to key.ImageWidth (implying the context DOES specify a length) but returns plain literals 'AS WRITTEN with NO padding or truncation' (implying it does NOT). Both cannot follow from the same reading of §8.3.3.6.4. Whichever branch is adopted must be applied uniformly and cited.

NEW SPEC VIOLATION INTRODUCED BY THE Ordered() FILTER ON START FIRST/LAST — the design demotes it to 'pre-existing divergence, keep the goldens off it'. §14.9.41.4 GR18 (:32236) and GR19 (:32238) say: 'If FIRST is specified, the file position indicator is set to the value of the **primary key** of the first existing logical record in the physical file **and the key of reference is set to the primary key**' (GR19 likewise for LAST). Suppression therefore must NEVER filter a START FIRST/LAST walk. The prescribed edit makes StartFirstLast walk `Ordered(_refKey)` with the filter live whenever _refKey is an alternate — so this change set actively CREATES a GR18/GR19 violation on a path that is currently only mispositioned. It needs a positive guard (StartFirstLast must use keyIndex = -1, per GR18/GR19's 'key of reference is set to the primary key') or an explicitly recorded GAP row — not a note telling the implementer to avoid testing it.

THE SUPPRESSION VALUE IS A FIXED FILE ATTRIBUTE AND THE DESIGN NEVER SAYS IT IS PERSISTED. §9.1.6 (:11238) lists 'SUPPRESS WHEN attribute' among the attributes that 'apply to the file at the time it is created and cannot be changed throughout the lifetime of the file'. The design routes the value only compile-time → RuntimeApi → CobolFile.AddAlternateKey → IndexedConnector._alts, i.e. it lives entirely in the file connector and is re-declared by whatever program opens the file. Nothing writes it to, or reads it back from, the physical file. That makes it a connector attribute, not a fixed file attribute, which is a straight §9.1.6 conformance defect and also the reason defect (D) below has no place to hook.

COBOLNET1578's CATEGORY CHECK WILL OVER-FIRE ON LEGAL LITERALS (see missingSpecBranches B and C for the two concrete classes it wrongly rejects). Because the check is prescribed as an Error, an over-firing category rule turns conforming programs into compile failures — the worst failure mode for a category check. The category logic must be written against the spec's actual literal taxonomy, not an enumeration of five figurative keywords.
missingSpecBranches: (A) §8.3.3.6.4 GR2/GR3 — figurative constant length. Not cited at all; see designDefects. This is the single largest omission.

(B) SYMBOLIC-CHARACTERS ARE FIGURATIVE CONSTANTS AND ARE OMITTED. §8.3.3.6.2 Format 7 is 'ALL symbolic-character-1', and ISO_COBOL.md:5727 states 'A symbolic-character is a user-defined figurative constant that represents a value specified in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph.' §12.4.5.6.3 SR7 admits 'a figurative constant' with no restriction on which, so `SUPPRESS WHEN <symbolic-character>` and `SUPPRESS WHEN ALL <symbolic-character>` are both legal. The design's binder enumerates only ZERO/SPACE/QUOTE/HIGH-VALUE/LOW-VALUE plus ALL literal, and its category test ('an alphanumeric figurative') has no branch for a symbolic-character — COBOLNET1578 would reject a conforming program. Note also §8.3.3.6.3 SR1a is irrelevant here (it restricts only numeric-literal contexts), so no figurative form is excluded by it.

(C) NATIONAL HEXADECIMAL LITERALS (NX"…") ARE OMITTED. ISO_COBOL.md:44865: 'A literal of class national is identified by the opening literal delimiter N", or for hexadecimal literals, NX"'. The design's category rule says a national key requires 'NATLIT or a national-usable figurative' and an alphanumeric key requires 'STRINGLIT/HEXLIT'. An NX"…" literal on a national alternate key is a conforming national literal and would be rejected by COBOLNET1578. The binder must accept the national-hex token (and the implementer must confirm whether the lexer emits a distinct NATHEXLIT or folds it into NATLIT).

(D) THE OPEN '39' FILE-ATTRIBUTE-CONFLICT BRANCH IS ENTIRELY ABSENT. §14.9.27.4 GR10 (:29274): 'During the execution of the OPEN statement when the file connector is matched with the file and the file exists, the attributes of the file connector … are compared with the fixed file attributes of the file. If the attributes don't match, a file attribute conflict condition occurs, the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful, and the I-O status … is set to '39'. **The implementor defines which of the fixed-file attributes are validated** during the execution of the OPEN statement.' §9.1.13 item 7 (:11572) restates '39'. Because §9.1.6 names SUPPRESS WHEN a fixed attribute, the minimum obligation is a DOCUMENTED implementor decision — and Annex A item 129 (:39584) makes it mandatory: 'OPEN statement (validation of fixed file attributes). This item is **required**. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation.' The design proposes neither the check, nor a CONFORMANCE.md / implementor-defined row, nor a GAP row. The parallel DELETE FILE branch (§14.9.10.4 GR18, :26793 — same '39', with an OVERRIDE escape) is likewise unaddressed.

(E) §12.4.5.7 FORMAT 2 (KEY-LEVEL COLLATING SEQUENCE) IS THE CLAUSE THAT ACTUALLY GOVERNS AN ALTERNATE KEY'S COMPARISON, and the design's openQuestion #2 names only the file-level clause. §12.4.5.7.1: 'Multiple collating sequences may be used by specifying a collating sequence clause unique to the primary key or to specific alternate record keys.' §12.4.5.7.3 SR4: 'Data-name-1 shall be a name specified as the data-name in an ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause…'. Since §12.4.5.6.4 GR6 and §14.9.51.4 GR35 both defer to 'the collating sequence for the file', the key-level format is the direct resolution path for a suppressed alternate key and must be named in the GAP row, not just the file-level clause.

(F) §8.8.4.2.7 DEFINES TWO COMPARISON KINDS AND THE DESIGN IMPLEMENTS ONLY ONE. The design cites §8.8.4.2.7 for space-extension. §8.8.4.2.7 in full (:9650ff): 'Two kinds of comparison are defined: standard comparison and locale-based comparison. Locale-based comparison is used when the alphanumeric program collating sequence in effect is locale based; otherwise, standard comparison is used.' The space-extension rule quoted is the STANDARD branch (item 2). The locale branch says 'trailing spaces are truncated from the operands except that an operand consisting of all spaces is truncated to a single space' — which, for the very common SUPPRESS WHEN SPACE case, is a materially different predicate. IsSuppressed hard-codes PadRight + CompareOrdinal with no acknowledgement that the locale branch exists.

(G) §14.9.30.4 GR32's duplicates sentence (see citationErrors) imposes an ORDER requirement on random READ over a duplicate alternate key: 'the first record found is the first record in a sequence of duplicates that was released to the operating environment.' The prescribed ReadRandom edit adds only a visibility filter to an in-place scan of `_recs`; the design never establishes that `_recs` order equals release (Arrival) order after REWRITE re-arrival (`target.Arrival = _nextArrival++`) has reordered logical position without moving the list element. Either scan `Ordered(keyIndex)`/order by Arrival, or state and test the invariant.

(H) §12.4.5.6.4 GR3 ('The data description of data-name-1 or data-name-2 … shall be the same as that used when the physical file was created. The number of alternate record keys for the file shall also be the same…') sits two rules above the GR6 the design implements and is the companion to the §9.1.6 persistence hole in designDefects. It is not mentioned. Record it with (D) as one GAP row rather than leaving the fixed-attribute story silently unaddressed.

specs.title: PICTURE clause EDITING phrase (user-defined insertion editing)

spec.construct: C4-picture-editing — PICTURE clause EDITING phrase (user-defined arbitrary-size simple insertion + sign-sensitive fixed/floating insertion), ISO/IEC 1989:2023 §13.18.40 Format 1

specCitations.what: The general format — the EDITING phrase is a repeatable optional tail on the PICTURE clause; the inner IS/FOR group is itself optional.
specCitations.quote: `PICTURE`/`PIC` … followed by `IS character-string-1`, followed by a large square bracket (optional section) containing: `EDITING character-1` followed by another large square bracket (optional section) containing a left curly brace with two options: top option is `IS literal-1`; bottom option is `FOR` followed by a left curly brace containing two stacked options: `NEGATIVE IS literal-2` (top) and `POSITIVE IS literal-3` (bottom) … then `...` (ellipsis) appears to the right.

specCitations.what: character-1 domain — the exclusion list.
specCitations.quote: Character-1 shall be any basic letter in the COBOL character set except those specified in a CURRENCY-SIGN clause or a basic letter character A, B, C, D, E, N, P, R, S, V, X, Z or their lowercase equivalents.

specCitations.what: Literal class + the 50-character ceiling.
specCitations.quote: If USAGE IS NATIONAL is specified for the subject of the entry or if character-string-1 contains the symbol 'N', literal-1, literal-2, and literal-3 shall be national literals. Otherwise, literal1, literal-2, and literal-3 shall be alphanumeric literals. The total number of characters in literal-1, literal-2, or literal-3 shall not exceed 50.

specCitations.what: character-1 must actually occur in the picture.
specCitations.quote: If the EDITING phrase is specified, the character identified by character-1 shall appear at least once in character-string-1.

specCitations.what: No two EDITING phrases share character-1.
specCitations.quote: If more than one EDITING phrase is specified in one PICTURE clause, no two instances of character-1 shall be the same character.

specCitations.what: The two modes: IS ⇒ fixed(simple) insertion symbol; FOR ⇒ extended editing sign control symbol, numeric/numeric-edited only.
specCitations.quote: If literal-1 is specified, character-1 is a fixed editing sign control symbol. If the FOR phrase is specified, character-1 is an extended editing sign control symbol, character-1 is limited to numeric or numeric-edited data items, and the following rules apply:

specCitations.what: Equal-length literals; the restricted symbol inventory under FOR; the spaces default; the sign-control and floating-point prohibitions.
specCitations.quote: a) Literal-2 and literal-3 shall occupy the same number of character positions. … b) Character-string-1 shall contain character-1 and only the symbols '9', '.', the currency symbol, 'P', 'V', or 'Z'. … c) If only POSITIVE is specified, the default character for the unspecified phrase is the space character repeated for the number of characters in literal-2. If only NEGATIVE is specified, the default character for the unspecified phrase is the space character repeated the number of characters in literal-3. … No editing sign control symbols may be specified in character-string-1. Extended editing sign control symbols shall not be specified for a floating-point edited item.

specCitations.what: The validity requirement for the picture when FOR is NOT specified — character-1 may be the ≥2-occurrence symbol.
specCitations.quote: If the FOR phrase is not specified, the following rules apply: a) Character-string-1 shall contain: — at least on one of the symbols from the set 'A', 'N', 'X', 'Z', '1', '9', *, or — at least two occurrences of one of the symbols from the set character-1, 'x', '+', '-', and the currency symbol.

specCitations.what: At most two extended editing sign control symbols.
specCitations.quote: For fixed insertion with editing sign control, only one currency symbol and only one editing sign control symbol may be used in character-string-1. For extended editing sign control symbols, either one or two extended editing sign control symbols may be used in character-string-1.

specCitations.what: When two are specified, phrase ORDER binds to picture position.
specCitations.quote: When extended editing sign control symbols are used and two are specified, the first occurrence of the EDITING phrase shall be for the leftmost symbol in character-string-1 and the second occurrence shall be for the rightmost symbol in character-string-1.

specCitations.what: Currency-symbol placement under extended editing sign control.
specCitations.quote: For extended editing sign control, the currency symbol when used shall be either the leftmost symbol in character-string-1, optionally preceded by character-1, or the rightmost symbol in character-string-1 optionally followed by character-1.

specCitations.what: character-1 (IS form) is a category-defining insertion symbol for alphanumeric-edited, national-edited AND numeric-edited.
specCitations.quote: GR7: To define an item as alphanumeric-edited, character-string-1 shall include — at least one symbol 'A' or one symbol 'X', and — at least one instance of character-1 or one of the symbols from the set 'B', '0', '/'. … GR13a: … at least one symbol '9' and at least one instance of character-1 or at least one of the symbols from the set 'B', 'CR', 'DB', '0', '/', ',', '.', '+', '-', the currency symbol.

specCitations.what: THE master implementation rule: POSITIVE behaves as '+', NEGATIVE behaves as '-'. (Note the literal numbers are transposed in the printed text — the format diagram binds NEGATIVE↔literal-2, POSITIVE↔literal-3.)
specCitations.quote: In the following general rules, for a PICTURE clause with the FOR phrase all references to '+' apply to POSITIVE is literal-2, and all references to '-' apply to NEGATIVE IS literal-3 unless otherwise indicated.

specCitations.what: THE SIZE-COUNTING RULE — four distinct cases. This is the single most error-prone rule in the construct.
specCitations.quote: es  Character-1 in character-string-1 represents a character position into which the associated literal-1, literal-2, or literal-3 is to be placed. If character-1 is a simple insertion symbol or a fixed insertion symbol, the size of literal-1 is counted in the size of the item. For fixed editing sign control symbols, each character used in the symbol is counted in the size of the item. For extended editing sign control symbols with fixed insertion, each occurrence of the character(s) specified in the associated literal are counted in the size of the item. For floating inserting, one occurrence of literal-2 or literal-3 is counted in the size of the item plus one character for each repetition of character-1.

specCitations.what: Format validation of an EDITING position.
specCitations.quote: es  If the FOR clause is not specified, the character position (s) corresponding to character-1 shall be checked to contain literal-1. If the FOR clause is specified, the character positions following NEGATIVE shall be checked to contain literal-2 and the character positions following POSITIVE shall be checked to contain literal-3.

specCitations.what: IS form = SIMPLE insertion (unconditional, value-independent).
specCitations.quote: Simple insertion editing — Character-1 and the symbols 'B', '0', '/', ',' and, if literal=1 is specified, character-1 are used as the simple insertion editing symbols. Simple insertion editing results in the insertion character occupying the same character position in the edited item as the associated symbol occupies in character-string-1.

specCitations.what: FOR form = FIXED insertion, sign-selected.
specCitations.quote: Fixed insertion editing — Character-1, the currency symbol and the editing sign control symbols '+', '-', 'CR' and 'DB' are used as the fixed insertion editing symbols. … When character-1 is used, and is not a simple insertion character, it represents literal-2, or literal-3 as the insertion characters.

specCitations.what: Results of fixed insertion editing for the es rows. The two result COLUMNS are swapped in the extracted markdown relative to Table 9 and Annex D.24.
specCitations.quote: | **Editing symbol** | **Positive or zero value** | **Negative value** | … | character-1, NEGATIVE phrase | literal-2 | literal-2 or spaces | | character-1, POSITIVE phrase | literal-3 or spaces | literal-3 |  … Literal-2 or literal-3 or spaces means one instance of literal-2 or literal-3 or as many spaces as there are characters in literal-2 or literal-3.

specCitations.what: Floating insertion admits the extended editing sign control symbols; Table 9's es rows are correctly oriented and are the second witness against Table 8.
specCitations.quote: Floating insertion editing — The currency symbol, the extended editing sign control symbols, if specified, and the fixed editing sign control symbols '+' and '-' are used as the floating insertion symbols. Floating insertion editing is indicated by specifying a string of at least two identical floating insertion editing symbols. … | **Data item positive or zero** | **Data item negative** | … | character-1 NEGATIVE phrase | literal-2 or spaces | literal-2 | | character-1 POSITIVE phrase | literal-3 | literal-3 or spaces |

specCitations.what: Floating landing position — where the literal goes.
specCitations.quote: One way is to represent any or all of the leading numeric character positions to the left of the decimal point position by the same insertion symbol. The result is that a single occurrence of the replacement character(s) is (are) placed into the character position(s) immediately preceding whichever of the following is encountered first: — the first nonzero numeric character in the item — the first character position for which no floating insertion editing is specified — the decimal point position. Any character positions preceding this (these) insertion character(s) will contain the space character.

specCitations.what: Digit CAPACITY of a floating zone = (occurrences − 1).
specCitations.quote: The leftmost symbol of the insertion string represents the leftmost limit of the floating characters in the data item. … The second floating symbol represents the leftmost limit of the numeric data that may be stored in the item. During editing, nonzero numeric characters may replace all the insertion symbols at or to the right of this limit.

specCitations.what: The precedence-table slot for 'es'.
specCitations.quote: If the EDITING phrase is specified, the precedence of 'es' as related to Table 10, Format 1 picture symbol order of precedence, has the same precedence as the 'cs' symbol in the column and row of non-floating insertion symbols.

specCitations.what: Three worked examples with exact expected bytes, plus the floating SIZE trap. Examples 2, 3 and the size note verify exactly against the derived algorithm; example 1 does NOT (see risks).
specCitations.quote: 01 item PIC IS LLLL9.99F  EDITING "L" FOR NEGATIVE IS "("  EDITING "F" FOR NEGATIVE IS ")"  BLANK WHEN ZERO. — The statement 'MOVE -123.45 TO item' would result in 'b(123.45)' … 01 item PIC IS L999.99  EDITING "L" FOR NEGATIVE IS "DEBIT "  BLANK WHEN ZERO. — 'MOVE -123.45 TO item' would result in 'DEBIT 123.45' … 'MOVE 123.45 TO item' would result in 'bbbbbb123.45' not '123.45' … 'PIC LLLL9,88 EDITING "L" FOR NEGATIVE IS "DEBIT "' would result in an item size of 13 characters: 6 for the first 'L', 3 for the next three, and 4 for the numbers.

specCitations.what: De-editing — when it happens and what an unrepresentable image does.
specCitations.quote: 5) De-editing takes place only when the sending operand is a numeric-edited data item and the receiving item is a numeric or a numeric-edited data item. … If the category of the sending operand is numeric-edited, the content of the sending operand shall be as specified in 14.6.13.2, Incompatible data, and de-editing establishes the operand's numeric value, which may be signed.

specCitations.what: An image that no editing operation could have produced ⇒ EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE + undefined result. This is the de-edit failure contract for EDITING.
specCitations.quote: When a numeric-edited data item is the sending operand of a de-editing MOVE statement and the content of that data item is not a possible result for any editing operation in that data item, the result of the MOVE operation is undefined and an EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE exception condition is set to exist.

specCitations.what: Definition of de-editing.
specCitations.quote: de-editing — logical removal of all editing characters from a numeric-edited data item in order to determine that item's numeric value

currentState.summary: ABSENT END-TO-END in the greenfield compiler. (1) Does NOT lex: there is no EDITING token in any Grammar/Core/*.g4 — `grep -n EDITING src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/*.g4` returns nothing. (2) Does NOT parse: `pictureClause : PIC PIC_STRING ;` has no tail, and `dataDescriptionClause` has no editing alternative. A 2023 program using EDITING is a raw ANTLR syntax error today at EVERY --std, not a clean COBOLNET0900. (3) Does NOT bind: PictureAnalyzer's §13.18.40.3 SR2 whitelist has no 'es' concept, so character-1 (e.g. 'L') falls to the `default:` arm and is rejected COBOLNET0808 'invalid PICTURE symbol'. (4) Does NOT emit/format: CobolEdit has no es handling anywhere. (5) The ONLY thing that already exists is the reserved-word metadata: ReservedWords.Table.cs and tests/version-matrix/reserved-words.json both carry EDITING as r2023-only — so NO reserved-words.json/Table change is needed, only a constructs.json interval row. ARCHITECTURAL BLOCKER (the reason this is the batch's largest item): the entire edited-picture pipeline assumes ONE MASK CHARACTER == ONE OUTPUT CHARACTER POSITION. CobolEdit.Format allocates `new char[pattern.Length]` and indexes output by mask index; MaskCapacity/MaskScale/DeEdit/FormatAlphanumeric all share that invariant; PicInfo.Length is computed as a symbol COUNT; and the emitters pass the mask as a bare C# string literal plus a program-level `EditCfgArgs` suffix. EDITING breaks the 1:1 invariant (character-1 expands to a literal of up to 50 characters) and is a PER-ITEM (not per-program) datum, so it cannot ride EditCfgArgs. NOTE (related, pre-existing, NOT in scope): the currency symbol has the identical GR14 multi-character 'currency string' rule but is modelled as a single `char currency` throughout — multi-character CURRENCY SIGN strings are already unsupported; the expansion pass designed below is the mechanism that would later fix that too. LEGACY: `src/CobolSharp.Compiler` has no EDITING implementation either (grep across the greenfield tree found only the CorrespondingBinder DE-EDITING comment and the ReservedWords row) — there is NO proven legacy algorithm to port for this construct; the existing CobolEdit two-pass fill/suppress algorithm (itself the ported legacy one) IS the base to extend.

semanticChanges.change:
Add `string? editing = null` as a trailing optional parameter to EVERY public entry point — Format, TryFormat, DeEdit, MaskCapacity, MaskScale, FormatAlphanumeric — and to the private FractionDigits and FindFloatingPlacement. Default null == today's behavior byte-for-byte (the whole existing corpus is unaffected). CORE ALGORITHM (the two-pass fill/suppress engine is KEPT and operates unchanged on MASK SLOTS — one slot per mask character, including one slot per character-1 occurrence; a new THIRD pass expands slots to the final image):

  (0) PRE-SCAN. `var es = EditingSymbols.Get(editing);` For each es symbol s, count its occurrences in `pattern`: n(s). s FLOATS iff s.SignSensitive && n(s) >= 2 (editing rule 6 — only the extended editing sign control symbols float; the IS form is simple insertion and never floats, editing rule 3). s is FIXED iff !floats. Mirror this EXACTLY on the cs/'+'/'-' pre-scan already at CobolEdit.cs:60-84.

  (1) DIGIT CAPACITY (`trueDigitCount`, CobolEdit.cs:74-82). Add: a FLOATING es slot counts as a digit position; a FIXED es slot does NOT. `hasFloating` must also become true when any es floats, so the existing `effectiveDigitCount = trueDigitCount - 1` reservation applies to the es zone (§13.18.40.5 rule 6: "The second floating symbol represents the leftmost limit of the numeric data"). CAUTION: the existing `hasFloating ? trueDigitCount - 1 : trueDigitCount` subtracts exactly ONE across the whole mask; SR24 permits at most TWO extended symbols but SR25 forces the second to be the RIGHTMOST symbol (a trailing fixed sign position, e.g. D.24 ex1/ex2's 'F'), and §13.18.40.3 SR27 forbids two distinct floating strings — so at most ONE zone ever floats and the single subtraction stays correct. Assert it.

  (2) FractionDigits (CobolEdit.cs:329-359). In the right-of-point loop add: a FLOATING es character counts as a fraction digit position; a FIXED es character does not. Also add es characters to the P-scaling `LastIndexOfAny(['9','Z','*'])` digit-position probes ONLY for floating es (a fixed es is an insertion position, like ','). Under SR12b a FOR-form picture admits P and V, so this path is reachable.

  (3) PASS 1 (right-to-left fill, CobolEdit.cs:99-144). Add a case ahead of the existing switch: if the mask char is an es symbol, then if it FLOATS, `output[i] = digitIdx >= 0 ? digits[digitIdx--] : '0';` (identical to the floating cs arm at :104); else `output[i] = ES_MARKER;` where ES_MARKER is a private const char '�' that can never occur in a picture or an image. Record the slot index in an `int[] esSlot` side table so pass 3 knows which symbol each marker belongs to (a marker alone does not identify which character-1 it was, once two es symbols exist).

  (4) PASS 2 (left-to-right suppression, CobolEdit.cs:151-186). Add a case: a FLOATING es slot suppresses exactly like the floating cs/'+'/'-' arms — `if (output[i] == '0') output[i] = ' '; else { suppressing = false; allIntegerSuppressed = false; }`. A FIXED es slot holds a marker: it is neither a digit nor a suppression symbol — `break` out of the switch WITHOUT clearing `suppressing` (it behaves like the leading currency/sign position, which the existing loop also falls through on). Do NOT let a fixed es slot set allIntegerSuppressed=false.

  (5) FULL-FIELD BLANK (CobolEdit.cs:191-199). The `!pattern.Contains('9')` guard must also treat a floating es zone as suppressible (it already is, since es slots are not '9'). When the field blanks, a FIXED es slot must still receive its marker (its literal is a fixed insertion and per Table 8 is emitted per the SIGN even in an all-suppressed field) — EXCEPT under BLANK WHEN ZERO, which short-circuits earlier. Set the whole-field-blank output to ' ' for every slot including es markers ONLY when asteriskFill is false and there is no fixed es; when a fixed es is present keep its marker so pass 3 emits the sign-selected literal. FLAG: this precise corner (zero value, all-suppressible mask, a FIXED es present, no BLANK WHEN ZERO) has NO worked example in D.24 — see openQuestions.

  (6) FLOATING PLACEMENT (CobolEdit.cs:203-217, FindFloatingPlacement). Add a third placement branch for a floating es: `int pos = FindFloatingPlacement(pattern, output, s.Symbol); if (pos >= 0) output[pos] = ES_MARKER;` and record esSlot[pos] = index of s. FindFloatingPlacement needs no change (it is already parameterized on the float char).

  (7) PASS 3 — NEW: EXPANSION. Build the final image with a StringBuilder over the slots: a slot holding ES_MARKER emits `negative ? sym.NegText : sym.PosText` (width w); every other slot emits its single character. THIS IS THE ONLY PLACE THE 1:1 INVARIANT IS BROKEN, and it is broken exactly once, at the very end. `negative` is the already-computed `value < 0` (CobolEdit.cs:48). Per Table 9 / D.24 (see risks: Table 8's columns are transposed): NEGATIVE-phrase-only => NegText = literal-2, PosText = spaces(len); POSITIVE-phrase-only => PosText = literal-3, NegText = spaces(len); both => PosText = literal-3, NegText = literal-2. The binder has already normalized this into the spec string, so the runtime does a pure lookup — one place, one rule.

  (8) BLANK WHEN ZERO (CobolEdit.cs:54). `return new string(' ', pattern.Length)` becomes `return new string(' ', ExpandedWidth(pattern, es, currencyChar))` where ExpandedWidth = Σ over slots of (es marker ? w : 1). This MUST equal PicInfo.Length — add a runtime Debug.Assert and a unit test asserting `Format(...).Length == PicInfo.Length` over the whole matrix.

  (9) MaskCapacity (:281-307). Same digit-position amendment as (1); the returned Capacity is a DIGIT count, unaffected by literal widths.

  (10) FormatAlphanumeric (:364-381). Under the IS form an es symbol makes the item ALPHANUMERIC-EDITED (GR7) or NATIONAL-EDITED (GR10). Add: an es slot emits sym.PosText (== NegText for the IS form — an alphanumeric-edited item has no sign, editing rule 3 is unconditional). Output length becomes the expanded width, so this method must also build via StringBuilder rather than `new char[picture.Length]`.

  (11) DeEdit (:228-260) — REWRITE, do not patch. The mask-index==image-index walk is invalid once a literal is wider than one character. New algorithm, driven left-to-right by a cursor over the image:
      pos = 0; value = 0; negative = false;
      for each mask slot i:
        - FIXED es s: compare image[pos..pos+w] against s.NegText then s.PosText. If it matches NegText and NegText != PosText, negative = true. If it matches neither, set the EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE flag (§14.6.13.2 / §14.9.25.4 — an image that is not a possible editing result). pos += w.
        - FLOATING es zone (a maximal run of s in the mask, n occurrences, width W = w + n - 1): take image[pos..pos+W]; skip leading spaces; if the next w characters match NegText -> negative = true (when distinct from PosText), else if they match PosText -> positive, else EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE; the REMAINING characters of the zone are the low-order digits, and the zone contributes exactly (n-1) digits with the un-consumed leading positions contributing 0. pos += W. NOTE this literal-matching approach is REQUIRED, not merely tidier: a naive 'rightmost n-1 characters are the digits' shortcut silently corrupts values whenever the literal ENDS in a digit (e.g. literal "A1": mask LLL, value 5 renders 'bA15' and the shortcut yields 15 instead of 05).
        - every existing symbol class: unchanged behavior, pos += 1.
      Keep the existing `if (image.Contains('-')) negative = true;` heuristic ONLY for the built-in floating minus; it must NOT be applied when an es literal legitimately contains '-'.
  Returns the unscaled value at MaskScale(picture, …, editing).

At the entry-clause collection loop that currently feeds line 1877-1879: harvest `pictureClause.editingClause()` into a `List<EditingSymbol>` in SOURCE (phrase) order, then pass it to Analyze. Per editingClause ctx:
  - character-1 = the FIRST `literal`. It shall be a one-character alphanumeric (or national, SR9) literal -> COBOLNET1581 if it is numeric, figurative, or not exactly 1 character.
  - Neither IS nor FOR present -> COBOLNET1586 (no defined general rule; reject loud, never a silent misbind).
  - `IS? literal` present -> EditingSymbol(c, PosText: lit1, NegText: lit1, SignSensitive: false). SR9: len(lit1) <= 50 -> COBOLNET1581.
  - `FOR editingSignPhrase+` -> collect NEGATIVE-> lit2 and POSITIVE-> lit3. Duplicate NEGATIVE or duplicate POSITIVE -> COBOLNET1587. SR12a: when both present, lit2.Length != lit3.Length -> COBOLNET1582. SR12c: the absent one defaults to `new string(' ', other.Length)`. Then EditingSymbol(c, PosText: lit3 ?? spaces, NegText: lit2 ?? spaces, SignSensitive: true). SR9: each <= 50 -> COBOLNET1581.
  - SR11 across phrases: duplicate character-1 -> COBOLNET1580.
On ANY of these errors, DROP that symbol from the list (so PictureAnalyzer's SR2 whitelist then reports the unmapped character honestly rather than cascading) — the compile has already failed; recovery only keeps the doomed emit crash-free, matching the file's established recovery posture.

The two Report-Writer Analyze funnels at :487 and :625 must thread the same harvested list (the RW SOURCE/SUM picture is a real pictureClause and may legally carry EDITING). If a wave decides RW EDITING is out of scope, it must still be REJECTED LOUD there rather than silently dropped — a dropped map would produce a wrong-width report line. Prefer threading; it is the same helper call.

Thread the new argument through the fragment builders and BOTH compile-time passthroughs: `EditFormat(value, scale, maskLiteral, cfgArgs)` and `EditTryFormat(...)` already take a free-form `cfgArgs` suffix — callers append `ctx.EditArgs(pic)` to it, so those two signatures need NO change (document it). `EditFormatAlphanumeric(value, maskLiteral)` gains an `editingArgs` parameter. `MaskScale(picture, currency, commaMode)` (line 620) and `EditCompose(value, valueScale, picture, blankWhenZero, currency, commaMode)` (line 627) each gain a trailing `string? editing` and forward it — these are the COMPILE-TIME folds (edited-receiver working scale; a numeric literal VALUE baked as a constant edited image per §13.18.63 GR6) and they are WRONG without the map.

Today a program using EDITING is a raw ANTLR syntax error at every --std, so the grammar and the gate MUST land in the same change set or the pre-2023 behaviour is a parse error rather than an honest edition diagnostic. tests.covers: Annex D.24 example 3 VERBATIM — the FOR/NEGATIVE fixed extended editing sign control symbol, the SR12c spaces default for the unspecified POSITIVE case, and the GR14 'es' fixed size rule. This is the primary oracle: the spec states both expected results as literal bytes.
tests.sketch:
01 ITM PIC L999.99 EDITING "L" FOR NEGATIVE IS "DEBIT " BLANK WHEN ZERO.
MOVE -123.45 TO ITM. DISPLAY ITM.
MOVE  123.45 TO ITM. DISPLAY ITM.
EXPECTED (item size = 12 = len("DEBIT ")=6 + "999.99"=6, per GR14 'es'):
  line 1: `DEBIT 123.45`
  line 2: `      123.45`   (six leading spaces — D.24: "would result in 'bbbbbb123.45' not '123.45'")
Derivation: negative -> NegText = literal-2 = "DEBIT " (Table 9 orientation, confirmed by D.24); positive -> PosText = spaces(6) (SR12c). BLANK WHEN ZERO is present but never fires.

tests.covers: Annex D.24 example 2 VERBATIM — FLOATING extended editing (character-1 repeated, editing rule 6 + Table 9), TWO EDITING phrases (SR24 two extended symbols, SR25 leftmost/rightmost ordering), the GR14 floating size rule, and the floating landing position (rule 6a).
tests.sketch:
01 ITM PIC LLLL9.99F
       EDITING "L" FOR NEGATIVE IS "("
       EDITING "F" FOR NEGATIVE IS ")"
       BLANK WHEN ZERO.
MOVE -123.45 TO ITM. DISPLAY ITM.
EXPECTED: ` (123.45)`  (9 bytes: space, '(', '1','2','3','.','4','5',')')
Derivation, fully traced against the designed algorithm: size = L-zone (w=1 + (4-1) reps = 4) + "9.99" (4) + F fixed (1) = 9. Digit capacity = 3 (L zone, n-1) + 1 ('9') + 2 (fraction) = 6. scaled=-12345 -> digits "012345". Pass 1 fills L slots 3..0 with '2','1','0','0' and the '9' with '3'. Pass 2 suppresses slot0 and slot1 to spaces, stops at slot2='1'. Floating placement puts the L marker at slot1 (rightmost suppressed in the zone). Pass 3 expands: slot0=' ', slot1="(" , then "123.45", then the F marker -> ")". Also add a positive MOVE (+123.45) asserting `  123.45 ` — both markers expand to spaces(1) per SR12c.

risks: ⚠ SPEC DEFECT #1 — Table 8's 'es' rows are COLUMN-TRANSPOSED in specs/ISO_COBOL.md:20805-20806. It reads `character-1, NEGATIVE phrase | literal-2 | literal-2 or spaces` under headers `Positive or zero value | Negative value`, i.e. literal-2 on POSITIVE. THREE independent witnesses say otherwise: (a) Table 9 (:20857) carries the same two rows correctly oriented (`literal-2 or spaces | literal-2`); (b) Annex D.24 example 3 states in prose that MOVE -123.45 yields 'DEBIT 123.45' and MOVE 123.45 yields 'bbbbbb123.45'; (c) GR12 (:20501) makes NEGATIVE behave as '-' and POSITIVE as '+', and Table 8's own '+'/'-' rows are correctly oriented. IMPLEMENT THE TABLE 9 / D.24 ORIENTATION: NegText fires when value < 0. The scout doc flagged this from D.24 alone; the Table 9 cross-check is the confirming second witness. Anyone re-deriving from Table 8 alone will invert the whole feature.

⚠ SPEC DEFECT #2 (NOT in the scout doc — new finding) — Annex D.24 EXAMPLE 1 IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE AND MUST NOT BE GOLDENED AS WRITTEN. It gives `PIC IS L9999.99F` with `MOVE -123.45` yielding '(b123.45)'. That requires the second character position to be a SPACE, but a '9' symbol never suppresses (GR14: "Each symbol '9' represents a decimal digit position") — the correct result for that picture is '(0123.45)'. The narrative that follows ('If you do not want spaces following the leading symbol, you would use floating symbols') depends on the space, so the picture was almost certainly meant to be zero-suppressing (`LZZZ9.99F`, which does yield '(b123.45)'). Examples 2 and 3 and the size note all verify EXACTLY against the algorithm designed here; example 1 does not. Golden examples 2 and 3; add a unit test asserting '(0123.45)' for the picture as literally printed, with a comment recording this finding.

⚠ SPEC DEFECT #3 — SR12c (:20300) has its literal numbers swapped: 'If only POSITIVE is specified, the default ... is the space character repeated for the number of characters in literal-2' — but literal-2 is the NEGATIVE literal and does not exist in that branch. Intent (and the only self-consistent reading given SR12a's equal-length requirement): the ABSENT phrase defaults to spaces of the SPECIFIED literal's length. GR12 (:20501) has the same transposition ('all references to + apply to POSITIVE is literal-2'). Both are harmless once recognized, but a literal transcription produces nonsense.

⚠ THE 1:1 MASK INVARIANT IS THE CENTRAL ARCHITECTURAL HAZARD. `new char[pattern.Length]` (CobolEdit.cs:97), `new string(' ', pattern.Length)` (:54), and the mask-index==image-index DeEdit walk (:245) all encode it, and PicInfo.Length is a symbol COUNT (PictureAnalyzer.cs:249). The design confines the break to ONE new expansion pass at the very end, but any missed site produces a SILENTLY WRONG-WIDTH image, not a compile error. Mandatory audit: `grep -rn "EditMask\|pattern.Length\|picture.Length" src/Cobol.Net.Compiler src/Cobol.Net.Runtime --include=*.cs | grep -v obj` and justify every hit.

DFA/AMBIGUITY: adding the EDITING lexer token plus `| EDITING` to cobolWord means the token can appear both as the editingClause head and in a user-word slot. The dangerous shape is a data entry NAMED EDITING immediately following a PICTURE clause: `05 A PIC 9. 05 EDITING PIC 9.` — ANTLR must not let `editingClause*` consume the following entry's name. It should not: editingClause requires a `literal` after EDITING and the next token is the level-number INTEGER (entries are level-number-led), so prediction fails the alternative immediately. VERIFY EXPLICITLY with a test at --std 85 in both the level-numbered and the (illegal but parseable) unnumbered arrangement before trusting it.

SHARED-RULE OVER-FIRE (DEVLOG 736): pictureClause is referenced from CobolData.g4:238, CobolReportWriter.g4:90 and CobolScreen.g4:51. The added tail is purely optional so it cannot over-fire structurally, and the 0900 gate is correct in all three sections — but the FULL legacy guard is still mandatory because the change touches the rule every NIST CCVS data, report and screen entry parses through.

DO NOT wrap VisitEditingClause in `InGatedDataEntry` by pattern-matching the neighbouring BASED/ANY LENGTH/DYNAMIC LENGTH gates. That guard restricts firing to non-66/88 dataDescriptionEntry contexts and would SILENTLY SUPPRESS the 0900 for report-group and screen pictures, where EDITING is equally a 2023 construct.

RESERVED-WORD DOUBLE-COUNT: reserved-words.json:1147 and ReservedWords.Table.cs:140 ALREADY carry EDITING with r2023=true. Do NOT add a row — the drift guards will fail on a duplicate. Only the constructs.json interval row (user-word-editing-2023) and the CheckedTokenTypes entry are new.

PicInfo VALUE EQUALITY: PicInfo is a `sealed record`. Carrying the map as an array/list member would silently degrade equality to reference identity. The design uses an encoded STRING (EditingSpec) specifically to avoid this. If an implementer 'improves' it to a collection, any code comparing PicInfo instances breaks in a way no test currently covers.

DIGIT-CAPACITY SUBTRACTION: CobolEdit's `hasFloating ? trueDigitCount - 1 : trueDigitCount` subtracts exactly ONE across the entire mask. That remains correct only because SR27 forbids two floating strings and SR25 forces a second extended symbol to be the trailing (fixed) one. Add an assertion — if a future relaxation admits two floating zones, the capacity silently over-counts by one and every value truncates wrongly.

EXISTING RELATED GAP (do not fix here, but do not let it confuse the implementer): GR14's currency-symbol rule is IDENTICAL in shape to the 'es' rule ('The first occurrence of the currency symbol adds the number of characters in the currency string to the size of the item'), yet the compiler models currency as a single `char` throughout. Multi-character CURRENCY SIGN strings are already unsupported. The expansion pass designed here is the mechanism that would later close that gap; resist the temptation to close it in the same change set.

EFFORT: this is an L. Grammar (3 files) + reserved-word funnel + PicInfo + PictureAnalyzer (7 distinct rule checks + the size rewrite) + DataBinder (2-3 funnels) + a new runtime type + a substantive CobolEdit rewrite (new pass 3, rewritten DeEdit, 6 signature changes) + 8 emitter sites + 10 diagnostics + 2 registry rows + 5 goldens + 12 negative fixtures + 2 unit suites. Do NOT attempt it in one commit; the natural seam is (1) grammar + gate + reserved word + reject-everything-at-bind, (2) IS-form simple insertion end-to-end, (3) FOR-form fixed, (4) FOR-form floating + de-editing.
openQuestions: THE BARE FORM. `EDITING character-1` with neither IS nor FOR is admitted by the Format 1 diagram (the inner group is bracketed) but NO syntax rule or general rule assigns it a meaning — SR12 covers only 'if literal-1 is specified' and 'if the FOR phrase is specified', and GR14 'es' describes only literal-1/2/3 placement. I propose REJECTING it (COBOLNET1586) on the project's never-silently-misbind doctrine. The alternatives I considered and rejected for lack of any basis: defaulting literal-1 to character-1 itself, or to a single space. This is a genuine spec gap, not a transcription defect — worth an owner note if the P14 traceability inventory wants a documented interpretation.

SR12a SCOPE — PER-PHRASE OR CROSS-PHRASE? I read 'Literal-2 and literal-3 shall occupy the same number of character positions' as scoped to ONE EDITING phrase (it sits under 'If the FOR phrase is specified ... the following rules apply'). But SR24 permits two extended phrases, and an alternative reading requires ALL extended literals in the clause to share a width. D.24 example 2 is consistent with both ('(' and ')' are each 1 character). I implement the per-phrase reading and do NOT cross-check widths between phrases. A cross-phrase check would additionally reject `EDITING "L" FOR NEGATIVE IS "((" EDITING "F" FOR NEGATIVE IS ")"`, which nothing in the spec clearly forbids.

CAN ONE EDITING PHRASE CARRY BOTH NEGATIVE AND POSITIVE? The Format 1 diagram draws them as a stacked exclusive choice, which literally read means no. But SR12a (equal lengths) and SR12c ('If only POSITIVE is specified ... If only NEGATIVE is specified') are meaningless unless both may appear together. I resolve toward YES (grammar `FOR editingSignPhrase+`) as the only self-consistent reading, matching the scout's conclusion. If the owner reads the diagram strictly, change the grammar to `FOR editingSignPhrase` and delete COBOLNET1587.

THE IS FORM WITH >=2 OCCURRENCES. Editing rule 6 lists only 'the extended editing sign control symbols' as floating, so I treat repeated IS-form character-1 as N INDEPENDENT simple insertions (size N x len(literal-1)). But SR12's non-FOR branch (a) offers 'at least two occurrences of one of the symbols from the set character-1, x, +, -, and the currency symbol' as a way to make the picture VALID — grouping character-1 with the genuinely floating symbols. If that sentence is meant to imply the IS form can float, the size rule and rendering change completely. I am confident in the non-floating reading (editing rules 3 and 6 are explicit and disjoint), but the SR12 wording is a real counter-signal. No worked example in D.24 covers it.

ZERO VALUE, ALL-SUPPRESSIBLE MASK, FIXED es PRESENT, NO BLANK WHEN ZERO. Editing rule 7b says an all-Z mask over a zero value blanks the entire item. Does a FIXED es position (a fixed insertion, like a leading currency symbol) still emit its sign-selected literal in that blanked field? By analogy with the currency symbol — which the current implementation also blanks in the full-field case (CobolEdit.cs:194-198) — I keep the es marker and emit PosText. But the analogy is not airtight and D.24 has no example. Low-frequency corner; worth a decision note.

EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE ON DE-EDIT. §14.6.13.2 (:24904) requires that a numeric-edited sender whose content 'is not a possible result for any editing operation in that data item' set EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE with an undefined result. The rewritten literal-matching DeEdit is the FIRST place in this codebase that can actually DETECT that condition (the current index-walk silently contributes zero for any non-digit). Is raising the EC in scope for this construct, or does it belong to a separate EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE work item covering all numeric-edited senders? I have specified detecting it and flagging it, but not the raise plumbing — that decision affects whether this construct also touches the EC infrastructure.

NATIONAL EDITING (SR9). A national subject requires national literals, and the resulting item is national-edited — which PictureAnalyzer already stages not-implemented (COBOLNET0899, Constructs.NationalEdited2002, PictureAnalyzer.cs:133). So national EDITING inherits an honest rejection for free. Confirm that inheriting the 0899 is the wanted posture rather than a dedicated national-EDITING staging row.

FORMAT VALIDATION (GR15 'es'). The VALIDATE statement is required to check that an es position contains literal-1 (or literal-2/literal-3 per the sign). I have NOT specified this — it depends on the state of the VALIDATE format-validation implementation, which I did not survey. If VALIDATE format checking is live, GR15 'es' is an additional required branch; if it is staged, this construct inherits that staging. The implementer should check before declaring the construct complete against the P14 traceability inventory.

HIGH on the editing/size algorithm: I traced it against all four Annex D.24 data points and it reproduces examples 2 and 3 byte-for-byte plus the stated size-13 result exactly; the one failure (example 1) I can explain as a spec transcription error with a specific reconstruction of the intended picture (LZZZ9.99F), which is itself strong evidence the model is right. HIGH on the diagnostic inventory — each of the ten maps to one quoted syntax rule. MEDIUM on three design decisions that rest on ambiguous or defective spec text and are called out in openQuestions: the bare EDITING form (no governing rule exists), whether one phrase may carry both NEGATIVE and POSITIVE (diagram says no, SR12a/SR12c say yes), and whether the IS form can float (editing rules 3/6 say no, SR12's non-FOR branch hints yes). I did NOT survey the VALIDATE format-validation implementation, so the GR15 'es' branch is unscoped.
