specs.title: PERFORM Format 3 (exception-checking PERFORM) + the UNTIL EXIT phrase

spec.construct: C5-perform-format3 — PERFORM Format 3 (exception-checking PERFORM) + the UNTIL EXIT phrase (ISO §14.9.28)

specCitations.what: The complete Format-3 syntax skeleton
specCitations.quote: `PERFORM` [ `WITH LOCATION` ] `imperative-statement-1` … `WHEN` followed by a choice between two options: `EXCEPTION` followed by an optional bracket containing one of these options stacked vertically: `{ file-name-1 } ...`, `INPUT`, `OUTPUT`, `IO`, `EXTEND` — `{ exception-name-1 ...` or `{ exception-name-2 FILE file-name-2 } ...` … followed by `imperative-statement-2` with `...` indicating repetition of the entire WHEN clause. [ `WHEN OTHER EXCEPTION` imperative-statement-3 ] [ `WHEN COMMON EXCEPTION` imperative-statement-4 ] [ `FINALLY` imperative-statement-5 ] `END-PERFORM`

specCitations.what: The UNTIL EXIT alternative on Formats 1/2
specCitations.quote: A square bracket (optional) containing: WITH TEST followed by a curly brace (required choice) containing: BEFORE / AFTER — Followed by: UNTIL then a curly brace (required choice) containing: condition-1 / EXIT

specCitations.what: UNTIL EXIT placement restriction
specCitations.quote: The UNTIL EXIT phrase shall not be specified in a PERFORM statement with or under a PERFORM statement with the VARYING phrase or either the TEST BEFORE or TEST AFTER phrase

specCitations.what: Format-3 file-name uniqueness
specCitations.quote: If file-name-1 or file-name-2 is specified in a WHEN phrase, it shall not be specified more than once in any of the WHEN phrases within the scope of a format 3 PERFORM statement unless all such instances are specified in conjunction with an exception-name.

specCitations.what: Format-3 exception-name uniqueness
specCitations.quote: All instances of an exception-name shall be specified only once in a format 3 PERFORM statement unless done so in conjunction with different file-names.

specCitations.what: FILE phrase restricts the exception-name family
specCitations.quote: If file-name-2 is specified, exception-name-2 shall begin with the COBOL characters 'EC-I-O'.

specCitations.what: UNTIL EXIT semantics
specCitations.quote: If the until-phrase with the EXIT reserved word is specified, execution proceeds exactly as if the same PERFORM statement were coded but with condition-1 specified except that condition-1 never evaluates as true.

specCitations.what: UNTIL EXIT escape asymmetry
specCitations.quote: For an inline PERFORM, this can be done by an EXIT PERFORM (but not EXIT PERFORM CYCLE) statement. For an out-of-line PERFORM this can be done by a GOBACK or STOP statement. … an EXIT PARAGRAPH (from a performed paragraph) or an EXIT SECTION (from a performed section) do not escape a PERFORM with the UNTIL EXIT phrase.

specCitations.what: The implicit TURN / PUSH ALL / TURN OFF ALL / POP ALL scope of Format 3
specCitations.quote: If checking for exception-name-1 or exception-name-2 is not enabled for imperative-statement-1 by a TURN directive, an implicit TURN directive for exception-name-1 or exception-name-2 is assumed before the first statement in imperative-statement-1. If LOCATION is specified, that implicit TURN directive contains LOCATION. If the WHEN OTHER phrase is used, only those exception conditions that are enabled at the point at which they are detected are processed by the WHEN OTHER phrase. Within imperative-statement-1 any TURN directive that turns off checking for an exception that is specified in a WHEN phrase will prevent that WHEN phrase from being invoked if that exception condition would otherwise have been set to exist. An implicit PUSH ALL followed by TURN OFF ALL is assumed at the end of imperative-statement-1. Immediately preceding the END PERFORM phrase, there is an implicit POP ALL followed by an implicit TURN directive with OFF specified for any exception conditions that were implicitly turned on before the first statement in imperative-statement-1.

specCitations.what: The Format-3 range
specCitations.quote: When the PERFORM statement is executed, control is transferred to imperative-statement-1. The specified set of statements for a format 3 PERFORM statement consists of all statements contained within imperative-statement-1. However, other statements may be executed depending on whether or not an exception was raised.

specCitations.what: FINALLY is the end of the PERFORM; no transfer out; EXIT PERFORM in FINALLY
specCitations.quote: If the FINALLY phrase is specified, the end of the PERFORM statement begins at imperative-statement-5. There shall be no statements that include a transfer of control out of the PERFORM statement within imperative-statement-5. Any EXIT PERFORM statement within imperative-statement-5 transfers control to an implicit CONTINUE statement following the END-PERFORM. If the FINALLY phrase is not specified, the end of the PERFORM statement is indicated by END-PERFORM.

specCitations.what: WHEN arm selection + USE shadowing
specCitations.quote: If during the execution of imperative-statement-1 an exception condition associated with a WHEN phrase is raised, imperative-statement-2 is executed. The rules for determining a match are specified in General rules 3a to 3g of the USE statement. At the completion of the execution of imperative-statement-2, control is passed as indicated in General rule 20 or, if WHEN COMMON is specified, to imperative-statement-4. Any USE declarative that would normally match the exception condition is ignored.

specCitations.what: WHEN OTHER EXCEPTION
specCitations.quote: If during the execution of imperative-statement-1 any exception condition that is not associated with any exception condition specified in a WHEN phrase is raised and there is a WHEN OTHER phrase, imperative-statement-3 is executed. At the completion of the execution of imperative-statement-3, control is passed to the end of the PERFORM statement or, if WHEN COMMON is specified, to imperative-statement-4. … Any USE declarative that would normally match the exception condition is ignored.

specCitations.what: WHEN COMMON
specCitations.quote: If WHEN COMMON is specified, imperative-statement-4 is executed. At the completion of the execution of imperative-statement-4, control is passed as indicated in General rule 20.

specCitations.what: Resumption after a handled exception (the nonfatal/fatal split)
specCitations.quote: If execution of the last statement in imperative-statement-1 completes successfully, execution proceeds to the end of the PERFORM statement. … If the exception condition was nonfatal, execution continues with an implicit CONTINUE statement immediately following the statement in imperative-statement-1 in which the exception condition occurred. If that statement was the last statement in imperative-statement-1, execution continues at the end of the PERFORM statement. If the exception condition was fatal, execution continues as specified in 14.6.13.1.3, Fatal exception conditions.

specCitations.what: FINALLY belongs to the end of the PERFORM
specCitations.quote: The end of the PERFORM statement includes the statements in a FINALLY phrase, if it is specified.

specCitations.what: Handlers are not re-caught
specCitations.quote: Any exception conditions raised during the execution of imperative-statement-2, imperative-statement-3, imperative-statement-4, or imperative-statement-5 will not cause transfer of control to any of these imperative-statements. The results are as if these statements were specified in a format 2 PERFORM statement.

specCitations.what: Checking state after the PERFORM
specCitations.quote: At the completion of the execution of the PERFORM statement, If WHEN is specified and an exception condition was raised and checking for that exception condition was enabled by a TURN directive before the execution of the PERFORM statement, that checking remains enabled. If there is a TURN directive within the range of the PERFORM statement, the checking for that TURN directive is retained. Otherwise, any checking for an exception condition specified in a WHEN phrase is not enabled.

specCitations.what: The FATAL path through a Format-3 PERFORM — WHEN, then COMMON, then abnormal termination
specCitations.quote: If the executed statement is within imperative-statement-1 of a PERFORM statement that contains a WHEN phrase that specifies the exception-name associated with the exception condition or an exception-name of a higher level in the same hierarchy, the imperative statement in the WHEN phrase is executed. If WHEN COMMON is specified, the imperative-statement within the COMMON phrase is executed. Execution of the last imperative statement is terminated abnormally as specified in 14.6.12, Abnormal run unit termination.

specCitations.what: The NONFATAL path — WHEN preempts USE entirely
specCitations.quote: If the executed statement is within imperative-statement-1 of a PERFORM statement that contains a WHEN phrase that specifies the exception-name associated with the exception condition or an exception-name of a higher level in the same hierarchy, the imperative statement in the WHEN phrase is executed. Execution of the imperative statement in the WHEN phrase completes as specified in the rules for the PERFORM statement. No associated USE EXCEPTION declarative is executed. If a conditional phrase with a NOT phrase is specified in the interrupted statement, the imperative-statement in that phrase is also not executed.

specCitations.what: The tiered match order GR17 delegates to (a=F1 file, b=F1 mode, c=F3 file+level-3, d=F3 file+level-2, e=F3 level-3, f=F3 level-2, g=F3 level-1)
specCitations.quote: A declarative is selected for execution by analyzing the USE statements in the source element in the order in which they are specified. The first declarative that satisfies the selection criteria is executed and no other declaratives are executed. … a) All format 1 USE statements in which file-name-1 is specified … b) All format 1 USE statements in which file-name-1 is not specified … c) All format 3 USE statements in which file-name-2 is specified and exception-name-2 is a level-3 exception-name … e) All format 3 USE statements in which file-name-2 is not specified and exception-name-1 is a level-3 exception-name … g) Any format 3 USE statements in which file-name-2 is not specified and exception-name-1 is a level-1 exception-name

specCitations.what: A WHEN match suppresses the USE F1 declarative too
specCitations.quote: If the input-output statement that raised the exception was specified in imperative-statement-1 of an exception-checking PERFORM statement and the exception condition did not match the criteria in any WHEN phrases within that PERFORM statement, or the input-output statement was not specified within the scope of an exception-checking PERFORM statement, the procedures associated with a USE statement are executed after completion of the standard input-output exception routine

specCitations.what: EXIT PERFORM in a Format-3 PERFORM; CYCLE forbidden
specCitations.quote: SR8: The EXIT PERFORM statement may be specified only in an inline or exception-checking PERFORM statement. The CYCLE phrase shall not be specified within an exception-checking PERFORM statement. — GR4: If an EXIT PERFORM statement is specified in an exception-checking PERFORM statement, control passes to an implicit CONTINUE statement immediately preceding the END-PERFORM phrase specified for that PERFORM statement or, if the FINALLY phrase is specified, immediately preceding the FINALLY phrase.

specCitations.what: EXIT PROGRAM … RAISING LAST is legal in a WHEN phrase
specCitations.quote: The LAST phrase may be specified only in a declarative procedure or a WHEN phrase in a PERFORM statement.

specCitations.what: RAISE confinement inside Format 3
specCitations.quote: Within an exception-checking PERFORM statement, the RAISE statement shall not be specified in any imperative statement other than imperative-statement-1.

specCitations.what: PUSH/POP forbidden inside Format 3
specCitations.quote: The POP directive shall not be specified within an exception checking PERFORM statement. / The PUSH directive shall not be specified within an exception checking PERFORM statement.

specCitations.what: The TURN-inside restriction that contradicts §14.9.28.4 GR14
specCitations.quote: A TURN directive shall not be specified within an exception processing PERFORM statement.

specCitations.what: EC-I-O-WARNING is toggled by a WHEN phrase
specCitations.quote: The exception-name EC-I-O-WARNING may be turned on only by specifying it explicitly within a TURN directive or by its presence in a WHEN phrase in an exception-checking PERFORM statement. Similarly, it may be turned off only by an explicit TURN directive or the end of an exception-checking PERFORM statement.

specCitations.what: Only the lowest-level names carry status indicators; a WHEN phrase enables checking
specCitations.quote: All exception-names may be specified in the WHEN phrase of a PERFORM statement or in TURN compiler directives to enable to enable or disable checking for a specific exception condition or exception conditions subordinate to the exception condition that is specified. By default, checking is not enabled for any exception condition.

specCitations.what: The EXCEPTION-* functions report the WHEN-selecting condition
specCitations.quote: If an exception condition is raised and an associated exception declarative is executed or a statement in an associated WHEN phrase in a PERFORM statement is executed, a reference to the EXCEPTION-STATUS function within that declarative or WHEN phrase returns identifying information associated with the exception condition that caused the declarative or WHEN phrase to be executed.

specCitations.what: A WHEN phrase's statements may reference nondeclarative procedures
specCitations.quote: 1) Statements in a WHEN phrase of an active PERFORM statement where that WHEN phrase is specified with an exception-name, a file-name, or an open option as specified in 14.9.28, PERFORM statement, General rule 17.

specCitations.what: Statement-level restrictions inside imperative-statement-1
specCitations.quote: CLOSE SR3: A CLOSE statement that specifies more than one file-name shall not be specified in imperative-statement-1 in an exception-checking PERFORM statement. — DELETE FILE SR4: A DELETE FILE statement that specifies more than one file-name shall not be specified in imperative-statement-1 in an exception-checking PERFORM statement. — CANCEL GR9: If the CANCEL statement is executed in the flow of control in imperative-statement-1 of a PERFORM statement that contains a WHEN phrase and an EC-I-O exception condition specified for that exception exists, the statements in that WHEN phrase are not executed.

specCitations.what: An ON SIZE ERROR phrase preempts the WHEN phrase
specCitations.quote: If an EC-SIZE exception condition exists during the execution of the arithmetic statement other than during item identification and a SIZE ERROR phrase is specified for the statement, processing of the size error condition occurs as described below for the SIZE ERROR phrase, and no statements in an applicable WHEN phrase in a containing PERFORM statement are executed and no EC-SIZE exception declaratives are performed.

specCitations.what: Return-to-end-of-statement for ACCEPT/DISPLAY handled by a WHEN
specCitations.quote: If the ACCEPT statement is specified in a statement that is in imperative-statement-1 in an exception-checking PERFORM statement and a WHEN phrase in that statement specifies the exception condition that occurred, control is transferred to the imperative-statement in that WHEN phrase and the flow of control is specified in the rules for the WHEN phrase. If control is returned from the WHEN phrase, control is then transferred to the end of the ACCEPT statement.

specCitations.what: Both halves are COBOL-2023 introductions
specCitations.quote: 36) PERFORM Statement. An exception checking variant of this statement has been added. 37) PERFORM Statement. The PERFORM statement now allows the UNTIL EXIT phrase which causes an infinite loop.

specCitations.what: Exception-names are context-sensitive in a WHEN phrase
specCitations.quote: All exception-names are context-sensitive because they may appear only following: RAISE, RAISING (in GOBACK and EXIT PROGRAM), USE EXCEPTION, WHEN phrase of the PERFORM statement, and in the TURN compiler directive.

grammarChanges.orderingNote: Place alphabetically in the same band as FINAL/FIRST (near CobolLexer.g4:437 `FINAL : 'FINAL' ;`). MUST be placed AFTER nothing that prefixes it — 'FINAL' and 'FINALLY' are distinct literals and ANTLR's implicit maximal-munch over literal tokens picks the longest match regardless of order, so no reordering hazard exists; keep the alphabetical convention.

grammarChanges.newText: LOCATION    : 'LOCATION' ;   // PERFORM Format 3 WITH LOCATION (ISO §14.9.28.2; also the >>TURN … WITH LOCATION directive word, §7.3.25.2); 2023 reserved word
grammarChanges.orderingNote: Place alphabetically near LINAGE/LIMIT (CobolLexer.g4 ~:448). No prefix collision with any existing literal (LOCK, LINE are distinct).

grammarChanges.newText:
| FINALLY
    | LOCATION
grammarChanges.orderingNote: MANDATORY reserved-word-collision mitigation. Both words are r85=false/r2002=false/r2014=false/r2023=true in tests/version-matrix/reserved-words.json, so a pre-2023 program may legally use FINALLY or LOCATION as a user-defined word. Adding them as unconditional lexer tokens would break that unless they also appear in the cobolWord funnel — exactly the pattern already used for COLS/COLUMNS (CobolLexer.g4:365-367 comment '§8.9 funnel gates ≥2002') and for EC/EO/CONDITION. Insert alphabetically inside cobolWord (after FACTORY / before FLOAT_BINARY for FINALLY; after LINE-family entries for LOCATION).

Insert this alternative IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the existing `| PERFORM statementBlock+ END_PERFORM` (currently CobolControlFlow.g4:27) and AFTER `| PERFORM performOptions+ statementBlock* END_PERFORM` (:26). Rationale: (1) it must outrank the bare inline-block form, whose `statementBlock+ END_PERFORM` cannot reach END-PERFORM across a WHEN token and would otherwise force a full-context re-prediction; (2) it must NOT outrank the performOptions+ form, or `PERFORM WITH TEST BEFORE UNTIL …` would try the LOCATION arm first on the shared WITH token. The Format-3 arm is unambiguously disambiguated by the REQUIRED `performWhenArm+`, so no IDENTIFIER-led alternative is introduced (DEVLOG 903 hazard avoided — every arm is keyword-led: PERFORM / WHEN / FINALLY / END-PERFORM).

grammarChanges.newText:
performWhenArm
    : WHEN OTHER EXCEPTION statementBlock+      # performWhenOtherArm
    | WHEN COMMON EXCEPTION statementBlock+     # performWhenCommonArm
    | WHEN performWhenSelector statementBlock+  # performWhenNamedArm
    ;
grammarChanges.orderingNote: ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. OTHER and COMMON must precede the general arm because `performWhenSelector`'s second alternative funnels through `useEcEntry : cobolWord (FILE fileName)*`, and cobolWord is a broad keyword funnel — if COMMON or OTHER is (or later becomes) a cobolWord member, a general-arm-first ordering would consume `WHEN OTHER EXCEPTION` as `WHEN <ec-name=OTHER>` followed by a bogus statement. Labelled alternatives (#performWhenOtherArm etc.) give the binder and the VersionConformancePass typed contexts instead of token probing.

`EXCEPTION useOnTarget?` must come FIRST: EXCEPTION is a hard token, and if EXCEPTION were also reachable through cobolWord the useEcEntry+ arm would shadow it. useOnTarget/useEcEntry are REUSED verbatim from the USE statement (CobolControlFlow.g4:218-228) — the same shapes GR17 delegates to, so no forked grammar. NOTE the shared-rule hazard (DEVLOG 736): useOnTarget and useEcEntry are now referenced from BOTH useStatement and performWhenSelector, so any VersionConformancePass visitor on those rules must positively guard on its parent context.
Standalone; referenced only from the Format-3 performStatement alternative. FINALLY is keyword-led so no DFA hazard.

Add `public BoundStatement BindExceptionCheckingPerform(Core.PerformStatementContext p)` — the whole Format-3 binder. Exact order of operations:
  1. `int id = ctx.EcState.NextPerformWhenId++;` `bool withLocation = p.LOCATION() is not null;`
  2. Partition `p.performWhenArm()` into named arms (PerformWhenNamedArmContext, source order preserved), at most one Other, at most one Common. REJECT (COBOLNET1578-family, see diagnostics): more than one WHEN OTHER; more than one WHEN COMMON; a WHEN OTHER or WHEN COMMON that is not after all named arms; a WHEN COMMON that is not the LAST arm (the format fixes the order OTHER then COMMON).
  3. Resolve each named arm's selector:
     - `EXCEPTION useOnTarget?`: fileName+ -> resolve each to a FileModel (unknown file -> the existing unresolved-file diagnostic path); INPUT/OUTPUT/I_O/EXTEND -> the runtime FileOpenMode ordinal (reuse whatever DataBinder/ProcedureTableBuilder uses for USE F1 ModeIndex); absent -> BareException=true.
     - `useEcEntry+`: for each entry, `cobolWord` is the exception-name; validate against `ExceptionCatalog.TryGet` -> COBOLNET1586 when unknown (mirror the >>TURN COBOLNET0711 text but with WHEN wording); then `info.IntroducedIn > edition.DialectLevel` -> REUSE COBOLNET0878 verbatim (same message the TurnState builder emits — an exception-name's per-edition window is one rule, one code). Each `FILE fileName` produces one (ec, file) pair; an entry with N FILE phrases produces N pairs; an entry with none produces one (ec, null) pair.
  4. SYNTAX RULES over the collected pairs:
     - SR16: any pair with a non-null File whose ec does not start with "EC-I-O" (ordinal, case-insensitive) -> COBOLNET1580.
     - SR15: an exception-name appearing in more than one pair with the SAME file (including twice with null file) -> COBOLNET1579.
     - SR14: a file-name appearing in more than one WHEN phrase where at least one of those appearances is NOT in conjunction with an exception-name (i.e. came from an `EXCEPTION useOnTarget` file list) -> COBOLNET1578.
  5. Build the GR14 implicit-TURN set: ONLY from the exception-name form. Literal reading of GR14 — "If checking for exception-name-1 or exception-name-2 is not enabled … an implicit TURN directive for exception-name-1 or exception-name-2 is assumed" — the `WHEN EXCEPTION file/INPUT/OUTPUT/I-O/EXTEND` forms name NO exception-name and therefore get NO implicit TURN; they ride the always-active I-O status path exactly as a USE F1 declarative does (§14.9.49.4 GR6). Also: WHEN OTHER contributes NOTHING to the implicit set (GR14: "only those exception conditions that are enabled at the point at which they are detected are processed by the WHEN OTHER phrase").
  6. `using (ctx.EcState.Turn.PushPerformScope(implicitOn, withLocation, p.Start.Line))` and with `ctx.EcState.PerformWhenStack` pushed as (Id:id, InHandler:false, InFinally:false), bind `statementBlock+` -> the body. Nested Format-3 PERFORMs nest the stack and the TurnState frames naturally.
  7. `using (ctx.EcState.Turn.PushSuppressAll())` and with the stack top's InHandler:true, bind every arm body, the Other body, the Common body, and (with InFinally:true as well) the FINALLY body. This is GR14's implicit PUSH ALL + TURN OFF ALL over the handler region, and it is what makes GR21 true by construction: no statement in a handler can carry a BoundEcChecked wrapper, so no handler statement can re-dispatch.
  8. GR16 enforcement over the FINALLY body: any BoundGoTo / BoundExitParagraph / BoundExitSection whose target lies outside the PERFORM, or any BoundGoBack / BoundStopRun / BoundExitProgram / BoundResume -> COBOLNET1583. (BoundExitPerformWhen inside FINALLY is LEGAL — GR16 defines it as transferring to the implicit CONTINUE after END-PERFORM.)
  9. `ctx.EcState.PerformWhen = true;` (drives the EcFeatures gate).
  10. Return `new BoundExceptionCheckingPerform(id, withLocation, body, namedArms, other, common, finallyBody, p.Start.Line)`.
  ALSO in this file: `BindRaise` (~:216) must reject a RAISE bound while `ctx.EcState.PerformWhenStack` has a top frame with InHandler==true or InFinally==true -> COBOLNET1582 (§14.9.29.3 SR4). And RESUME (`BindResume`, the deferral note at :122) stays declarative-only — remove the stale "a later wave" comment and replace it with the openQuestion-flagged decision recorded in the deep-dive.

Add, next to BoundInlinePerform (:495):

  `public sealed record BoundPerformWhenArm(PerformWhenKind Kind, IReadOnlyList<(string Ec, FileModel? File)> EcEntries, IReadOnlyList<FileModel> Files, int? ModeIndex, bool BareException, IReadOnlyList<BoundStatement> Body, int SourceLine);`
  `public sealed record BoundExceptionCheckingPerform(int Id, bool WithLocation, IReadOnlyList<BoundStatement> Body, IReadOnlyList<BoundPerformWhenArm> Arms, BoundPerformWhenArm? Other, BoundPerformWhenArm? Common, IReadOnlyList<BoundStatement> Finally, int SourceLine) : BoundStatement;`
  `public sealed record BoundExitPerformWhen(int ScopeId, int SourceLine) : BoundStatement;`
  Wire StatementChildren/Recurse for the ONE shared generated visitor (the standing PATH-A rule: never a bespoke switch) so the child statement lists (Body, each arm's Body, Other.Body, Common.Body, Finally) are all visited. Extend `EcFeatures` with a final positional member `bool HasPerformWhen` and include it in `Any`.

Add two pieces of emission context, mirroring the existing `SentenceEndLabel` precedent: `public string? PerformWhenEndLabel { get; set; }` (the `__pfEnd{N}` label an EXIT PERFORM inside imperative-statement-1 targets) and `public bool InPerformWhenHandler { get; set; }` (when true, a dispatcher-level transfer must RETURN a code from the generated handler method instead of writing `__pc`/`break`). Also `public int? PerformWhenScopeId { get; set; }` — the innermost Format-3 id, consumed by EcEmitter.EcDispatchExpr.

Three targeted changes, all guarded by DispatchState so nothing else changes shape:
  (1) `Visit(BoundGoTo)` (:110): when `_dispatchState.InPerformWhenHandler` -> `w.Line($"return {n.TargetPc};"); return true;` (the >=0 arm of the shared dispatch protocol — the CALLER performs the `__pc=r; break;`). Otherwise unchanged.
  (2) `Visit(BoundExitPerformWhen)` (new): when `_dispatchState.InPerformWhenHandler` -> `w.Line("return -4;"); return true;` else -> `w.Line($"goto {_dispatchState.PerformWhenEndLabel};"); return true;` (§14.9.14.4 GR4).
  (3) `Visit(BoundExitParagraph)` (:111) and the NEXT SENTENCE / sentence-end path (:140-143): when `InPerformWhenHandler`, these are dispatcher-level transfers that a handler method cannot perform -> report COBOLNET1583 at BIND time instead (see the binder change) rather than emitting broken code. Add a defensive `throw new InvalidOperationException` in the emitter so a missed bind check surfaces loudly rather than silently miscompiling.

The USE machinery (EmitUseMachinery, :156-230) and __IoCheck must respect §14.9.49.4 GR6: an I-O exception raised inside imperative-statement-1 that MATCHES a WHEN phrase must NOT also run the USE F1 declarative. This falls out automatically if — and only if — the I-O status->EC bridge routes through EcDispatchExpr. Verify at implement time that __IoCheckEc's `__sel` chain (EcEmitter.cs:335-349) is the one used for statements in a Format-3 body; if a statement instead hits the plain `__IoCheck` (no EC names enabled — the `WHEN EXCEPTION file-name` case, which gets NO implicit TURN), the WHEN arm must be consulted BEFORE the F1 declarative switch. Concretely: when a Format-3 scope is active, emit `int __s = __PfDisp{N}(__EcOfStatus(__st), __f); if (__s != -3) { …protocol…; return; }` ahead of the existing F1 file-name switch at :335.

Expose the open-mode of a file connector by key for the GR3b (`WHEN EXCEPTION INPUT|OUTPUT|I-O|EXTEND`) arms: `public static int ModeOf(string key)` returning the `FileOpenMode` ordinal (or -1 when not open / unknown). If the existing generated __IoCheck already obtains the mode by another route, REUSE that route instead and add nothing (the one-mechanism rule) — check DispatchEmitter.EmitUseMachinery's mode source first.

NO new runtime state is required. GR14/GR22's PUSH ALL / TURN OFF ALL / POP ALL are COMPILE-TIME directive semantics realized entirely by the TurnState scope frames — do NOT add a runtime turn stack. The §14.6.13.1.1 EXCEPTION-STATUS/-LOCATION/-STATEMENT guarantee inside a WHEN phrase already holds: the raise site calls ExceptionState.Set/SetIo BEFORE dispatching, and the handler runs synchronously inside __PfWhen{N}. Confirm ExceptionCatalog exposes `UnderLevel2` and a level accessor publicly (it does — EcEmitter.cs:270-286 already uses both).

PERFORM (exception-checking): exception-name '{name}' is specified more than once{ for file '{file}'} — ISO/IEC 1989:2023 §14.9.28.3 SR15 permits repetition only in conjunction with different file-names
PERFORM (exception-checking): the FILE phrase is specified with exception-name '{name}', which does not begin with 'EC-I-O' — ISO/IEC 1989:2023 §14.9.28.3 SR16
EXIT PERFORM CYCLE is not permitted within an exception-checking PERFORM statement — ISO/IEC 1989:2023 §14.9.14.3 SR8
the RAISE statement may appear only in imperative-statement-1 of an exception-checking PERFORM statement, not in a WHEN / WHEN OTHER / WHEN COMMON / FINALLY phrase — ISO/IEC 1989:2023 §14.9.29.3 SR4
the FINALLY phrase of an exception-checking PERFORM statement shall contain no statement that transfers control out of the PERFORM statement ('{statement}') — ISO/IEC 1989:2023 §14.9.28.4 GR16
the {PUSH|POP} directive shall not be specified within an exception-checking PERFORM statement — ISO/IEC 1989:2023 §7.3.22.3 SR4 / §7.3.20.3 SR4
the UNTIL EXIT phrase shall not be specified in, or under, a PERFORM statement with the VARYING phrase or with the TEST BEFORE or TEST AFTER phrase — ISO/IEC 1989:2023 §14.9.28.3 SR8
PERFORM (exception-checking): '{name}' in a WHEN phrase is not an exception-name of ISO/IEC 1989 §14.6.13.1 (and not a valid EC-USER-/EC-IMP- name)

PERFORM (exception-checking): the WHEN {OTHER|COMMON} EXCEPTION phrase may be specified at most once and shall follow all WHEN phrases that specify an exception-name or file-name (WHEN COMMON last) — ISO/IEC 1989:2023 §14.9.28.2 Format 3

editionGating.behaviorByEdition:
BOTH halves are COBOL-2023 introductions (Annex E.3.3 items 36 and 37); neither exists in 1985, 2002 or 2014.

(A) PERFORM … UNTIL EXIT — ALREADY GATED AND LANDED. --std 85 / 2002 / 2014: REJECT with COBOLNET0900 fired from VersionConformancePass.ParseArm.VisitPerformUntil on ctx.EXIT(). --std 2023 (default): ACCEPT. Plain `UNTIL condition-1` remains edition-invariant (1985-continuous) and is NOT gated. No implementation work remains on this row.

(B) PERFORM Format 3 (exception-checking) — NEW ROW. --std 85 / 2002 / 2014: REJECT with COBOLNET0900 ('the exception-checking PERFORM statement … requires COBOL-2023 (targeting COBOL-YYYY)'), fired on RECOGNITION from a new VersionConformancePass.ParseArm.VisitPerformStatement override keyed on `ctx.performWhenArm().Length > 0`. --std 2023: ACCEPT. Because the grammar is a SUPERSET grammar (edition predicates were removed from parsing), Format 3 PARSES at every --std and the single VersionConformancePass over the bound tree is the only enforcement point — do NOT add an {isXXXX()}? gate to the .g4.

RESERVED WORDS: FINALLY and LOCATION are already recorded r85=false / r2002=false / r2014=false / r2023=true in tests/version-matrix/reserved-words.json (rows at :1616 and :2300). Adding them as unconditional lexer tokens is only safe because they are ALSO added to the cobolWord funnel, which is what lets a pre-2023 program keep using them as user-defined words. No reserved-words.json change is required.

PER-EC EDITION WINDOWS: an exception-name written in a WHEN phrase is subject to the SAME per-name introduction window the >>TURN directive already enforces — reuse COBOLNET0878 verbatim (TurnState.Build already emits it), never a new code. This matters for the 2023-only EC families (VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE rows 40/61), though in practice a below-2023 Format 3 is already rejected by COBOLNET0900 first.

CONTINUITY: nothing is removed in any edition; both rows have removedIn:null.

tests.sketch:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. PFMWHEN1.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    PERFORM
        DISPLAY "A"
        RAISE EXCEPTION EC-USER-OOPS
        DISPLAY "B"
      WHEN EC-USER-OOPS
        DISPLAY "HANDLED"
      WHEN COMMON EXCEPTION
        DISPLAY "COMMON"
      FINALLY
        DISPLAY "FINALLY"
    END-PERFORM
    DISPLAY "AFTER"
    STOP RUN.

EXPECTED stdout (exact bytes "A\nHANDLED\nCOMMON\nB\nFINALLY\nAFTER\n"):
A / HANDLED / COMMON / B / FINALLY / AFTER.
DERIVATION: GR14 — the WHEN names EC-USER-OOPS, so an implicit TURN enables checking for it over imperative-statement-1; without that the RAISE would act as CONTINUE (§14.9.29.4 GR1 NOTE) and print nothing. DISPLAY "A" -> "A". RAISE raises EC-USER-OOPS (all user-defined conditions are NONFATAL, §14.6.13.1.1). §14.6.13.1.4 #2 / GR17: imperative-statement-2 runs -> "HANDLED"; no USE declarative is consulted. GR17 tail + GR19: control passes to imperative-statement-4 -> "COMMON". GR20 nonfatal: execution continues with an implicit CONTINUE immediately following the RAISE -> DISPLAY "B" -> "B". The last statement of imperative-statement-1 completes -> the end of the PERFORM, which per GR16 BEGINS at imperative-statement-5 -> "FINALLY". Then "AFTER".

ALSO include a second PERFORM in the same program raising a condition for which checking is NOT enabled anywhere and asserting NO handler output at all.

risks: DFA / alternative-order hazard in performWhenArm: `performWhenSelector`'s second alternative funnels through `useEcEntry : cobolWord (FILE fileName)*`, and cobolWord is a large keyword funnel. If OTHER or COMMON is (or later becomes) a cobolWord member, a general-arm-first ordering silently mis-parses `WHEN OTHER EXCEPTION`. MITIGATION (already in the design): one `performWhenArm` rule with the OTHER and COMMON alternatives FIRST. VERIFY cobolWord membership of OTHER/COMMON at implement time and add a parser unit test asserting the labelled context type.

SHARED-RULE OVER-FIRE (DEVLOG 736): `useOnTarget` and `useEcEntry` become reachable from BOTH useStatement and performWhenSelector. Any existing or future VersionConformancePass/binder visitor on those rules will now also fire inside a PERFORM. Audit every current visitor over those two rules and add a positive parent-context guard before landing.

Adding FINALLY and LOCATION as unconditional lexer tokens RESERVES them at every edition unless the cobolWord funnel rows land in the SAME change. Omitting the funnel rows breaks pre-2023 programs that use them as data-names — and the breakage is a raw parse error at a data-division line, far from any diagnostic that names the cause. This is the highest-probability regression in the whole item; ship the funnel rows and the --std 2014 user-word conformance case together.

Changing `EcEmitter.EcDispatchExpr` touches the SINGLE funnel every raise site uses (the fatal-gate catch, EmitRaise, EmitSizeHandling, __IoCheckEc). A bug there mis-routes EVERY exception in the compiler, not just Format-3 ones. Keep the change strictly conditional on `DispatchState.PerformWhenScopeId is int` so the null path is provably byte-identical, and assert that with the zero-scaffolding unit test.

Adding `-4` to the shared dispatch-result protocol (-1 / -2 / -3 / >=0) is a cross-cutting protocol change. Every existing consumer that does `if (r >= 0)` is safe (-4 < 0), but any consumer doing `if (r != -2) throw;` will now THROW on a -4 it should have honored. Audit all four existing epilogue sites and route them through the new shared `EmitDispatchEpilogue` helper rather than hand-editing each.

FINALLY must NOT be emitted as a C# `try/finally`. The intuitive translation is wrong: §14.6.13.1.3 #4 terminates the run unit abnormally after the WHEN/COMMON handler on the FATAL path, so FINALLY must be SKIPPED there. A C# finally would run it. The perform_when_fatal_terminates golden is the only thing that catches this — do not defer it.

GR20's nonfatal resumption ('an implicit CONTINUE statement immediately following the statement in imperative-statement-1 in which the exception condition occurred') is NOT expressible by a try/catch around the whole body. The design depends on the existing per-statement inline dispatch shape. Any attempt to 'simplify' Format 3 into a single try/catch over the body silently breaks GR20 and will pass a naive golden that raises on the last statement — hence the perform_when_nonfatal golden deliberately raises in the MIDDLE.

Tier order (GR3a-3g) beats source order. A naive source-order if/else chain compiles, runs, and passes any golden with a single arm — it only fails when a level-2 arm precedes a level-3 arm. perform_when_tier_order.cob is the guard; it must be in the same commit.

Dispatcher-level transfers (GO TO, EXIT PARAGRAPH, EXIT SECTION, NEXT SENTENCE) inside a WHEN handler cannot execute inside the generated __PfWhen method. GO TO is handled by returning the target pc through the existing >=0 protocol; the others are rejected at bind (COBOLNET1583/GR16 for FINALLY, and a defensive emitter throw elsewhere). If a handler statement kind is missed, the result is a C# compile error in generated code (loud) or, worse, a `break` against the wrong construct (silent). Add the defensive `InvalidOperationException` in StatementEmitter.

EcBinder.EcWrap early-outs on `Turn.AnyEnabled` (:291). If AnyEnabled is not made frame-aware, a Format-3 PERFORM in a program with no >>TURN directive at all binds ZERO checked statements and the whole feature is a silent no-op that still passes a golden whose handler never runs. Make the AnyEnabled change first and unit-test it.

The reserved-word FINALLY/LOCATION addition requires an ANTLR regen; per feedback_commit_generated_parser the Generated/ tree is a build output and a failed regen must FAIL the build. Ensure java + pwsh prerequisites are present before starting, and run the FULL legacy guard in the same change set (the standing grammar-change rule).

Effort: this is genuinely L. Recommended landing order (each with guard-fast green before the next): (1) lexer tokens + cobolWord funnel + full legacy guard; (2) grammar rules + the COBOLNET0900 gate + the constructs.json row + the matrix row — Format 3 parses and is correctly rejected below 2023, binds to BoundUnsupported at 2023; (3) TurnState scope frames + unit tests; (4) binder + bound tree + all syntax-rule diagnostics + negative fixtures; (5) emitter + the positive goldens; (6) the SR8 'under' check (COBOLNET1585) as an independent tail. Steps 1-2 alone already retire the 'raw syntax error instead of COBOLNET0900' defect.
openQuestions: SPEC CONFLICT — TURN inside a Format-3 PERFORM. §7.3.25.3 SR5 says flatly 'A TURN directive shall not be specified within an exception processing PERFORM statement', but §14.9.28.4 GR14 describes at length what a TURN directive WITHIN imperative-statement-1 does ('any TURN directive that turns off checking for an exception that is specified in a WHEN phrase will prevent that WHEN phrase from being invoked'). These cannot both hold. THIS SPEC IMPLEMENTS GR14 (allow and honor an interior TURN, no diagnostic) on the grounds that GR14 is the statement-specific, more detailed rule and that rejecting TURN would make GR14's text dead. Note the wording difference — SR5 says 'exception PROCESSING PERFORM' while PUSH/POP SR4 say 'exception CHECKING PERFORM'; SR5 may be intended to scope only to the WHEN/handler region (where checking is off anyway per GR14's TURN OFF ALL), which would reconcile them. OWNER DECISION NEEDED. If the owner rules for SR5-literal, add a tenth diagnostic and convert perform_when_turn_off_inside.cob from a golden to a negative fixture.

SPEC CONFLICT — does FINALLY run on the FATAL path? GR16 + NOTE 8 make imperative-statement-5 'the end of the PERFORM statement', but GR20 routes a fatal condition to §14.6.13.1.3, whose item 4 says the WHEN handler runs, then WHEN COMMON, then 'Execution of the last imperative statement is terminated abnormally' — with no mention of FINALLY. THIS SPEC IMPLEMENTS THE LITERAL #4 READING: FINALLY does NOT run on the fatal path (which is why FINALLY is emitted as plain sequential code, not a C# finally). This is counter-intuitive to anyone reading FINALLY as a try/finally and deserves explicit owner ratification, because it is baked into the emission shape.

EDITORIAL DEFECT in GR18 — the rule contains a duplicated sentence and a bogus cross-reference: 'control is passed to the end of the PERFORM statement or, if WHEN COMMON is specified, to imperative-statement-4. At the completion of the execution of imperative-statement-3, control is passed as indicated in General rule 14.9.29 or, if WHEN COMMON is specified, to imperative-statement-4.' 'General rule 14.9.29' is not a general rule number (§14.9.29 is the RAISE statement); GR20 is almost certainly meant (GR17's parallel sentence says 'as indicated in General rule 20'). THIS SPEC TREATS WHEN OTHER EXACTLY LIKE A NAMED WHEN for the GR20 fatality split. Verify against the real ISO PDF (specs/'ISO+IEC+1989-2023...COBOL.pdf') before coding — the markdown extraction may have corrupted this paragraph.

The MEANING of a bare `WHEN EXCEPTION` with no file-name and no open-mode. The Format-3 figure brackets the target as OPTIONAL, but USE Format 1 requires one of the choices and the spec never defines the bare form's scope. THIS SPEC treats it as 'any EC-I-O condition on any file' and places it in the GR3f (level-2) band. Alternative readings: (a) it is a syntax error and the bracket is a figure-extraction artifact; (b) it means EC-ALL. Verify the bracket against the ISO PDF.

RESUME inside a WHEN phrase. §14.9.33.3 SR1 confines RESUME to a declarative procedure, but §14.6.13.1.3 #4's NOTE 1 ('The user is able to continue by using a RESUME statement') is attached to the Format-3 WHEN rule. If RESUME is meant to be legal in a WHEN, the -2 (RESUME NEXT STATEMENT) protocol code must be reachable from __PfWhen and the fatal path must be suppressible. THIS SPEC KEEPS RESUME DECLARATIVE-ONLY (SR1 literal) and leaves the note unimplemented. Confirm §14.9.33.3 SR1's exact text against the PDF — I did not read §14.9.33 directly in this pass.

§14.9.28.3 SR8's 'or UNDER a PERFORM statement with the VARYING phrase' — is 'under' LEXICAL nesting or DYNAMIC range? For an out-of-line `PERFORM VARYING … proc` whose performed paragraph contains a `PERFORM UNTIL EXIT`, the UNTIL EXIT is dynamically under a VARYING PERFORM but not lexically inside it. A dynamic check is not statically decidable in general. THIS SPEC PROPOSES a LEXICAL-nesting-only check (COBOLNET1585) and documents the dynamic case as a non-detection. Owner ratification needed on the scoping.

Whether the GR3b open-mode arms (`WHEN EXCEPTION INPUT|OUTPUT|I-O|EXTEND`) can reuse an existing mode source. I did not fully trace how the generated __IoCheck obtains a connector's open mode for USE F1 mode-scoped declaratives (DispatchEmitter.EmitUseMachinery, :156-230). If it already has one, use it and add NO FileRegistry.ModeOf — the one-mechanism rule. Resolve by reading that method before writing the runtime change.

GR14's implicit-TURN set is derived ONLY from the exception-name WHEN forms in this design (the file/open-mode forms name no exception-name, so GR14's 'implicit TURN directive for exception-name-1 or exception-name-2' does not reach them; they ride the always-active I-O status path like a USE F1 declarative). This is a literal reading and it makes the file/mode arms behave exactly like USE F1, which §14.9.49.4 GR6 supports. But an alternative reading is that `WHEN EXCEPTION F-IN` implies an implicit TURN of EC-I-O for F-IN. The two differ observably when an EC-I-O condition on F-IN would otherwise be unchecked. Ratify before implementing step 4.

Statement-level Format-3 restrictions I found but did not design checks for, because they belong to their own verbs: §14.9.6 SR3 (a multi-file CLOSE) and §14.9.11 SR4 (a multi-file DELETE FILE) shall not appear in imperative-statement-1; §14.9.5 GR9 (a CANCEL's implicit CLOSEs do not run WHEN phrases). These need one diagnostic each (or a shared one) in the CLOSE/DELETE FILE binders, plus a CANCEL emitter suppression. Should they ride this item or be split into a follow-on? They are cheap but they touch three other verbs' binders.

spec.confidence: medium-high overall, with an explicit split. HIGH on: current state (every claim carries a file:line I read directly, and the (A)-is-already-done finding contradicts the scout doc precisely because I verified rather than repeated it); the spec citations (I read §14.9.28 in full, §14.6.13.1.1-.1.5, §14.9.49 in full, §14.9.14, §14.9.29.3, and the PUSH/POP/TURN syntax rules, and quoted verbatim); the grammar design (token existence, cobolWord funnel obligation, reserved-words.json state, and the useOnTarget/useEcEntry reuse are all verified against the actual .g4 files); the edition gating (Annex E.3.3 items 36/37 read verbatim; the existing perform-until-exit-2023 row read verbatim). MEDIUM on the EMITTER lowering: the __PfWhen/__PfDisp chain, the -4 protocol extension, and the label/goto shape are designed against the real generated-code shapes I read (EcEmitter's dispatch protocol, DispatchEmitter's switch(__pc) skeleton, StatementEmitter's existing SentenceEndLabel goto precedent) and I believe they compose, but I did not compile a prototype — the interaction between a `goto __pfEnd{N}` and the enclosing `switch (__pc)` case block, and the placement of the label relative to C# definite-assignment, need a real build to confirm. citationErrors: MISLABELED SECTION: the citation headed "§14.9.33 RESUME (via §11365)" is not §14.9.33 at all. '11365' is a LINE NUMBER in specs/ISO_COBOL.md, and the quoted text ("1) Statements in a WHEN phrase of an active PERFORM statement where that WHEN phrase is specified with an exception-name, a file-name, or an open option as specified in 14.9.28, PERFORM statement, General rule 17.") is item 1 of §9.1.12 Input-output exception processing. The design also never uses §9.1.12's actual operative content: "The first one in the list that matches is the one selected. Any others that match are ignored." and its NOTE "EC-ALL and EC-I-O would match any input-output exception condition."

MISREPRESENTED RULE — the single most consequential citation error. openQuestions #5 asserts "§14.9.33.3 SR1 confines RESUME to a declarative procedure" and admits "I did not read §14.9.33 directly in this pass." The actual §14.9.33.3 SR1 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:30310) reads verbatim: "The RESUME statement may be specified only in a declarative or in an imperative statement in a WHEN phrase of an exception-checking PERFORM statement. In the latter case, the NEXT STATEMENT phrase shall be specified." RESUME in a WHEN phrase is EXPLICITLY LEGAL. §14.9.33.1 confirms: "The RESUME statement transfers control to a procedure-name or to the statement following the statement that caused a declarative or an imperative-statement in a WHEN phrase of an exception-checking PERFORM statement to be executed." Annex D (line 45606) confirms again: "3) In an exception-checking PERFORM statement, execute a RESUME statement with the NEXT phrase…". This is not an open question; the design's "KEEPS RESUME DECLARATIVE-ONLY" decision is simply wrong.

MERGED/CHERRY-PICKED QUOTE: the citation headed "§14.9.1 ACCEPT (line 25787) / §14.9.12 DISPLAY (line 26957)" presents ONE quote (ACCEPT's wording, ending "…control is then transferred to the end of the ACCEPT statement") as if it covered both. DISPLAY's actual text at :26957 is different and shorter: "If the DISPLAY statement is specified in a statement that is in imperative-statement-1 in an exception-checking PERFORM statement and a WHEN phrase. If control is returned from the PERFORM statement, control is then transferred to the end of the DISPLAY statement and the NOT ON EXCEPTION phrase, if specified, is ignored." The dropped clause ("the NOT ON EXCEPTION phrase, if specified, is ignored") is a behavioral requirement the design therefore never implements. Note the DISPLAY sentence is also visibly truncated in the markdown extraction — verify against the PDF.

ELIDED LOAD-BEARING CLAUSE in the §14.9.28.4 GR20 quote. The design's ellipsis hides: "If an exception-condition was raised during the processing of imperative-statement-1 that caused a transfer to the imperative-statement in a WHEN phrase, and the processing in General rules 17, 18, and 19 is completed, return depends on whether the exception condition was fatal or nonfatal." The nonfatal-resumption rule is CONDITIONAL on a WHEN transfer having actually occurred; as quoted it reads unconditional.
§14.6.13.1.3 item 4 quote is verbatim but the design omits items 1 and 3 that PRECEDE it in the same ordered list, both of which change the Format-3 fatal path (see missingSpecBranches).

The design's editionGating section claims the only edition effect is a clean 2023 introduction gate, and never mentions row 26 or Annex E.2 item 19.
designDefects: SPEC-VIOLATING EMISSION — GO TO inside a WHEN phrase. §14.9.17.3 SR3 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:27634) states flatly: "A GO TO statement shall not be specified in a WHEN phrase of an exception-checking PERFORM statement." The design never cites this rule and instead BUILDS SUPPORT FOR IT: the StatementEmitter change #1 says "Visit(BoundGoTo) (:110): when _dispatchState.InPerformWhenHandler -> w.Line($\"return {n.TargetPc};\")", and the __PfDisp protocol's ">=0 resume pc" arm exists specifically to carry a GO TO target out of a handler. That whole mechanism implements a construct the spec forbids. It must be a bind-time diagnostic instead, and the >=0-from-handler path deleted.

The design rejects a construct the spec permits and permits one it forbids, in the same subsystem: RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT is legal (indeed the only legal RESUME form) in a WHEN phrase per §14.9.33.3 SR1, and the design excludes it; GO TO is illegal in a WHEN phrase per §14.9.17.3 SR3, and the design supports it. Both must flip. Note the -2 (RESUME NEXT) protocol code the design says is unreachable from __PfWhen is in fact exactly what §14.9.33.4 GR2a requires there, and §14.6.13.1.3 #4 NOTE 1 ("The user is able to continue by using a RESUME statement") makes RESUME the ONLY way to survive a fatal condition caught by a WHEN — a capability the design's fatal path cannot express.

The design has no mechanism for the general conditional-phrase preemption rule. §14.6.13.1.4 item 1 (which PRECEDES the WHEN item 2 in the same ordered list) and §14.6.13.1.3 item 1 make ANY conditional phrase without a NOT phrase take precedence over the WHEN arm; Annex D.2.3.4.3 enumerates it: the WHEN code is not executed when the condition is "1) invalid key and the INVALID KEY phrase is specified; or 2) at end and the AT END phrase is specified; or 3) end-of-page and AT EOP phrase or AT END-OF-PAGE phrase is specified; or 4) any exception and ON EXCEPTION phrase is specified." §14.9.49.4 GR6 repeats it ("unless an AT END or INVALID KEY phrase takes precedence"). The design implements only the ON SIZE ERROR instance via §14.7.5 and treats it as a one-off, so the whole family (AT END, INVALID KEY, AT EOP/END-OF-PAGE, ON EXCEPTION, ON OVERFLOW) is unhandled — and worse, §14.6.13.1.3 item 1 says a FATAL condition so handled follows the NONFATAL rules, i.e. no abnormal termination, which the design's fatal-path emission cannot express.

Exception OBJECTS are absent from the entire design. §14.6.13.1.1: "An exception condition is either a condition associated with a specific exception status indicator or an exception object" and "An exception object is a nonfatal exception condition". §14.9.49.4 GR3 opens "If an exception object was raised, the method specified in General rule 14 is applied. Otherwise, the following rules are applied in order" — so GR17's delegation to GR3a–3g explicitly does NOT cover objects, while GR18's WHEN OTHER ("any exception condition that is not associated with any exception condition specified in a WHEN phrase") arguably does. The design's own evidence notes the grammar already accepts `RAISE objectReference`, so an object CAN be raised inside imperative-statement-1 today. The design must state and implement a rule; it currently has none.

The grammar admits a Format-3 PERFORM with ZERO named WHEN arms (`performWhenArm+` where the arm rule includes the OTHER and COMMON alternatives), e.g. `PERFORM CONTINUE WHEN OTHER EXCEPTION CONTINUE END-PERFORM`. In the §14.9.28.2 Format-3 figure the OTHER, COMMON and FINALLY groups are square-bracketed (optional) but the named WHEN group is NOT — it is a required repeating group. COBOLNET1587 as specified only polices order and multiplicity, not the at-least-one-named-arm requirement. Either add the rule or record it as a deliberate figure-reading with PDF verification.

GR22's second sentence — "If there is a TURN directive within the range of the PERFORM statement, the checking for that TURN directive is retained" — says RANGE, and §14.9.28.4 GR1 defines range to include declarative procedures executed as a result of statements in the range. The TurnState scope-frame model is purely lexical, so a >>TURN in a performed procedure is not retained. At minimum document this as a scoped non-implementation. Separately: GR22's presupposition that an interior TURN exists is a THIRD independent witness (with GR14) against the §7.3.25.3 SR5 literal reading; openQuestion #1 should record that the evidence is 2-to-1 for GR14, not evenly balanced.
