§14.9.33.3 SR1 + §14.9.33.4 GR2a — RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT in a WHEN phrase (legal, and the NEXT STATEMENT phrase is MANDATORY there). Needs: binder acceptance in a WHEN, a diagnostic for `RESUME AT procedure-name-1` in a WHEN, the -2 protocol code reachable from __PfWhen, and a golden. Currently designed as unsupported.

§14.9.22 INITIALIZE SR2 (:27902) — "Identifier-1 shall be specified only once if the INITIALIZE statement is specified in imperative-statement-1 of an exception-checking PERFORM statement." Not in the design.
§14.9.23 INITIATE SR3 (:28051) — an INITIATE specifying more than one report-name shall not be specified in an exception checking PERFORM statement. Not in the design.
§14.9.26 MERGE SR1 (:28595) — "A MERGE statement may appear anywhere in the procedure division except in imperative-statement-1 of an exception-checking PERFORM statement…". Not in the design.
§14.9.27 OPEN SR3 (:29161) — an OPEN specifying file-name-1 more than once shall not be specified in imperative-statement-1. Not in the design.
§14.9.37 SORT SR3 (:31821) — "A SORT statement shall not appear in imperative-statement-1 of an exception-checking PERFORM statement…". Not in the design.
§14.9.45 TERMINATE SR3 (:32611) — a TERMINATE specifying more than one report-name shall not be specified in an exception checking PERFORM statement. Not in the design.

§14.9.50 VALIDATE SR6 (:33139) — "A VALIDATE statement that specifies more than one identifier shall not be specified in an exception-checking PERFORM statement." Not in the design. (The design's openQuestion #9 lists only CLOSE SR3, DELETE FILE SR4 and CANCEL GR9 — 7 of the 10 statement-level restrictions are missing.)

Per-statement WHEN-return general rules beyond ACCEPT/DISPLAY: OPEN (:29339 — "If the OPEN statement is specified in imperative-statement-1 … and there is an applicable WHEN phrase … execution continues according to the rules for that WHEN phrase. No applicable USE declarative is executed."), RECEIVE (:30205), SEND (:31070), WRITE (:33577 — the END-OF-PAGE-absent case). Each specifies where control goes after the WHEN returns; none are cited or designed.

§14.6.13.1.3 item 3 — "If the exception condition is a fatal EC-I-O exception condition, then the rules for 9.1.13, I-O status apply, then if the implementor has not specified otherwise, the following rules apply for all fatal exception conditions." This runs BEFORE item 4's WHEN dispatch and makes item 4 implementor-overridable. Omitted, and it interacts directly with the design's FINALLY-on-fatal decision.

§9.1.12 Input-output exception processing — the ordered 'applicable exception processing statements' list (WHEN phrase first, then USE declarative), its tie-break ("The first one in the list that matches is the one selected"), and its NOTE that EC-ALL and EC-I-O match ANY input-output exception condition. The NOTE directly answers the design's openQuestion about where a bare `WHEN EXCEPTION` / an EC-ALL arm sits relative to I-O conditions.

Annex E.2 item 19 (a and b) — the 2023 SUBSTANTIVE behavior change bundled with this feature: (a) with no INVALID KEY phrase, a declarative specifying INPUT/OUTPUT/I-O/EXTEND is NOW executed on an invalid key condition (previously not); (b) for a READ exception that is neither invalid-key nor at-end, an INPUT or I-O declarative is NOW executed (previously not). This is a per-edition behavior difference in EXISTING constructs, already tracked as VCR row 26, and belongs in this item's editionGating and version-matrix coverage. Entirely absent.
The at-least-one-named-WHEN requirement implied by the unbracketed WHEN group in the §14.9.28.2 Format-3 figure (see designDefects).

§14.9.14.3 SR3's companion constraint to the SR6 the design does cite: an EXIT PROGRAM RAISING an EC-USER level-3 exception-name requires that name in the procedure division header RAISING phrase — relevant because SR6 makes `EXIT PROGRAM … RAISING LAST` legal in a WHEN and the design plans no check on the sibling form.
corrections: Add a diagnostic (next in the 1578+ block) for §14.9.17.3 SR3: "a GO TO statement shall not be specified in a WHEN phrase of an exception-checking PERFORM statement — ISO/IEC 1989:2023 §14.9.17.3 SR3", raised in ControlFlowBinder.BindGoTo whenever ctx.EcState.PerformWhenStack's top frame has InHandler==true or InFinally==true. DELETE the StatementEmitter change #1 (the `return {n.TargetPc};` handler path) and the ">=0 resume pc" arm of the __PfWhen/__PfDisp protocol — with GO TO forbidden and RESUME AT procedure-name forbidden, no handler can produce a pc. Add a negative fixture tests/conformance/negative/perform_when_goto.cob.

Reverse the RESUME decision. §14.9.33.3 SR1 permits RESUME in a WHEN phrase and REQUIRES the NEXT STATEMENT form there. In EcBinder/BindResume: when the innermost PerformWhenScope has InHandler==true, accept `RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT` and reject `RESUME AT procedure-name-1` with a new diagnostic citing §14.9.33.3 SR1. Emit it from __PfWhen{N} as `return -2;` (the existing RESUME-NEXT protocol code), and make the raise-site epilogue honor -2 by continuing at the implicit CONTINUE after the raising statement per §14.9.33.4 GR2a — which for the NONFATAL case is byte-identical to GR20's resumption, and for the FATAL case must SUPPRESS the abnormal termination (§14.6.13.1.3 #4 NOTE 1). Add tests/conformance/2023/perform_when_resume_next.cob covering both fatalities. Delete openQuestion #5. Also note that FINALLY is not a WHEN phrase, so RESUME remains illegal in imperative-statement-5.

Add one shared diagnostic for the ten statement-level restrictions inside imperative-statement-1, parameterized on the statement name and the specific rule: CLOSE §14.9.6 SR3, DELETE FILE §14.9.11 SR4, INITIALIZE §14.9.22 SR2, INITIATE §14.9.23 SR3, MERGE §14.9.26 SR1, OPEN §14.9.27 SR3, SORT §14.9.37 SR3, TERMINATE §14.9.45 SR3, VALIDATE §14.9.50 SR6 — plus the CANCEL §14.9.5 GR9 emitter suppression (a CANCEL's implicit CLOSEs do not run WHEN phrases). Implement as ONE check driven by a table keyed on bound-node kind, consulted from the Format-3 body binder, rather than edits scattered across nine verb binders. Ship one negative fixture with all nine variants. Resolve openQuestion #9 as 'rides this item' — a table lookup is cheaper than a split.

Add a design section for the conditional-phrase preemption family, citing §14.6.13.1.4 item 1, §14.6.13.1.3 item 1, §14.9.49.4 GR6 and Annex D.2.3.4.3 items 1–4. Rule: if the raising statement carries a conditional phrase WITHOUT a NOT phrase that covers the condition (AT END, INVALID KEY, AT EOP/AT END-OF-PAGE, ON EXCEPTION, ON SIZE ERROR, ON OVERFLOW), the __PfDisp call at that site must be SUPPRESSED entirely (emit the literal -3 path, not the __PfDisp path) and, per §14.6.13.1.3 item 1, a fatal condition so handled must follow the nonfatal rules (no abnormal termination). Generalize EcEmitter.EcDispatchExpr's new PerformWhenScopeId branch to consult a per-statement 'has covering conditional phrase' flag already available on EcStatementInfo. Add a golden asserting `READ … AT END` inside a Format-3 body with a `WHEN EC-I-O-AT-END` arm runs the AT END phrase and NOT the arm.

Add an explicit exception-object rule and cite it. §14.9.49.4 GR3's preamble excludes objects from the GR3a–3g tier order that GR17 delegates to, so a named WHEN arm can never match an object; §14.6.13.1.1 makes an object an exception condition, so GR18's WHEN OTHER catches it. Recommended: named arms never match an exception object; WHEN OTHER EXCEPTION does; an object reaching no arm falls to §14.6.13.1.5. If the implementer disagrees, record the alternative and its citation — but the design may not remain silent, because `RAISE objectReference` already parses inside imperative-statement-1.

Fix the three citation labels: retitle "§14.9.33 RESUME (via §11365)" to "§9.1.12 Input-output exception processing, item 1"; split the merged ACCEPT/DISPLAY citation into two, using DISPLAY's own text at :26957 including "and the NOT ON EXCEPTION phrase, if specified, is ignored" (and flag that sentence as extraction-damaged — verify in the PDF); restore the elided middle clause of the GR20 quote.

Change the constructs.json vcr field to reference the EXISTING docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row 79 (:196) and clear its `<!-- todo -->` marker; do not allocate a new row. Add an editionGating paragraph for Annex E.2 item 19 a/b (VCR row 26, :127): at --std 2023 a declarative specifying INPUT/OUTPUT/I-O/EXTEND is executed for an invalid-key condition with no INVALID KEY phrase, and for a non-at-end/non-invalid-key READ exception; at 85/2002/2014 it is not. Add the corresponding version-matrix behavior rows.

Either add an at-least-one-named-WHEN check (extend COBOLNET1587 or add a code) or record an explicit figure-reading decision with PDF verification. The §14.9.28.2 figure brackets OTHER, COMMON and FINALLY but not the named WHEN group.

Amend openQuestion #1: §14.9.28.4 GR22 ("If there is a TURN directive within the range of the PERFORM statement, the checking for that TURN directive is retained") is a second rule that presupposes a legal interior TURN, so the evidence for honoring GR14 over §7.3.25.3 SR5 is stronger than the design states. Also record that the TurnState frame model implements only LEXICAL nesting while GR22 says 'range' (which §14.9.28.4 GR1 extends to performed declaratives) — a documented scoped non-implementation.

Add the per-statement WHEN-return rules for OPEN (:29339), RECEIVE (:30205), SEND (:31070) and WRITE (:33577) alongside the ACCEPT/DISPLAY ones, and add §14.6.13.1.3 item 3 (fatal EC-I-O routes through §9.1.13 I-O status first, and item 4 is implementor-overridable) to the fatal-path design — this bears directly on the unresolved FINALLY-on-fatal question, which should stay an owner decision but must be restated with items 1 and 3 in view, not item 4 alone.

citationErrors: Repo line citations are mostly accurate but several are off by 1-2 lines and must not be trusted verbatim by a serial implementer: 'EcEmitter.cs:36-37 EcDispatchExpr' is actually EcEmitter.cs:35-36; 'EcEmitter.cs:120-136 the fatal-gate try/catch' is actually :118-136 (the epilogue lines are :131-133); 'StatementEmitter.cs:140 SentenceEndLabel goto precedent' is actually StatementEmitter.cs:138; 'tests/version-matrix/constructs.json:175-185' — the perform-until-exit-2023 row begins at :174.

'src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolControlFlow.g4:18-28 — performStatement has 7 alternatives' is correct in count but the cited span is :18-28 including the rule header; the alternatives are :19-27. Cosmetic, but the implementer inserting 'IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the existing | PERFORM statementBlock+ END_PERFORM (currently CobolControlFlow.g4:27)' should be told the anchor is the TEXT of that alternative, not the line number, which will shift.

The spec's claim that EcEmitter's EmitDispatchSelector is 'the exact template the WHEN selector reuses' misreads what that template covers: EmitDispatchSelector (EcEmitter.cs:253-287) emits ONLY the GR3c/GR3d/GR3e/GR3f/GR3g tiers. GR3a and GR3b (file-name and open-mode scoped Format-1 declaratives) are NOT in it — they live in the __IoCheck selector generated by DispatchEmitter.EmitUseMachinery. The spec's __PfWhen{N} pseudo-code presents GR3a/GR3b as if copied from the same template; they are not.

The ISO citations themselves could not be re-verified in this pass (specs/ISO_COBOL.md is a private submodule not checked out in this working tree). Every §/GR quotation in the spec is therefore UNVERIFIED by this review — including the GR18 'editorial defect' claim and the §14.9.33.3 SR1 text the researcher admits not having read. A second pass with the submodule initialized (git submodule update --init --recursive) is required before any of the GR14/GR16/GR20/GR21 semantics are baked into the emitter.
currentStateErrors: FALSE 'no existing mechanism' claim for the unknown-exception-name diagnostic. The spec proposes NEW code COBOLNET1586 for "'{name}' in a WHEN phrase is not an exception-name". That diagnostic ALREADY EXISTS as COBOLNET0711, and already takes a caller-supplied context string: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/EcBinder.cs:97 `ctx.Edition.Error("COBOLNET0711", $"{context}: '{name}' is not an exception-name of ISO/IEC 1989 §14.6.13.1 (and not a valid EC-USER-/EC-IMP- name)")`, with the identical text emitted at TurnState.cs:46 and ProcedureTableBuilder.cs:425. COBOLNET1586's proposed message is a near-verbatim copy. This is a second mechanism for a job that already has one, and it contradicts the spec's own stated rationale two paragraphs earlier for reusing COBOLNET0878 ('an exception-name's per-edition window is one rule, one code').

THREE bound-node type names in the design DO NOT EXIST. The GR16 FINALLY transfer-out check (EcBinder step 8) names `BoundExitSection`, `BoundStopRun`, and `BoundGoBack`. Verified: there is no BoundExitSection anywhere — ControlFlowBinder.BindExit returns `new BoundUnsupported("EXIT SECTION")` (EXIT SECTION is NOT IMPLEMENTED AT ALL, so the GR16 check cannot key on it); STOP RUN is `BoundStop(TerminationStatus? Status)` (BoundTree.cs:393); GOBACK binds via `Call.BindGoback(gb)` (StatementBinder.cs:304) and there is no `BoundGoBack` record in BoundTree.cs. `BoundResume(int TargetPc)` (BoundTree.cs:795) and `BoundExitParagraph(int SourceLine)` (:514) are the only two named correctly.

MISSED EXISTING MECHANISM for running a handler body. The spec asserts handler bodies must be emitted inline into a generated `__PfWhen{N}` method, and never notes that the compiler ALREADY has exactly one mechanism for running an exception-handler body: `__RunUse(int __id, int __startPc, int __endPc)` (DispatchEmitter.cs:176-184), which re-enters the PC dispatcher over the handler's pc range and converts a ResumeSignal into the dispatch-result code. Every existing USE declarative handler runs that way. Emitting WHEN/FINALLY bodies into a separate C# method is a SECOND mechanism for handler-body execution, and it is the direct cause of defects 4, 6 and 9 below (dispatcher-level statements stop working inside it). The spec must either justify the fork explicitly against feedback_singular_pattern, or lower the arms into pc-space paragraphs like every other handler.

The 'VCR row 79 — CONFIRM before committing' uncertainty is resolvable NOW and the answer is yes: docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md:196 is literally `| 79 | PERFORM statement — exception-checking variant | E.3.3 item 36 | 2014→2023 | ... | new-feature-gate <!-- todo --> |`, and row 80 is the already-consumed PERFORM UNTIL EXIT row. Row 79 is free and correct. The `<!-- todo -->` marker on :196 must be cleared in the same change set.

The stated DFA risk 'if OTHER or COMMON is (or later becomes) a cobolWord member' is currently FALSE and should be stated as such: grep of CobolWords.g4 shows neither OTHER nor COMMON (nor EXCEPTION, nor FILE) is a cobolWord alternative today. The mitigation ordering is still correct as future-proofing, but the implementer should not be led to believe there is a live collision.
designDefects: FATAL: the TurnState scope-frame design mutates a PROCESS-WIDE STATIC SINGLETON. `TurnState.Build` returns `public static readonly TurnState Empty` whenever the group has no >>TURN events (TurnState.cs:29,38) — which is the COMMON case for a Format-3 program. `PushPerformScope` / `PushSuppressAll` as specified mutate instance state (`_scopes`), so binding a Format-3 PERFORM in a directive-free program pushes frames onto `TurnState.Empty`, leaking scope state across compilation units, across programs in a group, and across parallel test compilations in the same process. Non-deterministic, and it will corrupt unrelated tests.

AnyEnabled is being given two incompatible meanings. TurnState.cs:62-64 documents it as the GROUP-level EC-machinery gate, and its real consumer is BinderDriver.cs:83 `bool ecActive = turn.AnyEnabled || units.Any(u => u.Bound.Ec is { Any: true })` — evaluated AFTER all units are bound, i.e. after every Format-3 frame has been popped. A scope-transient `|| _scopes.Any(...)` therefore contributes nothing at that call site while silently changing the property's contract. The EcWrap early-out (EcBinder.cs:291) needs a DIFFERENT, scope-local predicate.

AnyEnabledFor is not addressed at all. BinderDriver.cs:383 `data.ExternalDescribe = Procedure.EcBinder.ExternalNames.Any(session.Turn.AnyEnabledFor)` drives EC-EXTERNAL descriptor registration and is likewise a post-bind group-level query. A WHEN phrase naming an EC-EXTERNAL-* condition enables checking for it (GR14) but would leave ExternalDescribe false, so the descriptors the check needs are never emitted. Scope frames structurally cannot answer this query; a group-level accumulation set of WHEN-named exception-names is required.

The `-4` EXIT-PERFORM protocol code carries no scope identity, so it is WRONG under nesting. `__PfDisp{M}` chains outward (`return __r == -3 ? __PfDisp{outer}(...) : __r`), so a `-4` produced by the OUTER PERFORM's WHEN handler is returned through the INNER PERFORM's raise site, whose epilogue emits `if (__r == -4) goto __pfEnd{inner};`. Control lands at the end of the INNER PERFORM instead of the outer one, silently violating §14.9.14.4 GR4. The escape code must encode the scope id (e.g. a distinct negative band per scope, or an out-parameter), and the epilogue must compare against its OWN id.

LARGEST UNADDRESSED GRAMMAR HAZARD — WHEN ambiguity with nested EVALUATE/SEARCH. `evaluateStatement : EVALUATE ... evaluateWhenClause+ END_EVALUATE?` (CobolControlFlow.g4:78-82) and `searchStatement : SEARCH ... searchWhenClause+ END_SEARCH?` (:126-131) have OPTIONAL scope terminators. Inside `PERFORM <statementBlock+> WHEN ...`, an EVALUATE or SEARCH written without its explicit terminator makes the PERFORM's WHEN arms indistinguishable from the inner statement's WHEN clauses. `evaluateWhenItem : valueRange | valueOperand | condition` will silently consume `WHEN EC-USER-A` as a value operand, and `evaluateWhenClause`'s explicit `| WHEN OTHER statementBlock*` alternative will swallow `WHEN OTHER EXCEPTION ...`. Greedy-subrule/first-alternative resolution means this mis-parses with NO diagnostic. The design has no mitigation, no ordering note, and no test.

`performWhenSelector`'s second alternative `useEcEntry+` is an IDENTIFIER-led greedy list (useEcEntry : cobolWord (FILE fileName)*, CobolControlFlow.g4:218-220) terminated here by `statementBlock+` rather than by the period that terminates it in useStatement. This is the DEVLOG-903 hazard class in a subtler form: the funnel must stop at the first statement-starting token, and any statement starter that is (or becomes) a cobolWord member is absorbed into the exception-name list. Needs an explicit non-greedy/guarded formulation and a dedicated parser test asserting arm boundaries.

EXIT PARAGRAPH, EXIT SECTION and NEXT SENTENCE inside a WHEN / WHEN OTHER / WHEN COMMON arm are LEGAL COBOL (GR16's transfer-out prohibition applies only to imperative-statement-5), yet the design has no lowering for them — only 'a defensive InvalidOperationException in StatementEmitter'. That is a compiler CRASH on legal source, and it violates process rule 3 (implement completely to the spec, never scope to what a test references). BoundExitParagraph's emission uses `_dispatchState.CurrentPc + 1` (StatementEmitter.cs:111), which is meaningless inside a generated handler method — a direct consequence of the second-mechanism fork above.

`(WITH? LOCATION)?` makes WITH optional, but the format the spec itself quotes is `[ WITH LOCATION ]` — WITH is REQUIRED when LOCATION is written. This is an unratified leniency introduced silently. Either cite the house optional-word tolerance precedent (as useStatement does for STANDARD/ON at CobolControlFlow.g4:180-182) in the grammar comment, or write `(WITH LOCATION)?`.

The DEVLOG-736 shared-rule audit is listed as a RISK, not performed. `useOnTarget` and `useEcEntry` become reachable from a second parent; the spec instructs 'audit every current visitor over those two rules' but names zero visitors and provides no result. That audit is a required deliverable of this design, not a note for the implementer.

The FINALLY/LOCATION cobolWord funnel rows make both words legal user-defined words at EVERY edition INCLUDING 2023, yet the spec's own test asserts 'the same program at --std 2023 must be REJECTED by the reserved-word check'. No semanticChange wires that rejection; src/Cobol.Net.Editions/ReservedWords.cs / ReservedWords.Table.cs are never mentioned. As written the 2023 half of that test cannot pass.
missingSpecBranches: GR3a / GR3b — the `WHEN EXCEPTION file-name-1` and `WHEN EXCEPTION INPUT|OUTPUT|I-O|EXTEND` selector families (half of all Format-3 WHEN forms) have NO completed design. The spec places them in __PfWhen{N} but then concedes in the DispatchEmitter change that the I-O routing must be 'verified at implement time', and in an openQuestion that it never traced how __IoCheck obtains a connector's open mode. Since __EcDispatch implements only GR3c-g and GR3a/3b live in __IoCheck, this is an undesigned seam, not a detail.

§14.7.5 (ON SIZE ERROR preempts the WHEN phrase) is cited verbatim in specCitations but appears in NO semanticChange and NO test. EcEmitter.EmitSizeHandling is named as a raise site whose behavior changes via EcDispatchExpr — which is exactly the WRONG direction: the spec requires SIZE ERROR to SUPPRESS the WHEN arm.
§14.9.1 ACCEPT / §14.9.12 DISPLAY 'control is then transferred to the end of the ACCEPT/DISPLAY statement' after a WHEN arm returns — cited, never designed, never tested.

§14.9.14.3 SR6 (EXIT PROGRAM … RAISING LAST is legal in a WHEN phrase) — cited, but no binder change; the current BindExit RAISING path (ControlFlowBinder.cs:~95) is unmodified, so LAST inside a WHEN will hit whatever confinement check exists today.

§14.6.13.1.1's EXCEPTION-STATUS guarantee inside a WHEN phrase is asserted to 'already hold' with no code change, but the raise site sets ExceptionState only on some paths (EcEmitter.cs:130-131 sets it only `if (ec.Info.WithLocation)`). For a WHEN-selected condition the status must be set unconditionally. One golden mentions it; no semanticChange implements it.

§7.3.25.4 GR4's second half — EC-I-O-WARNING 'may be turned off only by an explicit TURN directive or the END of an exception-checking PERFORM statement' — has no test and no analysis of the interaction with an ENCLOSING >>TURN that had it on (GR22 says such checking is retained; a frame pop cannot distinguish).

§14.9.28.4 GR22's 'If there is a TURN directive within the range of the PERFORM statement, the checking for that TURN directive is retained' — no design. Interior events stay in `_events` and remain line-ordered, so they will keep applying after END-PERFORM; whether that satisfies GR22 or over-applies is unanalyzed and untested.

§14.9.6 SR3 (multi-file CLOSE), §14.9.11 SR4 (multi-file DELETE FILE) and §14.9.5 GR9 (CANCEL's implicit CLOSEs do not run WHEN phrases) are found, cited, and then deliberately EXCLUDED to openQuestions. Per feedback_spec_scopes_not_tests these are in-scope Format-3 rules and belong in this item.
No test covers the EVALUATE/SEARCH-inside-imperative-statement-1 parse (defect 5). Given it is a SILENT mis-parse, it needs a dedicated parser-level fixture, not a golden.

No test covers a Format-3 PERFORM whose imperative-statement-1 contains an OUT-OF-LINE `PERFORM para` that raises. GR15 ('all statements contained within imperative-statement-1') suggests the performed paragraph is NOT in range, but the design never states the ruling, and the emitted `goto __pfEnd{N}` would be an illegal cross-switch-section jump if it were.

No negative fixture for `WHEN` naming a LEVEL-2 or LEVEL-1 name — which is REQUIRED to be legal here (the GR3d/GR3f/GR3g tiers) even though EcResolveLevel3 rejects non-level-3 names with COBOLNET0710. The design must state explicitly that the WHEN binder does NOT call EcResolveLevel3, and a test must prove COBOLNET0710 is not emitted.
corrections: DELETE proposed diagnostic COBOLNET1586. Instead call the existing shared reporter path with a new context string: `ctx.Edition.Error("COBOLNET0711", $"PERFORM (exception-checking) WHEN phrase: '{name}' is not an exception-name of ISO/IEC 1989 §14.6.13.1 (and not a valid EC-USER-/EC-IMP- name)")`, matching EcBinder.cs:97 / TurnState.cs:46 / ProcedureTableBuilder.cs:425. The remaining nine codes then occupy COBOLNET1578-1585 plus one, and the batch's next-free pointer advances accordingly (state the exact count to the deconfliction stage: NINE new codes, not ten).

Replace the three nonexistent type names in the GR16 FINALLY check with the real ones: `BoundGoTo`, `BoundGoToDepending`, `BoundExitParagraph`, `BoundStop`, `BoundStopLiteral` (no — StopLiteral does not transfer; exclude it), `BoundResume`, the GOBACK node produced by `Call.BindGoback` (read its return type before writing the check), and `BoundExitProgram`. Note explicitly that EXIT SECTION currently binds to `BoundUnsupported("EXIT SECTION")` (ControlFlowBinder.BindExit), so the GR16 check cannot detect it — either record that as a documented non-detection or implement EXIT SECTION first.

Do NOT push scope frames onto the TurnState instance. Either (a) remove the `Empty` singleton and have Build always return a fresh instance, or preferably (b) keep TurnState immutable and put the Format-3 scope stack on the per-bind `EcBindState` (where PerformWhenStack already lives), passing the active frames into `Turn.Enabled/WithLocation` as an argument. This eliminates the static-mutation bug and the AnyEnabled contract corruption in one move.

Leave `TurnState.AnyEnabled` and `AnyEnabledFor` untouched. Change EcBinder.EcWrap's early-out at EcBinder.cs:291 to `if (!ctx.EcState.Turn.AnyEnabled && ctx.EcState.PerformWhenStack.Count == 0) return bound;`. For the group-level gates, rely on `EcFeatures.HasPerformWhen` at BinderDriver.cs:83, and ADD a group-level accumulated set of WHEN-named exception-names on EcBindState so BinderDriver.cs:383's `ExternalDescribe` computation can also consult it: `... || Procedure.EcBinder.ExternalNames.Any(session.WhenNamedEcs.Covers)`.

Scope-tag the EXIT-PERFORM escape code. Replace the flat `-4` with a per-scope band, e.g. `return -(100 + scopeId);` from a handler, and emit the epilogue as `if (__r{id} == {-(100 + p.Id)}) goto __pfEnd{p.Id};`. Audit the four existing epilogue sites (EcEmitter.cs:132-133, EmitRaise ~:164, EmitSizeHandling, __IoCheckEc ~:349) so `if (__r != -2) throw;` cannot fire on the new band — route all four through the new EmitDispatchEpilogue helper as the spec already proposes.

Add an explicit design section and a parser fixture for the EVALUATE/SEARCH WHEN ambiguity. Recommended resolution: within imperative-statement-1 of a Format-3 PERFORM, require the explicit scope terminator (END-EVALUATE / END-SEARCH) on any nested statement that has WHEN clauses, and emit a dedicated diagnostic when it is absent, citing §14.4's imperative-statement/delimited-scope rules. Add a parser test asserting `WHEN OTHER EXCEPTION` after an unterminated EVALUATE produces the diagnostic rather than binding to evaluateWhenClause's `WHEN OTHER` alternative.

Either lower WHEN/OTHER/COMMON/FINALLY arm bodies into pc-space paragraphs and run them through the existing `__RunUse`/`__Dispatch(startPc, endPc)` mechanism (DispatchEmitter.cs:176-184) — the one-mechanism-per-job answer, which makes GO TO, EXIT PARAGRAPH, EXIT SECTION and NEXT SENTENCE work for free — or, if the generated-method fork is kept, add a written justification against feedback_singular_pattern AND a complete lowering for every dispatcher-level statement kind. A 'defensive InvalidOperationException' on legal COBOL is not acceptable under process rule 3.

Complete the GR3a/GR3b design before implementation: read DispatchEmitter.EmitUseMachinery (DispatchEmitter.cs:163-230) and the generated `__IoCheck` in full, decide where the file-name and open-mode WHEN bands live relative to the F1 declarative switch, and state it concretely. Do not leave 'verify at implement time' in a spec the implementer is to follow verbatim.

Set the constructs.json row's vcr field to `"VCR row 79 (PERFORM statement — exception-checking variant)"` (confirmed free and correct at docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md:196) and clear the `<!-- todo -->` marker on that row in the same change set.
Change `(WITH? LOCATION)?` to `(WITH LOCATION)?` to match the quoted format, or add a grammar comment citing the house optional-word precedent at CobolControlFlow.g4:180-182.

Add semanticChanges (not openQuestions) for §14.7.5 SIZE ERROR preemption, §14.9.1/§14.9.12 ACCEPT/DISPLAY return-to-end-of-statement, §14.9.14.3 SR6 (EXIT PROGRAM RAISING LAST in a WHEN), the unconditional ExceptionState set for a WHEN-selected condition, and §14.9.6 SR3 / §14.9.11 SR4 / §14.9.5 GR9. Each needs a named file and a test.

State explicitly in the EcBinder step-3 text that the WHEN binder must NOT use `EcResolveLevel3` (EcBinder.cs:~94) — level-1 and level-2 names are legal in a WHEN phrase (GR3d/GR3f/GR3g tiers) and COBOLNET0710 must not fire. Add a positive golden with `WHEN EC-BOUND` and `WHEN EC-ALL`.

Initialize the spec submodule (`git submodule update --init --recursive`) and re-verify every §/GR quotation — particularly §14.9.28.4 GR14/GR16/GR18/GR20/GR21/GR22, §14.6.13.1.3 item 4, §14.9.33.3 SR1 (which the researcher admits not reading), and the bare-`WHEN EXCEPTION` bracket — before any emitter shape is committed. Two of these readings (FINALLY-skipped-on-fatal, interior-TURN-legal) are baked into the code shape and are currently unverified against the authority.

specs.title: Wave H code half: MCS / COMMIT / ROLLBACK / VALIDATE recognize-and-name

spec.construct: WaveH-recognize-and-name — MCS (SEND/RECEIVE) · COMMIT/ROLLBACK · VALIDATE: recognize-and-name non-support diagnostics

specCitations.what: THE governing sentence for MCS + COMMIT/ROLLBACK: the mandatory compile-time warning mechanism, and the explicit excuse from parsing unsupported syntax correctly.
specCitations.quote: An implementation shall provide a warning mechanism at compile time to indicate use of syntactically-detectable processor-dependent language elements not supported by that implementation. Although this warning mechanism shall identify processor-dependent elements that are not supported, it is not required to diagnose syntax errors within this unsupported syntax. The implementor is not required to produce executable code when unsupported processor-dependent language elements are used.

specCitations.what: The license NOT to implement a processor-dependent element — makes recognize-and-name a legitimate END STATE, not an interim one.
specCitations.quote: Language elements that pertain to specific processor-dependent elements for which support is not claimed need not be implemented. … The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation.

specCitations.what: Optional-element disposition (governs VALIDATE): documentation, not implementation, is the obligation.
specCitations.quote: Language elements that an implementor may, but need not, implement are listed in A.4, Optional language element list. An implementor shall identify in user documentation the optional language elements for which that implementor claims support.

specCitations.what: Obsolete-element rule + its warning obligation (governs VALIDATE at 2023).
specCitations.quote: An implementation shall support obsolete language elements of the facilities for which support is claimed. … An implementation shall provide a warning mechanism that optionally may be invoked by the user at compile time to indicate use of an obsolete element in a compilation group.

specCitations.what: THE decisive license for VALIDATE non-support — obsolete ALONE would require support; obsolete AND optional does not.

specCitations.what: RECEIVE general format — the full operand tail the recognizer must swallow.
specCitations.quote: RECEIVE FROM data-name-1 GIVING identifier-1 data-name-2 [ CONTINUE AFTER { arithmetic-expression-1 SECONDS | MESSAGE RECEIVED } ] [ ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-1 ] [ NOT ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-2 ] [ END-RECEIVE ]

specCitations.quote: Format 1 (to-message-server): SEND TO { literal-1 | message-server-name-1 } FROM identifier-1 RETURNING data-name-1 [ ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-1 ] [ NOT ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-2 ] END-SEND. specCitations.what: ROLLBACK is a BARE VERB with the identical CONTINUE-equivalence rule.
specCitations.quote: 14.9.36.2 General format: ROLLBACK … GR1) If this statement is executed when there is no active APPLY COMMIT clause, then it has the same effect as a CONTINUE statement with no additional phrases.

currentState.summary: MANDATORY/OPTIONAL FINDING (the item explicitly requested): all three facilities are NON-MANDATORY, so recognize-and-name is a LEGITIMATE END STATE for D13's 100%-conforming target, not an interim step. MCS = processor-dependent (A.3 item 4) and COMMIT/ROLLBACK = processor-dependent (A.3 items 6–7): §4.2.6 says such elements 'need not be implemented' when support is not claimed. VALIDATE = optional (A.4.14) AND obsolete (F.2 item 5), and F.2's disposition paragraph exempts elements that are 'also optional' from the obligation to support obsolete elements. HOWEVER — and this is the load-bearing inversion — §4.2.6 paragraph 3 makes the compile-time WARNING MECHANISM itself mandatory ('shall provide'), and §4.2.13 makes an obsolete-element warning mechanism mandatory. Today MCS and VALIDATE produce a GENERIC parse error, not a named warning, and COMMIT/ROLLBACK produce an unrelated reserved-word ERROR. That is a live §4.2.6/§4.2.13 NON-CONFORMANCE. Wave H is therefore conformance-MANDATORY work even though the three facilities are not. AS-BUILT, empirically re-probed at HEAD 6d6c655d with the built Debug cobol.exe (all three scout claims CONFIRMED, no drift): (1) `RECEIVE FROM TG GIVING MSG TG.` at --std 2023 → `error COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input 'RECEIVEFROM'` + `cannot parse construct near 'FROM'`. (2) `VALIDATE REC.` at --std 2023, 2002 AND 85 → `error COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input 'VALIDATEREC'`. (3) `COMMIT.` / `ROLLBACK.` at --std 2023 → `error COBOLNET0901: 'COMMIT' is a reserved word in COBOL-2023 and cannot be used as a user-defined word (ISO 8.9)` (both words). COMMIT/ROLLBACK behave DIFFERENTLY from the other two because a bare word + period PARSES cleanly as a paragraph-name definition and is then rejected by the §8.9 funnel. NONE of RECEIVE/SEND/VALIDATE/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/MESSAGE-TAG is a lexer token — all lex as IDENTIFIER; their reserved-ness is decided post-parse by the ReservedWords table. There is no bound node, no emitter path, and no EC engine for any of the three. The reusable warning mechanism EXISTS and has exactly ONE live caller (SCREEN SECTION, COBOLNET1560). The legacy CobolSharp.Compiler tree offers NO algorithm worth porting here — non-support recognition is pure frontend/diagnostic plumbing with no runtime semantics.

editionGating.behaviorByEdition:
MCS (`RECEIVE FROM T GIVING M N.` / `SEND TO S FROM M …`): --std 85 → ACCEPTED with COBOLNET1578 warning, statement inert, program runs (facilityWord fires because IsReservedAt(85)=true; this correctly also names the '85 Communication Module, which is likewise unsupported). --std 2002 / 2014 → RECEIVE/SEND are USER WORDS, the predicate is false, the token stays a name; `RECEIVE FROM …` is not a statement and REJECTS with the generic COBOL0001 parse error — CORRECT below-facility behavior, not a regression. --std 2023 → ACCEPTED with COBOLNET1578. CONTINUITY at 2002/2014: `01 RECEIVE PIC X(4). … MOVE "A" TO RECEIVE.` must compile CLEAN (no 0901, no 1578).

COMMIT/ROLLBACK (`COMMIT.` / `ROLLBACK.`): --std 85 / 2002 / 2014 → the words are USER WORDS; `COMMIT.` parses as an ordinary empty paragraph named COMMIT and compiles CLEAN (no diagnostic at all). --std 2023 → ACCEPTED with COBOLNET1579 (was COBOLNET0901 error), empty paragraph falls through, program runs, exit code 0. CONTINUITY below 2023: `01 COMMIT PIC 9. 01 ROLLBACK PIC 9.` compiles clean. NEGATIVE at 2023: `MOVE 1 TO COMMIT` (COMMIT as an OPERAND, not statement-leading) must STILL emit COBOLNET0901 as an ERROR — the position guard must not swallow a genuine §8.9 violation.

VALIDATE (`VALIDATE REC.`): --std 85 → VALIDATE is a USER WORD; `VALIDATE REC` is not a statement and REJECTS with COBOL0001 — CORRECT below-facility behavior. --std 2002 / 2014 / 2023 → ACCEPTED with COBOLNET1580, inert, program runs. CONTINUITY at 85: `01 VALIDATE PIC X(10). … MOVE "X" TO VALIDATE.` must compile CLEAN.
editionGating.constructsJsonRow:
NO ROWS. This is a POSITIVE finding, not an omission, and it is stronger than the scout's 'not an introduction gate' assertion. VersionMatrixTests computes the expected outcome as `compiles iff introducedIn <= V and (removedIn null or V < removedIn)` (tests/version-matrix/constructs.json:_comment) — a MONOTONE step function. None of the three facilities fits it: (a) MCS is NON-MONOTONE (compiles at 85, fails at 2002/2014, compiles at 2023) and the matrix cannot express a gap; (b) COMMIT/ROLLBACK COMPILE at every edition (below 2023 as a paragraph name), so any `introducedIn: 2023` row would assert a non-compile at 85/2002/2014 and FAIL; (c) VALIDATE alone would fit (`introducedIn: 2002`), but adding a lone row would imply the matrix covers the family when it demonstrably cannot, and the compile at 2002+ is a WARNING outcome the matrix's boolean model does not distinguish from real support — which would falsely read as a support claim. The per-edition behavior above is instead pinned by the explicit unit tests in `tests` below. If a future stage wants matrix coverage, the matrix schema needs a warning-outcome field first — recorded in openQuestions.

NO reserved-words.json changes either: all eight relevant rows (COMMIT, MESSAGE, MESSAGE-TAG, RECEIVE, ROLLBACK, SEND, VALIDATE, VALIDATE-STATUS) already exist with correct per-edition flags and Confidence "high" — verified at ReservedWords.Table.cs:84/274/275/350/381/394/461/462.

risks: ⛔ THE DFA-POISONING HAZARD (DEVLOG 903) — the reason the previous attempt was reverted at 6ca8d184. Do NOT under any circumstance add an IDENTIFIER-led `statement` alternative. The empirically-proven failure was `| {facilityWord("RECEIVE")}? mcsFacilityStatement` where `mcsFacilityStatement : IDENTIFIER (~DOT)*` — it regressed `COMPUTE R = B-NOT A.` to 'no viable alternative at input A' at ALL editions, across three independent variants (original position, moved-to-end, ~DOT→dataReference*). The corrected mechanism in this spec is KEYWORD-TOKEN-LED (`(RECEIVE | SEND) (~DOT)*` / `VALIDATE (~DOT)*`), which is unreachable during arithmetic/boolean-factor prediction. If the implementer sees ANY new 'no viable alternative' failure after this change, the first hypothesis is that an IDENTIFIER lead crept back in.

⛔ THE §8.9 FUNNEL REGRESSION THE SCOUT MISSED (highest-value new finding). CheckedTokenTypes (VersionConformancePass.cs:1512-1546) checks IDENTIFIER position-blind. RECEIVE/SEND/VALIDATE reach it as IDENTIFIER today. Promoting them to lexer tokens REMOVES them from that path, and IsProvableUserWordPosition only covers the data-description entry-name, paragraph/section-name, SELECT file-name, and PROGRAM-ID slots — so `MOVE X TO VALIDATE` at 2023 would silently STOP emitting COBOLNET0901. Semantic change (C)(A) adds the three token types to the set; if it is skipped, the battery may still be green (nothing tests that case today) and a real conformance hole ships silently.

⛔ EXIT-CODE CHANGE — the exact feedback_guard_fast_not_ci_complete trap. `COMMIT.` / `ROLLBACK.` at --std 2023 fail TODAY (COBOLNET0901 error, nonzero exit) and will SUCCEED with a warning (zero exit) after the change. Any legacy CliExitCodeTests expectation pinned to the COMMIT-fails behavior must be updated in the same change set. guard-fast.sh does NOT cover CliExitCodeTests or the characterization gate — run the FULL CI-equivalent plus `gh run watch`, never guard-fast alone.

SHARED-LEXER CHANGE ⇒ MANDATORY FULL LEGACY GUARD. The generated ANTLR lexer/parser is shared with the frozen legacy CobolSharp.Compiler. Three new tokens make tokenization NON-byte-identical for the strings RECEIVE/SEND/VALIDATE — a strictly larger blast radius than an additive parser rule. Run the full legacy conformance suite + legacy CliExitCodeTests + the characterization gate, not guard-fast.sh. MITIGATING EVIDENCE (verified, contradicts the scout's warning): every CM-series NIST program (CM101M…CM401M, corpus.tsv:355-363) and DB205A (:373) is `pending` / 'cataloged (not asserted)', so the '85 comm-statement parse change reaches NO asserted legacy golden.

DIRECT-IDENTIFIER GRAMMAR SLOTS lose these three words. The parser references IDENTIFIER (not cobolWord) in a handful of places: `functionName : IDENTIFIER` (Core/CobolExpressions.g4:312), `typeClause : TYPE IS? IDENTIFIER` (Core/CobolData.g4:312), `(IN IDENTIFIER)` (Core/CobolData.g4:490), `enterOperand : IDENTIFIER | LINKAGE` (CobolParserCore.g4:941), the screen LINE/COLUMN `(IDENTIFIER | PLUS | PLUSWORD)?` slots (Core/CobolScreen.g4:66/71), `DECIMAL-POINT IS IDENTIFIER` (Core/CobolSpecialNames.g4:55), and `RESERVE integerLiteral IDENTIFIER?` (:128). After the change `TYPE IS VALIDATE` / a type named RECEIVE stops parsing. This is the accepted, already-shipped cost of the RETRY/SHARING/UNLOCK/CONSTANT/AS token precedent, and the affected slots are type-name/function-name/index-name slots where the word is §8.9-reserved at ≥ its edition anyway — but it IS a real narrowing, and if any battery failure lands in one of those rules this is the cause.

THE (~DOT)* SWALLOW IS GREEDY: `RECEIVE … DISPLAY "X".` collapses into one swallow and the DISPLAY is SILENTLY DROPPED. §4.2.6 excuses diagnosing syntax errors within unsupported syntax; it does NOT excuse concealing that a following valid statement was consumed — that would be exactly the silent-wrong-answer class the project forbids. MITIGATION (mandatory, built into the message template): the warning text ends with 'the remainder of the sentence is consumed', and docs/CONFORMANCE.md §4 records the rule. A non-greedy `(~DOT)*?` would eliminate the problem entirely — see openQuestions.

THE COMMIT/ROLLBACK POSITION GUARD MUST NOT OVER-FIRE (the DEVLOG-736 shared-rule class). VisitCobolWord is a SHARED visitor reached by every user word in the compilation unit; the guard is positively anchored on `ctx.Parent is ProcedureNameContext { Parent: ParagraphNameContext }`, which is the paragraph-DEFINITION shape only. A data item named COMMIT, a qualified reference, and a GO TO / PERFORM target (which route through procedureName under OTHER parents) all keep the genuine 0901. The negative fixture commit-as-operand-2023 is the guard against this specific over-fire.

THE 1579 GUARD SHARES _flaggedWords WITH 0901. That is deliberate (a word yields at most one of the two, deduped per distinct word exactly like 0901 at :1628). But it means a program that uses COMMIT BOTH as a paragraph AND as a data-name gets whichever occurrence the visitor reaches first. Given the traversal order that is source order; the behavior is defensible but arbitrary — record it in the code comment rather than leaving it as an accident.

SEVERITY BAND MIS-CLASSIFICATION: all three MUST be Warning, not Error. §4.2.6 ¶3 says 'The implementor is not required to produce executable code' — a permission, not a requirement to reject. If any of the three ships at Error severity the program stops compiling and the fix is a regression relative to the CONTINUE-equivalence that §14.9.7.4 GR1 / §14.9.36.4 GR1 actually prescribe for COMMIT/ROLLBACK.

Emitting a 2023 section citation against COBOL-85 source violates feedback_bare_end / feedback_spec_fidelity_discipline.

designDefects: ⛔ FUNCTIONAL BUG — SEND IS NEVER RECOGNIZED. The gate is `{facilityWord(RECEIVE)}? mcsFacilityStatement` but the rule is `mcsFacilityStatement : (RECEIVE | SEND) (~DOT)*`. facilityWord(int tokenType) returns false unless `CurrentToken.Type == tokenType`, so a statement starting with SEND fails the predicate and the alternative is never entered. Half the MCS surface (§14.9.38 Formats 1 and 2) stays a generic COBOL0001 error, yet the spec's own golden `mcs_nonsupport.cob` contains a SEND statement and its unit test asserts '2 x COBOLNET1578 (RECEIVE + SEND)'. The spec is internally inconsistent and would fail its own tests.

⛔ SUPERSET-GRAMMAR INVARIANT VIOLATION — EDITION GATING PUSHED INTO THE PARSER. docs/rearchitecture/DESIGN-version-conformance-pipeline.md:51 states the contract verbatim: 'superset parse — grammar recognizes the UNION of all editions; NO edition {isYYYY()}? gates'. facilityWord reads `Edition.Year` and therefore IS an edition gate, just spelled through the reserved-word table instead of is2023(). The design doc pins the ONLY two surviving grammar predicates by name (§ 'Two constructs cannot be ungated outright' — boolExprAhead and retryPhraseAhead, both identity-carrying forward detectors that do NOT read the edition; retryPhraseAhead explicitly DEFERS the edition question to is2002()). The spec adds a third exception, edition-reading, and does not update DESIGN-version-conformance-pipeline.md — violating both the invariant and process rule 4 (deep-dives updated in the same change set). Note the real justification the spec never states: at 2002/2014 RECEIVE/SEND are legal user words and a paragraph named `RECEIVE.` would collide with an ungated `RECEIVE (~DOT)*` statement arm. That collision analysis is what the design doc requires before an exception is granted, and it is absent.

⛔ THE (~DOT)* SWALLOW BREAKS EVERY BLOCK-STRUCTURED CONTEXT. `statement` is reachable from `statementBlock : statement+` (CobolParserCore.g4:665), which is the body of IF/PERFORM/EVALUATE/READ AT END/ON EXCEPTION etc. `IF A = 1 RECEIVE FROM T GIVING M N END-IF.` makes the swallow consume END-IF (END-IF is not DOT), so the enclosing ifStatement never closes and the sentence fails to parse. Same for PERFORM…END-PERFORM, EVALUATE…WHEN…END-EVALUATE, and any inline scope terminator. Result: no named warning at all — the §4.2.6 warning mechanism this change exists to satisfy is NOT satisfied for the most common real-world shapes, and the failure is a generic COBOL0001. The spec's risk list only contemplates 'a trailing statement in the same sentence is silently dropped' and misses this entirely. The `authorContent : ~DOT+` precedent it cites is NOT analogous: authorContent sits in the IDENTIFICATION DIVISION where no scope terminators exist.

⛔ COMMIT/ROLLBACK ARE NOT ACTUALLY RECOGNIZED AS STATEMENTS. §14.9.7.2 makes COMMIT a statement, usable anywhere a statement is permitted. The proposal adds NO grammar rule and instead refines a diagnostic at `ProcedureNameContext { Parent: ParagraphNameContext }` — a position reachable only via `paragraphName : {IsAtLineStart()}? procedureName` followed by DOT. Therefore `IF X COMMIT END-IF.`, `PERFORM UNTIL D ROLLBACK END-PERFORM.`, `DISPLAY "A" COMMIT.`, and any COMMIT not first-on-line at a paragraph boundary remain generic parse errors with no named diagnostic. The change's central conformance claim — that §4.2.6's mandatory warning mechanism becomes satisfied — is false for the COMMIT/ROLLBACK facility in all but one accidental syntactic position.

⛔ SILENT WRONG ANSWER — COMMIT/ROLLBACK-AS-PARAGRAPH SPLITS THE ENCLOSING PARAGRAPH AND CHANGES CONTROL FLOW. ProcedureTableBuilder.AddParagraph registers each paragraph as its own PC range. Given `P1. DISPLAY "A". COMMIT. DISPLAY "B".`, `PERFORM P1` now executes ONLY `DISPLAY "A"` and returns at the new P1/COMMIT boundary — `DISPLAY "B"` is skipped. §14.9.7.4 GR1 requires CONTINUE-equivalence, i.e. NO control-flow effect; this design produces a control-flow effect with no diagnostic. The proposed golden (`MAIN. DISPLAY "BEFORE". COMMIT. ROLLBACK. DISPLAY "AFTER".` with straight fall-through and no PERFORM) is precisely the one shape that cannot expose the bug. This defect alone makes the COMMIT/ROLLBACK half of the design unsound as written.

TWO MECHANISMS FOR ONE JOB (feedback_singular_pattern). The same §4.2.6/§4.2.7 non-support warning band is emitted from two unrelated layers by two different APIs: MCS/VALIDATE via `Ctx.Edition.Warning(code, msg)` in StatementBinder, COMMIT/ROLLBACK via `_p._sink.Report(new EditionDiagnostic(...))` inside VersionConformancePass.VisitCobolWord. The spec's own helper doc-comment calls itself 'The ONE §4.2.6/§4.2.7/§4.2.13 non-support emit shape' while the COMMIT/ROLLBACK site bypasses it.

THE 1579 GUARD POISONS _flaggedWords. Sharing `_flaggedWords` with the 0901 funnel means a program that defines a paragraph `COMMIT.` AND misuses COMMIT as a data-name loses the genuine COBOLNET0901 §8.9 ERROR entirely (whichever occurrence the visitor reaches first wins, and the guard runs first in source order). The spec records this as 'defensible but arbitrary'; it is not defensible — it converts a hard conformance error into silence.

DiagnosticDescriptor FIELD MISUSE. The 4th positional parameter is `Title` — documented at src/Cobol.Net.Editions/Diagnostics/DiagnosticDescriptor.cs:22-25 as 'A short human summary … the docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md row text', explicitly 'NOT the runtime message'. The four proposed descriptors put full multi-clause runtime sentences (with em-dashes and §-lists) in that slot, which will render as unreadable rows in the generated docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md and diverges from every existing row's style.

UNANALYSED SHARED-LEXER SIDE EFFECT. Setting `subscriptTrigger: true` for RECEIVE/SEND/VALIDATE does not merely add them to cobolWord — it adds them to the lexer's `_dataNameTokens` set (scripts/gen-cobol-words.ps1 header), so a '(' immediately after any of those three words now switches the shared lexer into SUBSCRIPT mode, for the frozen legacy CobolSharp.Compiler as well. The risks section discusses token addition but never this mode change.

corrections: Fix the SEND gate. Either write two keyword-led alternatives — `| {facilityWord(CobolLexer.RECEIVE)}? mcsReceiveStatement` and `| {facilityWord(CobolLexer.SEND)}? mcsSendStatement` with `mcsReceiveStatement : RECEIVE (~DOT)*` / `mcsSendStatement : SEND (~DOT)*` — or keep one rule and write the predicate as `{facilityWord(CobolLexer.RECEIVE) || facilityWord(CobolLexer.SEND)}?`. Two rules is preferable: the StatementBinder arms then key on distinct contexts and the per-verb warning count the unit test asserts becomes natural.

Replace the greedy sentence swallow with a scope-terminator-aware set, or drop the swallow. Minimum fix: `(~(DOT | END_IF | END_PERFORM | END_EVALUATE | END_SEARCH | END_READ | END_STRING | ELSE | WHEN | AT | NOT))*` is fragile and I do not recommend it. The sound fix is to PARSE the operand tails per §14.9.31.2 and §14.9.38.2 (they are short, closed, and fully specified in the quoted general formats) and terminate on END-RECEIVE/END-SEND or the phrase boundary, exactly as every other statement rule in this grammar does. §4.2.6's excuse from diagnosing syntax errors inside unsupported syntax is a permission, not a licence to break the enclosing sentence. If the swallow is kept anyway, it MUST be tested inside IF/PERFORM/EVALUATE bodies before the design is accepted.

Redesign the COMMIT/ROLLBACK half as real keyword-led statements, not a diagnostic refinement. specCitations.quote: The SUPPRESS statement inhibits the printing of a report group.

specCitations.what: General format — note ONLY 'SUPPRESS' is underlined; 'PRINTING' is not

specCitations.what: Format notation: proves PRINTING is an OPTIONAL word, so bare `SUPPRESS` is legal
specCitations.quote: Within each format, uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics of the format.

specCitations.what: Second, corroborating statement of the optional-word rule
specCitations.quote: Optional words are reserved words or context-sensitive words. They are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats. They may be written to add clarity when the clause or phrase in which they are defined is written in the source unit.

specCitations.what: The ONLY syntax rule — the legality context
specCitations.quote: The SUPPRESS statement may appear only in a USE BEFORE REPORTING procedure.

specCitations.what: Scope: which group is suppressed
specCitations.quote: The SUPPRESS statement inhibits printing only for the report group named in the USE procedure within which the SUPPRESS statement appears.

specCitations.what: Lifetime: one presentation only — drives the arm/clear bracketing around the BeforeReporting hook
specCitations.quote: The effect of the SUPPRESS statement is limited to the current instance of the report group.  NOTE  To ensure correct results, a SUPPRESS statement can be executed again on each further occasion that the associated report group is to be inhibited.

specCitations.what: The EXHAUSTIVE list of inhibited functions
specCitations.quote: When the SUPPRESS statement is executed, the following report group functions are inhibited: a) The printing of the print lines of the report group. b) Any page advance associated with the report group. c) The processing of any NEXT GROUP clause in the report group. d) Any changes to LINE-COUNTER associated with the report group.

specCitations.what: The explicit NON-inhibition — control-break processing is untouched
specCitations.quote: If the associated report group is a detail, the SUPPRESS statement does not affect the sensing for control breaks or the subsequent control break processing.

specCitations.what: Independent confirmation that BOTH counters are frozen, and the dummy-group equivalence that fixes the implementation shape
specCitations.quote: The values of PAGE-COUNTER and LINE-COUNTER are not affected by the processing of a dummy report group, nor by the processing of a report group whose printing is suppressed by means of the SUPPRESS statement.

risks: SHARED GRAMMAR ⇒ MANDATORY FULL LEGACY GUARD. There is exactly one .g4 tree in the repo (src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/**; `find src -name '*.g4'` returns 11 files, all under Cobol.Net.Frontend) and the legacy CobolSharp.Compiler consumes the same generated parser. Per CLAUDE.md / feedback_grammar_approval, this change set requires the FULL legacy guard (scripts/guard-fast.sh is NOT CI-complete — also run the legacy conformance suite and a -c Release leg), even though no legacy program contains SUPPRESS.

ANTLR REGEN REQUIRED. Generated/ is a gitignored build output; the build regenerates it (java + pwsh prerequisites). A stale test-bin compiler DLL will hide the new rule — build Cobol.Net.sln BEFORE any `dotnet test --no-build` (feedback_fresh_build_before_no_build_test).

DFA HAZARD: NONE IDENTIFIED. SUPPRESS is keyword-led (DEVLOG 903 rule satisfied) and — verified by grep over all 11 .g4 files — the SUPPRESS token is referenced by NO existing parser rule, so the new arm cannot collide. Likewise `suppressStatement` is not a shared rule reachable from another section, so the DEVLOG 736 shared-rule over-fire hazard does not apply.

STALE-LEDGER TRAP: the C5 ledger entry asserts the SUPPRESS token is 'used only by COPY … SUPPRESS PRINTING'. This is FALSE at HEAD — the preprocessor has zero suppress handling (COPY … SUPPRESS PRINTING is itself unimplemented). An implementer who trusts the ledger may go looking for a preprocessor interaction that does not exist, or may fear a token conflict that does not exist. Independently: if COPY SUPPRESS PRINTING is ever implemented it belongs in the PREPROCESSOR (§7.2.1 text manipulation), never in the parser — it must not be routed through suppressStatement.
STALE RUNTIME COMMENT: ReportWriter.cs:53 claims the suppression flag is already 'staged'. No such field exists. Fix the comment in the same change set (feedback_docs_current_state_only).
VISITOR FAN-OUT: adding a BoundStatement record breaks every IBoundVisitor implementor with CS0535 until arms are added. Do not hand-enumerate — build and let the compiler list them.

GR3c IS A CITED NO-OP TODAY. NEXT GROUP stages loud at bind (COBOLNET0899 report-next-group), so 'inhibit NEXT GROUP processing' has no reachable code path. This MUST be stated as a cited no-op in the PresentBody comment, so that whoever implements NEXT GROUP knows the suppression early-return already covers it (the return precedes any NEXT GROUP handling by construction).

SEMANTIC-BRANCH RISK (see openQuestions 1): the SUM-reset decision. If the opposite reading is later adopted, exactly one line moves (EndOfGroupSumReset out of the suppressed branch) and exactly one test flips (SuppressedControlFootingStillResetsSums) — the risk is contained by design.

NOT A RISK BUT WORTH STATING: the four Present* hook sites must ALL route through RunBeforeReporting. A direct `g.BeforeReporting?.Invoke()` left behind would leave a stale _suppressed armed from a previous group and silently suppress the wrong group. Enforce with a grep assertion in review: after this change, `BeforeReporting?.Invoke()` must appear exactly ONCE in ReportWriter.cs, inside RunBeforeReporting.
openQuestions: SUM RESET UNDER SUPPRESSION — the one genuinely ambiguous branch. §14.9.45.4 GR3 introduces its list with 'the following report group functions are inhibited' and enumerates exactly (a)–(d); the SUM reset is NOT among them, and §13.18.54.4 GR2 ties the reset to 'the end of the processing of the report group' — the group IS processed under SUPPRESS, only its printing is inhibited. I therefore specify that EndOfGroupSumReset STILL RUNS, reinforced by the practical argument that a suppressed CONTROL FOOTING which failed to reset would carry the ended control group's totals into the next one. The counter-argument is the §13.18.41.4 GR3g PRESENT WHEN precedent, where an absent entry neither prints nor resets — but GR3g is an explicit rule about an ABSENT entry, whereas SUPPRESS leaves the entry present and merely unprinted, so I judge the precedent inapplicable. Flagging because the spec does not settle it in one sentence; the decision is pinned by a named test so a reversal is a one-line change.

GROUP INDICATE / first-body-on-page STATE UNDER SUPPRESSION. §14.9.45.4 GR3 does not mention _indicateFresh, _firstBodyOnPage, or _firstBodySinceInitiate equivalents. I specify they are LEFT UNTOUCHED, reasoning from GR3a (nothing was printed, so the next presented detail is still the first presentation for §13.18.29 purposes) and §8.4.3.15.4 GR5's dummy-group equivalence (a dummy group likewise touches none of them, per the existing `if (lines.Length == 0) return;` shape). The spec never states this directly; I consider it the only reading consistent with GR3a but it is an inference, not a quotation.

PAGE FOOTING SUPPRESSED DURING A PAGE ADVANCE. If a PF's own USE BEFORE REPORTING procedure suppresses it, my design skips the PF but still completes the physical advance and the PAGE-COUNTER increment (they belong to the body group's §14.9.16.4 GR6 sequence, not to the PF — and GR3b speaks of the advance 'associated with the report group' that was suppressed). Reasonable and cited, but the spec does not address the case explicitly.

DECLARATIVE-CONTEXT PROBE PRECISION. `ctx.BindCursor >= d.StartPc && ctx.BindCursor <= d.EndPc` is copied verbatim from EcBinder.BindResume (the project's established SR1 shape). I did not independently verify that BindCursor is accurate for statements nested inside IF/PERFORM bodies within a declarative. If RESUME's SR1 check has a known nesting hole, SUPPRESS inherits it — worth one probe during implementation (a SUPPRESS inside an IF inside the declarative must be accepted; the golden test above exercises exactly that shape, so the hole would surface immediately).

REPORTGROUPMODEL EQUALITY. I did not read the ReportGroupModel declaration. specs.title: VALUE clause Format 2 + the glued-multi-literal corruption reject

spec.construct: VF4-value-format2 — VALUE clause Format 2 (table format) + the glued-multi-literal corruption reject

specCitations.what: The Format-2 (table) general format — the authoritative syntax this construct must parse
specCitations.quote: Format 2 (table): { VALUE IS | VALUES ARE } { { literal-1 } ... FROM ( { subscript-1 } ... ) [ TO ( { subscript-2 } ... ) ] } ...

specCitations.what: Format 1 takes EXACTLY ONE literal — the basis of the multi-literal reject
specCitations.quote: Format 1 (data-item): VALUE IS literal-1

specCitations.what: The bare multi-literal list is legal ONLY in the report-section format
specCitations.quote: Format 4 (report-section): { VALUE IS | VALUES ARE } Followed by: { literal-1 } ...

specCitations.what: Format 2 inherits the Format-1 syntax rules 10-15 (notably SR12 REDEFINES, SR13/14 group-level, SR15 screen)
specCitations.quote: 16) Syntax rules 10, 11,12,13,14,and 15 above apply.

specCitations.what: VALUE/VALUES equivalence
specCitations.quote: 17) The words VALUE and VALUES are equivalent.

specCitations.what: The Format-2 subject must be a table element — the SR18 reject
specCitations.quote: 18) A data description entry that contains the VALUE clause shall contain an OCCURS clause or be subordinate to a data description entry that contains an OCCURS clause.

specCitations.what: Subscript operand shape
specCitations.quote: 19) Subscript-1 and subscript-2 shall be integer numeric literals.

specCitations.what: FROM subscript count + order + range
specCitations.quote: 20) In one FROM phrase, there shall be one subscript-1 specified for each OCCURS clause for the subject of the entry or superordinate to that entry, specified in the same order as a subscripted reference to the subject of the entry would be specified. Each instance of subscript-1 shall not exceed the maximum number of occurrences specified in the OCCURS clause associated with that instance.

specCitations.what: TO subscript count + range + the not-before-FROM ordering rule
specCitations.quote: 21) If the TO phrase is specified, there shall be one subscript-2 specified for each OCCURS clause ... The specification of subscript-2 in one TO phrase shall be such that the table element associated with subscript-2 is the same occurrence or a successive occurrence of the table element associated with the corresponding subscript-1.

specCitations.what: The dynamic-capacity reject: no TO phrase against an OCCURS DYNAMIC without TO
specCitations.quote: 22) A VALUE clause without the TO phrase shall not be specified in the same entry as an OCCURS clause with a DYNAMIC phrase but no TO phrase, or in any entry subordinate to such an OCCURS clause.

specCitations.what: The dynamic-capacity higher-level equality rule
specCitations.quote: 23) If the TO phrase is specified and an OCCURS clause with a DYNAMIC phrase but no TO phrase is specified in the same entry or in any superordinate entry, the values of subscript-1 and subscript-2 corresponding to all levels higher than that of the OCCURS clause, if applicable, shall be equal

specCitations.what: Format 4's multi-operand rule — the report-section leg of the reject
specCitations.quote: 35) If the VALUE clause has more than one operand, the entry shall be a repeating entry or shall be subordinate to a repeating entry. The number of operands of the VALUE clause shall be equal to the number of repetitions of the repeating entry ...

specCitations.what: Format 2 inherits the Format-1 general rules (sectional take-effect, group, ODO, alignment, BWZ, screen)
specCitations.quote: 11) General rules 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 10 above apply.

specCitations.what: THE odometer algorithm — the core of the emitter design
specCitations.quote: 12) A format 2 VALUE clause initializes a table element to the value of literal-1. The table element initialized is identified by subscript-1. Consecutive table elements are initialized, in turn, to the value of successive occurrences of the literal-1. Consecutive table elements are referenced by incrementing by 1 the subscript that represents the least inclusive dimension of the table. When any reference to a subscript, prior to incrementing it, is equal to the maximum number of occurrences, or, in the case of a dynamic-capacity table, the expected number of occurrences, specified by its corresponding OCCURS clause, that subscript is set to 1 and the subscript for the next most inclusive dimension of the table is incremented by 1.

specCitations.what: Literal-list CYCLIC reuse under a TO phrase
specCitations.quote: 13) If the TO phrase is specified, all occurrences of literal-1 are reused, in the order specified, as a source during the initialization described in General rule 12. This repetition is done until the table element identified by subscript-2 is initialized.

specCitations.what: The implied TO when the TO phrase is omitted
specCitations.quote: 14) If the TO phrase is not specified, it is as if the TO phrase were specified with each subscript-2 as the maximum number of occurrences, or, in the case of a dynamic-capacity table, the expected number of occurrences, of the table associated with each corresponding subscript-1.

specCitations.what: Overlapping FROM phrases — LAST wins
specCitations.quote: 15) If multiple specifications of the FROM phrase reference the same table element, the value defined by the last specified FROM phrase in the VALUE clause is assigned to the table element.

specCitations.what: Dynamic-capacity initial-capacity computation from the VALUE clause
specCitations.quote: 16) If an OCCURS clause with the DYNAMIC phrase is specified in the same entry as the VALUE clause, or in any entry superordinate to it, the initial capacity of the associated dynamic-capacity table is calculated according to the following subrules. If more than one VALUE clause applies, the maximum value thus calculated becomes the initial capacity. a) If a TO phrase is specified in the VALUE clause, the initial capacity is increased, if necessary, to the value of the corresponding subscript-2, provided that this value does not lie outside the range defined by the minimum and expected capacity specified in the OCCURS clause. If the value of subscript-2 lies outside this range, the initial capacity is unchanged. b) If no TO phrase is specified in the VALUE clause, the initial capacity is set equal to the expected capacity specified in the OCCURS clause.

specCitations.what: The CONTRASTING Format-1 rule that the current emitter implements (every occurrence the same value)
specCitations.quote: 9) A VALUE clause specified in a data description entry that contains an OCCURS clause or in an entry that is subordinate to an OCCURS clause causes every occurrence of the associated data item to be assigned the specified value.

specCitations.what: The VALUE clause is one of the two initializers of a dynamic-capacity table's current capacity
specCitations.quote: The current capacity of a dynamic-capacity table may be initialized explicitly in the FROM phrase of the OCCURS clause or implicitly in the VALUE clause. If neither is specified, the current capacity is initialized to zero.

specCitations.what: The initial-state carve-out for a dynamic table defined by an entry WITH a VALUE clause
specCitations.quote: 6) For each dynamic-capacity table, except where the table is defined by an elementary entry with a VALUE clause, the capacity of the table is set to the minimum capacity specified in the corresponding OCCURS clause.

specCitations.what: The normative-annex worked example that must compile as a golden
specCitations.quote: The initial capacity of a dynamic-capacity table may be defined using the VALUE clause with a TO phrase and several operands: 01 town-record. 03 town-name PIC X(20) OCCURS DYNAMIC FROM 1 TO 20 VALUES ARE "Leeds", "Bordeaux", "Pisa" FROM (1) TO (3).  ... sets the initial capacity of the table to 3.

specCitations.what: The informative table-handling annex naming the three table-initialization techniques
specCitations.quote: 3) The value of selected table elements may be specified using VALUE clauses with or without the optional TO phrase.

currentState.summary: Format 2 does NOT parse at any --std, and the Format-1 path silently CORRUPTS multi-literal VALUEs by text-gluing them. (1) PARSE: `valueClause` (CobolData.g4:487-491) has no FROM/TO-subscript phrase, so the spec's own Annex-D.3.7 example dies with a raw COBOL0001 parse error — a reject-valid-input failure, the class the review policy stages loud. (2) BIND: the `valueItem` rule (CobolData.g4:493-496) is a GREEDY operand loop (`valueClauseOperand (…)*`), so `VALUE 1 2 3` / `VALUE 1, 2, 3` (COMMA_SEP is a skipped separator token, CobolLexer.g4:713) parse as ONE valueItem holding three operands; `ExtractValue` (DataBinder.cs:2189-2204) then returns `item.GetText()` — the concatenation of all three operand texts. Result: `VALUE 1 2 3` binds RawValue "123", `VALUE "A" "B"` binds `A"B`. Zero diagnostics at every edition. The ledger's original 'binds the FIRST literal' filing is WRONG — `FirstOrDefault` is taken over valueItemS, not operands, and a bare list collapses into a single valueItem. (3) EMIT: `ValueInitializer.FieldInit` (ValueInitializer.cs:32-35) initializes an OCCURS table as `Enumerable.Repeat(element, n)` — one identical initializer per occurrence, i.e. Format-1 GR9 only; there is no per-occurrence mechanism at all. Dynamic tables (:25-30) take ONE `() => seed` lambda, so GR12/GR16 are unreachable. (4) GATE: no constructs.json row, no ConstructRegistry row, no ParseArm gate, no diagnostic mentions §13.18.63 Format 2 anywhere. (5) The 88-level (Format 3) path is SEPARATE and correct — BindCondition (DataBinder.cs:1566-1615) iterates every valueItem and folds per operand; it never calls ExtractValue, so the reject designed below cannot regress it. (6) The report-section (Format 4) path DOES call the same corrupting ExtractValue (DataBinder.Reports.cs:413-414), but report OCCURS is already staged loud (ReportOccursInGroup, DataBinder.Reports.cs:408-411), so a SR35-conforming repeating report VALUE cannot reach it today. (7) LEGACY: no proven algorithm to port — the legacy CobolSharp.Compiler tree has no Format-2 implementation either; this is greenfield.

grammarChanges.change: add alternative (Format 2) — replace the single-alternative rule at lines 487-491 with a two-alternative rule, Format 2 FIRST
grammarChanges.orderingNote: Format 2 MUST be the first alternative. ANTLR picks the first matching alternative, and the two arms share the `(VALUE|VALUES) (IS|ARE)?` prefix — the adaptive-LL(*) decision resolves on the FROM keyword that terminates the table arm's operand loop. Placing the bare-list arm first would let it consume the literals and then die on the unconsumed FROM (exactly today's failure). Both arms are KEYWORD-LED (VALUE/VALUES), satisfying the DEVLOG-903 mechanism rule; no IDENTIFIER-led arm is introduced.

grammarChanges.change: add rule — new, placed immediately after valueClause and before valueItem
grammarChanges.orderingNote: No alternative ordering concern (single alternative). The `COMMA?` between operands and between subscripts mirrors valueClause's existing handling of a comma NOT followed by whitespace (COMMA_SEP is skipped; bare COMMA survives, CobolLexer.g4:713-714) — without it `VALUES ARE "a","b" FROM (1)` (no space after the comma) would fail.

semanticChanges.change:
THE Format-2 subsystem. Two entry points.

1) `private void BindTableValues(Core.ValueClauseTablePhraseContext[] phrases, List<TableValueSpec> into, string where)` — pure syntax capture, per phrase:
   - Literals = phrase.valueClauseOperand().Select(RawValueOperandText).ToList()  (reuses the EXISTING fold — §8.8.3 concatenation + §13.10.3 SR2 constant-name substitution — so Format 2 and Format 1 see the same currency).
   - From = the first paren's integerLiteral list parsed to int; To = the second paren's list or null.
   - SR19 shape: any subscript that does not parse to an int, or is < 1, -> COBOLNET1580 (message names SR19).
   - Ordinal = the phrase index.

2) `internal void TableValuePass()` — a POST-FOREST pass (dimensions and dynamic capacities are only known once the forest is built and OdoResolve/DynamicResolve have run). Call it from the same post-build sequence as UsageInheritancePass/OdoResolve/DynamicResolve, AFTER DynamicResolve (it reads OccursSpec.ExpectedMax) and AFTER ExpandTypes (so TYPE-copied Format-2 entries are covered). For every DataItem with TableValues.Count > 0:
   a. DIMENSION CHAIN — walk self-then-ancestors to the record root, collecting every entry whose OccursSpec is non-null; REVERSE to outermost-first (SR20 order). Call it `chain`.
   b. SR18 — chain empty => COBOLNET1579 ("contains a VALUE clause in the table format but neither it nor any superordinate entry has an OCCURS clause"), skip the item.
   c. SR16 -> SR12 — the entry (or any ancestor) has a REDEFINES clause => COBOLNET1579's sibling message; reuse COBOLNET1579 with the SR12 wording (one diagnostic, two SR branches, both cited).
   d. Per-dimension MAXIMUM: `Cap(d) = d.OccursSpec.IsDynamic ? d.OccursSpec.ExpectedMax : d.OccursSpec.Max` (GR12/GR14 both say 'the maximum number of occurrences, or, in the case of a dynamic-capacity table, the expected number of occurrences').
   e. SR20 — From.Count != chain.Count => COBOLNET1580 (count). From[i] > Cap(i) (when Cap(i) is known) => COBOLNET1580 (range).
   f. SR21 — when To is non-null: To.Count != chain.Count => COBOLNET1580; To[i] > Cap(i) => COBOLNET1580; and the ROW-MAJOR ordinal of To must be >= that of From (`Ordinal(v) = fold over dimensions: acc*Cap(i) + (v[i]-1)`) => COBOLNET1580 ("subscript-2 shall identify the same or a successive occurrence"). When a Cap is unknown (a dynamic dimension with no TO in its OCCURS), compare lexicographically instead.

   i. BUILD TableValueMap — process the specs in Ordinal order (GR15: later overwrites). For each spec: effectiveTo = spec.To ?? chain.Select(Cap) (GR14). Run the GR12 ODOMETER from From to effectiveTo inclusive: start at cursor = From; assign map[Key(cursor)] = Literals[k % Literals.Count] (GR13 cyclic reuse — for the no-TO case the same cycling applies, since GR14 makes it a TO case); k++; then increment the LAST (least inclusive) subscript; whenever a subscript's pre-increment value equals Cap(i) set it to 1 and carry into i-1 (GR12 verbatim); stop after the element equal to effectiveTo has been assigned. Guard the loop with a hard iteration cap = product of Caps to make a mis-specified range terminate.
      Key(cursor) = string.Join('.', cursor) — 1-based, outermost first.

GR16 DYNAMIC INITIAL CAPACITY — for each chain member d with IsDynamic, over ALL specs on this item: cand = spec.To is not null ? spec.To[indexOf(d)] : (d.OccursSpec.ExpectedMax ?? 0); if spec.To is not null and cand is OUTSIDE [d.OccursSpec.Min, d.OccursSpec.ExpectedMax] leave it unchanged (GR16a's proviso); take the MAX over specs and over every VALUE clause that applies, and raise d.OccursSpec.InitialCap to it (never lower — 'increased, if necessary').

The data-item format takes exactly one literal (ISO §13.18.63.2 Format 1); a literal LIST requires the table format's FROM (subscript) phrase (ISO §13.18.63.2 Format 2). [report-section variant appends: ... or a repeating report entry (ISO §13.18.63.3 SR35)]

data item 'X': a table-format VALUE clause requires the entry to contain an OCCURS clause or be subordinate to one (ISO §13.18.63.3 SR18). [SR12 branch: ... and shall not be specified in an entry containing a REDEFINES clause or subordinate to one (ISO §13.18.63.3 SR16 → SR12)]

data item 'X': the table-format VALUE clause's FROM/TO subscripts are invalid — one integer subscript is required for each OCCURS clause of the entry or superordinate to it, in subscripted-reference order, none exceeding that OCCURS clause's maximum (expected, for a dynamic-capacity table) number of occurrences, and subscript-2 shall identify the same or a successive occurrence of the element identified by subscript-1 (ISO §13.18.63.3 SR19/SR20/SR21).

data item 'X': the table-format VALUE clause conflicts with a dynamic-capacity OCCURS clause — a VALUE clause without a TO phrase may not be specified in, or subordinate to, an entry whose OCCURS DYNAMIC clause has no TO phrase (ISO §13.18.63.3 SR22); and when TO is specified against such an OCCURS clause, subscript-1 and subscript-2 shall be equal for every level higher than that OCCURS clause (SR23).
