risks: SHARED-RULE OVER-FIRE (DEVLOG 736 — the named recurring hazard). `valueClause` is reached from data-description entries, level-88 entries, report-group entries and screen entries. The 0900 gate MUST carry the `InGatedDataEntry(ctx)` positive guard exactly as VisitOccursClause does; without it a report or screen VALUE would raise a spurious 0900. Equally, the SR18/SR20 binder checks run only from BindEntry (the data-entry binder), never from DataBinder.Reports — verify no report/screen path reaches BindTableValues.

THE 1578 REJECT'S BLAST RADIUS is the single largest regression risk: the greedy operand loop has been ACCEPTING (and silently gluing) multi-literal VALUEs for the life of the greenfield tree, so some existing conformance golden or NIST/CCVS corpus program may depend on the glued value. Before committing, run the FULL battery (Conformance 3699 + unit 313 + char 33 + legacy 167) and grep the corpora for a data-item VALUE with two adjacent literal operands. If a legacy-corpus program relies on it, that is a CCVS-leniency decision for the owner, not a reason to soften the check — file it, do not silently downgrade to a warning.

EMITTER PATH THREADING vs the PhysicalModel CACHE. PhysicalModel.cs:87 bakes `Values.FieldInit(c)` into the Physical record with NO path, and GroupValueSlicer composes from those cached strings. The path-aware branch must bypass the cache and reproduce PhysicalChildrenOf's member naming/filtering exactly; a divergence (a missed FILLER rename, an included 88 or RENAMES child, a shared-storage member) emits uncompilable C#. Mitigate by making the direct-children projection call the SAME predicate PhysicalChildrenOf uses rather than re-deriving it.

DYNAMIC-TABLE SEED CHANGE touches Cobol.Net.Runtime (CobolDynTable). Keeping the existing `Func<T>` ctor as a delegating overload is mandatory so every existing dynamic-table golden emits identically; the emitted `__i switch { … }` must also handle occurrences beyond the expected capacity (the `_` arm) or a runtime capacity growth throws.

ANTLR DECISION COST on valueClause. The two alternatives share the `(VALUE|VALUES) (IS|ARE)?` prefix and both begin with a literal-operand loop, so the ALL(*) decision must look ahead past an unbounded literal list to the FROM keyword. This is a full-context prediction on a HOT rule (every data-description entry). Watch the parse-time regression on the largest corpus programs; if measurable, left-factor the prefix instead: `(VALUE|VALUES) (IS|ARE)? (valueClauseTablePhrase+ | valueItem (…)* … )`.

GR16's InitialCap write requires flipping OccursSpec.InitialCap from `init` to `set`. That property is currently a single-writer invariant; a second writer must be documented in its XML doc and the write must be MONOTONIC ('increased, if necessary') so the OCCURS clause's own FROM value is never lowered.

RESERVED-WORD / DFA: none. FROM, TO, VALUE, VALUES, THROUGH, THRU are already lexer keywords; no new token is introduced, no word becomes reserved, and both grammar alternatives are keyword-led (no IDENTIFIER-led arm — DEVLOG 903 satisfied).

LEGACY GUARD: CobolData.g4 is the SHARED grammar file, so the change set requires the FULL legacy guard (scripts/guard-fast.sh is NOT CI-complete — run the CI-equivalent incl. the characterization gate and the legacy CliExitCodeTests, and a `-c Release` leg).

SR21's row-major ordinal comparison is undefined when a dimension's capacity is unknown (a dynamic OCCURS with no TO). The design falls back to a lexicographic comparison there; that is a derived, not a quoted, rule — flagged in openQuestions.
openQuestions: INTRODUCTION EDITION AUTHORITY. The 2023 spec does not itself date the table format, and Annex E's VALUE rows (items 27/28/29/43) are all numeric-edited changes, not the table format. `introducedIn: 2002` is asserted from the COBOL-2002 standard's §13.16.63, which is NOT in specs/ — it is exactly the A1 authority-sufficiency gap the plan §11 records, and D18 pre-authorizes acquiring the historical standards on that trigger. The implementer should either confirm against an acquired 2002 text or record the row as a derived date with the standing 'derive from the 2002 standard' vcr wording used by the sibling 2002 rows.

SR12 (VALUE forbidden in a REDEFINES entry or subordinate to one) does not appear to be enforced for FORMAT 1 today — the only REDEFINES/VALUE interaction found is the BASED-clause check at DataBinder.cs:2029-2045. This spec enforces SR12 for Format 2 (via SR16's inheritance). Whether to extend the same check to Format 1 in this change set, or file it as a separate finding, is a scoping call for the batch owner. It is a real gap either way.

THE SCREEN SECTION reaches ExtractValue through one of the two identified call sites, but I did not trace which. SR15 restricts Format 1 in the screen section (alphanumeric/national literal, no figurative constant) and Format 2's SR16 inherits SR15 — so a Format-2 clause in the screen section is nonsensical but currently parseable. The implementer should confirm the screen path and decide whether COBOLNET1579's SR18 branch covers it (a screen entry with OCCURS would pass SR18) or whether an explicit screen-section reject is needed.

SR21's 'same or a successive occurrence' comparison across a dimension whose capacity is unknown at compile time (a dynamic OCCURS with no TO phrase) has no spec-stated resolution. The design falls back to lexicographic subscript comparison; SR23 already forces the higher-level subscripts equal in exactly that configuration, which makes the lexicographic and row-major answers coincide for the reachable cases — but that is my derivation, not a quotation.

GR16's 'If more than one VALUE clause applies, the maximum value thus calculated becomes the initial capacity' spans SIBLING entries subordinate to the same dynamic OCCURS, not just multiple phrases of one clause. The design takes the max over all specs on all items whose dimension chain includes that table; the implementer should confirm the pass iterates every such item before finalizing InitialCap (i.e. compute all candidates first, then write once).

GR6/GR9's interaction with an OCCURS DEPENDING table under a Format-2 VALUE (GR11 inherits GR6: initialization behaves as if the DEPENDING item held the MAXIMUM) is specified but not exercised by any test above. A golden combining OCCURS DEPENDING with a Format-2 VALUE should be added if the implementer can construct one that SR22/SR23 permit.

citationErrors: ANNEX NORMATIVITY MISSTATED. The spec cites "Annex D.3.7 ... the normative-annex worked example that must compile as a golden". Annex D is explicitly informative: specs/ISO_COBOL.md:41920-41921 reads "## Annex D" / "(informative)". The D.3.7 heading is at :43192 ("D.3.7 Dynamic-capacity tables") and the town-record example at :43239-43244 — the line numbers and content are correct, but calling it normative is wrong. It is a legitimate golden; it is not normative authority.

THE SECOND ANNEX CITATION IS UNLABELED AND ALSO INFORMATIVE. "Annex (spec at :42902)" quoting "3) The value of selected table elements may be specified using VALUE clauses with or without the optional TO phrase" is D.3.3 "Values of tables" (heading at :42894), inside the same informative Annex D. Cite it as "Annex D.3.3 (informative)".

§8.5.1.9 IS THE PARENT SUBCLAUSE, NOT THE LOCATION OF THE QUOTE. The quoted sentence ("The current capacity of a dynamic-capacity table may be initialized explicitly in the FROM phrase of the OCCURS clause or implicitly in the VALUE clause...") is at :8199, which falls under "### 8.5.1.9.1 General" (heading at :8187); "## 8.5.1.9 Dynamic-capacity tables" is at :8184. Cite §8.5.1.9.1.

SR21 QUOTE ELIDES A NORMATIVE SENTENCE BEHIND AN ELLIPSIS. The spec's quote is "21) If the TO phrase is specified, there shall be one subscript-2 specified for each OCCURS clause ... The specification of subscript-2 ...". The elided text is a full normative sentence: "specified in the same order as a subscripted reference to the subject of the entry would be specified. Each instance of subscript-2 shall not exceed the maximum number of occurrences specified in the OCCURS clause associated with that instance." In a document an implementer follows verbatim, hiding a shall-sentence behind "..." is a fidelity defect even though the design happens to implement the check.

THE DYNAMIC-CAPACITY CARVE-OUT IS ATTRIBUTED TO THE WRONG RULES. The design's Cap(d) = "IsDynamic ? ExpectedMax : Max" is applied to the SR20/SR21 bound checks. The phrase "or, in the case of a dynamic-capacity table, the expected number of occurrences" appears ONLY in GR12 and GR14 (verified verbatim at :23446 and :23455). SR20 and SR21 say only "the maximum number of occurrences specified in the OCCURS clause" with no dynamic carve-out. Using expected capacity as the SR20/SR21 bound is a derivation, not a quotation, and must be flagged as such (it is defensible — a DYNAMIC OCCURS has no stated maximum — but it is not what SR20/21 say).

CROSS-CHECKED AND CORRECT (no defect, recorded so the implementer does not re-derive): §13.18.63.2 Formats 1/2/4 quotes match :23150-23188; SR16, SR17, SR18, SR19, SR20, SR22, SR23, SR35 are verbatim; GR11, GR12, GR13, GR14, GR15, GR16(a)(b) and Format-1 GR9 are verbatim; §14.6.2.3.2 item 6 is verbatim at :24102; §13.18.49.4 GR1 (SAME AS — exclusion list omits VALUE) and §13.18.57.4 GR3 (TYPE — subject's own VALUE wins) are both correctly numbered and correctly read.

THE editionGating CLAIM "The four NEW diagnostics 1578-1581 are EDITION-INVARIANT ... 1579/1580/1581 fire at 2002+" is presented as a complete edition analysis, but it omits that Format 2 ALSO carries the two existing VALUE edition gates — Constructs.ValueNumericLiteralNumericEdited2023 (VCR-86, Annex E.3.3 item 43) and COBOLNET1570 (VCR-34, Annex E.2 item 27). Both are edition-VARIANT and both are bypassed by this design.

THE openQuestion "SR12 ... does not appear to be enforced for FORMAT 1 today" is asserted from a partial search. The surrounding region does enforce other VALUE syntax rules (SR9 at :1837, SR5/SR10 at :1008-1026, SR4/SR5 at :1941). The implementer must re-grep for a REDEFINES/VALUE check under a different diagnostic band before concluding it is absent; the spec's evidence list only cites the BASED check at :2029-2045, which is a different rule.
designDefects: SR16'S INHERITANCE IS CITED BUT ONLY ONE-SIXTH IMPLEMENTED. SR16 (verbatim, :23299): "Syntax rules 10, 11,12,13,14,and 15 above apply." The design's own `what` field says "notably SR12 REDEFINES, SR13/14 group-level, SR15 screen" — yet the binder pass implements ONLY SR12 (step c) and never SR10 (boolean literals), SR11 (editing characters), SR13 (group-level VALUE: literal-1 same category as the group; no VALUE at subordinate levels), SR14 (no JUSTIFIED/SYNCHRONIZED subordinates, all subordinates usage DISPLAY), or SR15 (screen-section literal restrictions). Test-scoped, not complete-to-spec.

ALL-FORMATS SR1-SR9 ARE NEVER APPLIED TO FORMAT-2 LITERALS. SR1 (subject shall not be a strongly-typed group item or a variable-length group), SR2 (numeric range + exactly representable), SR3 (signed literal requires a signed or sign-bearing receiver), SR4/SR5 (alphanumeric/national literal category and size per literal), SR6 (numeric literals permitted in formats 1, 2, and 4 for numeric-edited, converted per MOVE), SR7 (class conformance), SR8 (BLANK WHEN ZERO), SR9 (VALUE prohibited with USAGE FUNCTION-POINTER / MESSAGE-TAG / OBJECT-REFERENCE / PROGRAM-POINTER) are all headed "ALL FORMATS" at :23216 and therefore govern every literal-1 of a Format-2 clause. The design routes Format-2 literals into TableValues/TableValueMap and never through any of these checks. This is a spec-completeness defect AND a live regression of SR9, which is enforced today.

GR5 (INHERITED VIA GR11) MAKES THE GROUP-LEVEL EMITTER SHAPE WRONG. GR11 (:23444) inherits GR5 (:23392): "If a VALUE clause is specified in a data description entry of a group item, the group area is initialized without consideration for the individual elementary or group items contained within this group." The design's emitter routes a group item to `Slicer.ComposedInit(group, path)`, which composes member-by-member from the CHILDREN — the opposite of GR5. GroupValueSlicer's existing group-area slice branch is guarded on `group.RawValue`, which is null for a Format-2 entry, so a Format-2 VALUE on a group item (fully legal: SR18 only requires an OCCURS in the entry or a superordinate) silently takes the wrong path. No test in the spec covers a Format-2 VALUE on a group item.

THE 1578 REJECT UNCONDITIONALLY REJECTS LEGAL FORMAT-4 SOURCE. The proposed ExtractValue errors whenever `operands > 1`, in the report path too (only the message text differs). SR35 (:23347, quoted correctly by the design) expressly PERMITS more than one operand when "the entry shall be a repeating entry or shall be subordinate to a repeating entry", and GR23 (:23503) — never cited anywhere in the spec under review — defines the semantics: "If the VALUE clause has more than one operand, successive operands are assigned to successive repeating printable items, horizontally and then vertically, as applicable, in that hierarchy. If no further operands remain, assignment begins again from the first operand." The design's justification ("report OCCURS is already staged loud") is a current-limitation argument, not conformance. Rejecting valid input is precisely the failure class this construct exists to fix.

THE SCREEN-SECTION openQuestion INVERTS THE SPEC. openQuestion 3 calls a Format-2 clause in the screen section "nonsensical" and floats "an explicit screen-section reject". The spec contemplates it: SR16 inherits SR15 (the screen-section literal restrictions) and GR11 (:23444) inherits GR10 (:23440, "If a VALUE clause is specified for a screen item, literal-1 specifies the value of the screen item that is displayed..."). A screen entry may carry OCCURS. Implementing a screen-section reject would itself be a conformance defect.

GR2/GR3/GR4 (INHERITED VIA GR11) — SECTIONAL TAKE-EFFECT IS UNIMPLEMENTED. GR11 inherits GR2 (file section: VALUE takes effect only during INITIALIZE; initial value undefined), GR3 (linkage section: only during INITIALIZE), and GR4 (external items only during INITIALIZE; based items only during ALLOCATE/INITIALIZE). The entire emitter design is initial-state only (ValueInitializer field initializers + the CobolDynTable seed); nothing routes TableValueMap into the INITIALIZE-statement path. A Format-2 VALUE in the file/linkage section, or on an EXTERNAL/BASED item, is therefore either dropped or applied at the wrong time.

THE RUNTIME seedAt CHANGE IGNORES THE INITIALIZED GATE. The design says the new `Func<int,T> seedAt` ctor "is used both for the initial fill and for §8.5.1.9.5 new-occurrence seeding". §8.5.1.9.5 (:8234) conditions that seeding on the OCCURS clause: "If the INITIALIZED phrase is specified in the OCCURS clause of a dynamic-capacity table, any elementary items not referenced ... are first initialized ... Otherwise, the content of any unreferenced locations in the new table element and the content of the other new occurrences are undefined." Applying seedAt to new occurrences unconditionally over-initializes when INITIALIZED is absent.

THE GRAMMAR PERMITS `VALUE ARE` AND `VALUES IS`. The proposed arm is `(VALUE | VALUES) (IS | ARE)?`. Every general format (Formats 2, 3, 4, 5 at :23155-23203) presents the pairing as a two-choice brace — VALUE IS / VALUES ARE — and SR39 (:23364) states it: "If the word VALUE is specified, the word IS may be specified. If the word VALUES is specified, the word ARE may be specified." The historical arm already has this looseness; the new arm replicates it while citing the general format as authority for its shape. (Note SR39's placement under the FORMAT 5 heading makes its scope arguable — flag it, do not assert either way.)

SR20's UPPER-BOUND CHECK IS SILENTLY SKIPPED FOR DYNAMIC DIMENSIONS. Step (e) checks `From[i] > Cap(i)` only "when Cap(i) is known". For an OCCURS DYNAMIC with a minimum but no TO, Cap is null and no bound check runs at all. There is also no check of subscript-1 against the OCCURS minimum. State the intended posture explicitly rather than leaving a hole.

GR6 (OCCURS DEPENDING, INHERITED VIA GR11) IS DEFERRED TO openQuestions WITH NO DESIGN. GR6 (:23400) requires initialization to behave "as if the value of the data item referenced by the DEPENDING phrase ... is set to the maximum number of occurrences". The design's Cap(d) reads `OccursSpec.Max` without stating whether that is the ODO maximum. Since GR6 is inherited, this is a required branch, not an optional extra.

SR16 → SR10 (boolean literals + size), SR11 (editing characters), SR13 (group-level literal category; no subordinate VALUE), SR14 (no JUSTIFIED/SYNCHRONIZED subordinates; usage DISPLAY), SR15 (screen-section literal restrictions).

§8.5.1.9.5 — the INITIALIZED-phrase precondition on new-occurrence initialization.

TEST GAPS: no golden for a Format-2 VALUE on a GROUP item (GR5); none for multiple no-TO FROM phrases (GR14 + GR15 combined); none for national or boolean Format-2 literals (SR5/SR10); none for a screen-section Format-2 VALUE; none for a file/linkage-section Format-2 VALUE + INITIALIZE (GR2/GR3); none for a repeating report entry with multiple operands (SR35/GR23 positive case); none for OCCURS DEPENDING + Format 2 (acknowledged but not added).

VERIFIED TRUE (no defect), recorded so the implementer does not re-derive: the glue mechanism (greedy `valueItem : valueClauseOperand ({pred}? valueClauseOperand)*` at CobolData.g4:494-496 + `item.GetText()` at DataBinder.cs:2189-2204); FROM/TO are absent from src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Parsing/CobolLexerWordSet.g.cs's _dataNameTokens, so `FROM (1)` stays in DEFAULT mode; COBOLNET1577 is the highest catalog code, so 1578 is genuinely next free; constructs.json DOES accept `status` and `expectDiagnostic` keys (170 rows, key union verified), so the proposed row is schema-valid; `Constructs.ValueTableFormat2002` is the correct generated name; ValueInitializer/GroupValueSlicer/PhysicalModel:87 structure is exactly as described; `ALL "-"` is ONE figurativeConstant operand (CobolExpressions.g4:405-420), so the 1578 reject will NOT false-fire on the ~100 NIST `VALUE ALL "-"` sites; a corpus sweep for a genuine two-literal data-item VALUE found only NC216A.cob:72 `VALUE " ."` (a single literal containing a space) — the 1578 blast radius appears to be zero, which the spec listed as its #1 risk.
designDefects: ARCHITECTURAL — GR16 writes into the WRONG model field and corrupts dynamic-table MINIMUM-capacity semantics. The design says 'raise d.OccursSpec.InitialCap'. OccursSpec.InitialCap (OdoModel.cs:53) is `FROM integer-4 — the minimum / initial current capacity (§13.18.38 GR16)` and the emitter passes it as CobolDynTable's `min` parameter, which the runtime stores as `_min` and uses as a permanent FLOOR (CobolDynTable.cs:38, :107 `long target = n < _min ? _min : n;`). For the Annex D.3.7 golden (`OCCURS DYNAMIC FROM 1 TO 20 ... FROM (1) TO (3)`) the design would write 3 into InitialCap, making the table's MINIMUM capacity 3 — so a later `SET town-name TO 1` is silently clamped to 3. §8.5.1.9 (:8199) and §13.18.38 keep the OCCURS FROM (minimum) and the VALUE-derived initial capacity DISTINCT. The design's own headline golden is broken by its own model choice.

GRAMMAR/BINDER — the new Format-2 arm opens THREE new silent-accept holes, because valueClause is SHARED and only the data-entry binder is taught the new alternative. (a) Level 88: `88 C VALUE "A" FROM (1).` now parses; BindCondition (DataBinder.cs:1566-1615) loops `value.valueItem()`, which is EMPTY for the Format-2 arm, so the condition-name binds with ZERO values and is silently registered (DataBinder.cs:1616 `parent.Own88s.Add(cond)`) — no diagnostic at any --std. Format 3's syntax has no FROM phrase, so this must be rejected. (b) Report section: DataBinder.Reports.cs:413-414 calls ExtractValue, whose first line in the rewrite is `if (items.Length == 0) return null;` — a Format-2 clause in an RD entry is silently ignored. Format 4 has no FROM phrase either. (c) Screen section: parses, never bound, no diagnostic. Also note the VersionConformancePass gate uses InGatedDataEntry, which deliberately excludes report/screen/88 — so at --std 85 none of these three even gets the COBOLNET0900. The design is not complete over the shared rule's reach.

BINDER — the 1578 reject MISSES the THRU spelling of the same corruption. `int operands = items.Sum(vi => vi.valueClauseOperand().Length)` returns 0 for a `valueClauseRange` valueItem (its operands are nested inside valueClauseRange, CobolExpressions.g4:42-44). So `01 W PIC 999 VALUE 1 THRU 5.` — illegal in Format 1 (THRU exists only in Formats 3 and 5) — takes operands==0, skips the reject, falls through to `item.GetText()` and binds the glued RawValue "1THRU5". Identical corruption class, left live.

EMITTER — the GroupValueSlicer path-aware projection as written emits UNCOMPILABLE C# for any group containing a REDEFINES class. The proposed replacement is `group.Children.Where(c => !c.IsRenames && !c.IsCondition).Select(c => $"{c.CsName} = ...")`. PhysicalModel.BuildPhysicals (PhysicalModel.cs:59-88) does substantially more: a `RedefinesTier.StringCanonical` class emits ONE field named `cls.BackingCsName` with type string and init `RuntimeApi.StrStore(Codec.ImageInitOf(c), width)` (not `c.CsName`), non-canonical Tier-B members yield NOTHING, and a `RedefinesTier.Alias` non-canonical yields nothing. The design acknowledges the hazard in `risks` and then tells the implementer to 'mirror its predicate rather than guessing' — that is precisely the re-derivation the deliverable is supposed to eliminate, on the change the design itself calls the riskiest. This is not decision-complete.

GRAMMAR — the alternative-ordering rationale is factually wrong about disambiguation, in a way that matters. The orderingNote claims the table arm 'is disambiguated solely by the mandatory FROM keyword after the literal list'. In the SCREEN SECTION, `screenFromClause : FROM (dataReference | literal)` (CobolScreen.g4:108-110) is a sibling alternative of `valueClause` in the SAME `screenClause` rule (CobolScreen.g4:34-59), so `VALUE "A" FROM WS-Y` is a legal Format-1-VALUE-then-FROM-clause sequence. Disambiguation therefore requires looking ONE TOKEN PAST the FROM (to LPAREN), not at FROM itself. ALL(*) will resolve it correctly, so this is not fatal — but the stated rationale is wrong and the left-factored fallback the risks section proposes (`(VALUE|VALUES) (IS|ARE)? (valueClauseTablePhrase+ | valueItem ...)`) does not change the lookahead depth either. Verified safe: FROM/TO/OCCURS are NOT in `cobolWord` (CobolWords.g4:9-89), so the operand loop cannot swallow them; no IDENTIFIER-led arm; no new token; DEVLOG-903 satisfied.

DOC REGRESSION — the proposed `newText` for valueClause replaces the existing block comment but DROPS its Format-3 content ('For level-88 condition entries, valueItem supports THRU ranges. Format 3 (§13.18.63): WHEN SET TO FALSE IS literal for condition-names; IN alphabet-name for character comparisons.'). feedback_grammar_doc_sync requires the comment to stay complete.
missingSpecBranches: §13.18.63.3 SR2/SR4/SR5/SR6/SR10 (the 'ALL FORMATS' category rules) are never applied to the Format-2 literals. Format-1 values run ValidateValueCategory (DataBinder.cs:1927 `if (rawValue is { } rv && pic is not null) ValidateValueCategory(pic, rv, entryWhere);`). The design's TableValuePass builds TableValueMap and never validates a single literal, so `03 E PIC 999 OCCURS 3 VALUES ARE "ABC" FROM (1)` is accepted silently. SR2 says 'all literals in the VALUE clause'. Every literal-1 must go through ValidateValueCategory with the same where-string.

§13.18.63.3 SR13 (inherited via SR16) permits a GROUP-level VALUE, and the design has no path for a Format-2 VALUE on a GROUP item. TableValueMap is read only in `InitializerFor` (the elementary branch); GroupValueSlicer.ComposedInit's group-VALUE slice path keys off `group.RawValue` only. So `03 R OCCURS 3 VALUES ARE "ABCD" ... FROM (1) TO (3).` on a group binds a TableValueMap that nothing consumes — silently dropped. SR13's companion ('The VALUE clause shall not be specified at subordinate levels within this group') is also unenforced for Format 2.
§13.18.63.3 SR1 ('The subject of the entry shall not be a strongly-typed group item or a variable-length group') — ALL FORMATS, unchecked for Format 2.

§13.18.63.3 SR16 → SR14 (a group-level VALUE forbids JUSTIFIED/SYNCHRONIZED on subordinates and forces usage DISPLAY) — the design enumerates SR12/13/14/15 in prose as 'inherited' but only designs an enforcement for SR12. SR13/SR14 get no check.

specs.title: FILE-CONTROL COLLATING SEQUENCE clause — the standard-alphabet core leg

spec.construct: VF2-collating-file-control — FILE-CONTROL COLLATING SEQUENCE clause (ISO §12.4.5.7), Formats 1 + 2

specCitations.what: Purpose of the clause — it is INDEXED-file record-key ordering, not program/sort collation
specCitations.quote: The COLLATING SEQUENCE clause specifies the collating sequence to be used for the ordering of record keys and alternate record keys for an indexed file. Multiple collating sequences may be used by specifying a collating sequence clause unique to the primary key or to specific alternate record keys.

specCitations.what: Format 1 (file-level) general format
specCitations.quote: Option 1: `IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2 ]` · Option 2 (inner curly braces with two lines): `FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1` / `FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2`

specCitations.what: Format 2 (key-level) general format
specCitations.quote: `COLLATING SEQUENCE OF` followed by curly braces containing two options: `data-name-1` / `record-key-name-1` followed by `… IS alphabet-name-3`

specCitations.what: Format 1 syntax rules: alphabet classes and the one-clause rule
specCitations.quote: 1) Alphabet-name-1 shall reference an alphabet that defines an alphanumeric collating sequence.  2) Alphabet-name-2 shall reference an alphabet that defines a national collating sequence.  3) Only one file-level format COLLATING SEQUENCE clause may be specified in one file control entry.

specCitations.what: Format 2 syntax rules: operand provenance, no subscripts, class agreement, no duplicate operand
specCitations.quote: 4) Data-name-1 shall be a name specified as the data-name in an ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause or in a RECORD KEY clause in the file control entry.  5) Record-key-name-1 shall be a name specified as a record-key-name in an ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause or in a RECORD KEY clause…  6) Data-name-1 and record-key-name-1 shall not be subscripted.  7) When the class of data-name-1 or record-key-name-1 is national, alphabet-name-3 shall reference an alphabet that defines a national collating sequence; otherwise, alphabet-name-3 shall reference an alphabet that defines an alphanumeric collating sequence.  8) Neither data-name-1 nor record-key-name-1 shall be specified in more than one COLLATING SEQUENCE clause.

specCitations.what: The sequence is a FIXED FILE ATTRIBUTE fixed at creating OPEN
specCitations.quote: Each collating sequence is a fixed file attribute and the collating sequence is set upon the successful execution of an OPEN statement that creates the physical file. The collating sequence used is the one that applies as specified in the following General rules.

specCitations.what: File-level applicability by class, and the native default per class; key-level clauses win
specCitations.quote: 2) An alphanumeric collating sequence referenced by alphabet-name-1 applies to any record keys of class alphanumeric, whether primary or alternate, not specified in a key-level format of another COLLATING SEQUENCE clause in the file control entry.  3) A national collating sequence referenced by alphabet-name-2 applies to any record keys of class national… 4) If alphabet-name-1 is not specified in the file control entry, the native alphanumeric collating sequence applies… 5) If alphabet-name-2 is not specified in the file control entry, the native national collating sequence applies…

specCitations.what: Key-level applicability
specCitations.quote: 6) Alphabet-name-3 applies to record keys identified by data-name-1 or record-key-name-1.

specCitations.what: The clause is REPEATABLE and appears ONLY in the indexed file-control format
specCitations.quote: `[ collating-sequence-clause ] ...`  … `[ ORGANIZATION IS ] INDEXED`  … where collating-sequence-clause is described in 12.4.5.7, COLLATING SEQUENCE clause.

specCitations.what: The DEFAULT when no clause is present is NATIVE — NOT the program collating sequence (contrast SORT/MERGE GR5b)
specCitations.quote: 6) If no COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is specified:  a) the collating sequence for alphanumeric record keys, both primary and alternate, is the native alphanumeric collating sequence;  b) the collating sequence for national record keys, both primary and alternate, is the native national collating sequence.

specCitations.what: EXTERNAL file connector consistency requirement for this clause
specCitations.quote: If the file connector referenced by file-name-1 is an external file connector …, all file control entries in the run unit that reference this file connector shall have: … g) The same specification of COLLATING SEQUENCE clauses.

specCitations.what: Prime-key UNIQUENESS is decided under the file's collating sequence — so EQUALITY, not only ordering, is weighted
specCitations.quote: The value of the associated record key shall not be equal to the value of the same record key in another record in the file. The equality or inequality is based on the collating sequence used for the file according to the rules for a relation condition.

specCitations.what: record-key-name-1 exists only via the SOURCE form of RECORD KEY / ALTERNATE RECORD KEY
specCitations.quote: RECORD KEY IS followed by a brace containing two alternatives: - data-name-1 - record-key-name-1 SOURCE IS { data-name-2 } ...

specCitations.what: Processor-dependent leg: LOCALE- or literal-defined alphabets for indexed keys
specCitations.quote: 41) The capability of specifying a collating sequence for primary and alternate keys of an indexed file where the alphabet specified in the COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is defined in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph with the LOCALE phrase or with literals is dependent on the capabilities of the processor.

specCitations.what: Processor-dependent leg: cultural sequences and per-key differing sequences (Format 2)
specCitations.quote: 42) The functionality of culturally-dependent collating sequences, multiple alternate record keys with different collating sequences, and collating sequences different from the primary record key is dependent on the capabilities of the processor.

specCitations.what: The SOURCE key form (the only source of record-key-name-1) is processor-dependent; CONFORMANCE row 40 = Not claimed
specCitations.quote: 40) The capability of specifying the SOURCE phrase of the RECORD KEY clause and ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause is dependent on the capabilities of the processor.

specCitations.what: Informative worked example — attests the FOR phrase inside Format 2 and the equality-under-alphabet effect
specCitations.quote: COLLATING SEQUENCE OF altkey_1 altkey_2 FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS Universal-order … COLLATING SEQUENCE OF prim-key FOR NATIONAL IS Universal-order … Selection of a collating sequence that equates two or more characters can be used to make keys match when the actual binary coding differs.

currentState.summary: ABSENT end to end — the clause has ZERO grammar surface and therefore no bind, no emit, no runtime. It is a hard generic parse error at every --std (probe-verified at HEAD). The VF2 ledger entry is ACCURATE. However the ledger's scope narrowing ('the mandatory core residue = the uniform file-level Format 1 clause naming a STANDARD-phrase alphabet') is a TEST-SCOPED narrowing that the project rule forbids adopting: every piece of machinery the FULL clause needs already exists and is proven — CollatingTable/NationalAlphabetDef (the SPECIAL-NAMES alphabet registry), the shared collatingForPhrase subrule, the CollatingTable->ushort[] weights emission path, CobolString.Compare(left,right,ushort[] weights), and an IndexedConnector whose keys are already addressed by a keyIndex (-1 prime, i alternate) — so per-key (Format 2) collation is a small extension, not a new subsystem. IndexedConnector today compares EVERY key ordinally and its own header comment names §12.4.5.7 as an unimplemented seam.

grammarChanges.orderingNote: WITHIN the new rule the three inner alternatives are LL(1)-distinguishable on their first token (OF / FOR / {IS|cobolWord}), so order is safe; OF is listed first for readability. WITHIN fileControlClauses the new arm must be inserted AFTER lockModeClause and BEFORE vendorFileControlClause. It cannot collide with any sibling: no other file-control clause begins with COLLATING, and SEQUENCE is a distinct token from SEQUENTIAL (organizationType). It MUST precede vendorFileControlClause because that arm is genericClause (IDENTIFIER-led) — although genericClause provably cannot match a reserved COLLATING token today, keeping every keyword-led arm ahead of the vendor sink is the standing rule.

THE CORE RUNTIME CHANGE. Add per-key weights and route EVERY key comparison AND EVERY key equality test through them.

1. State + API:
     private readonly Dictionary<int, ushort[]> _keyWeights = [];   // -1 prime, i alternate (§12.4.5.7 GR2/GR6)
     public void SetKeyCollating(int keyIndex, ushort[] weights) => _keyWeights[keyIndex] = weights;
     private ushort[]? WeightsFor(int keyIndex) => _keyWeights.TryGetValue(keyIndex, out var w) ? w : null;
     /// <summary>Compare two values of key <paramref name="keyIndex"/> under that key's collating sequence
     /// (ISO §12.4.5.7 GR2/GR6; the native default is ordinal, §12.4.5.2 GR6a). §12.4.5.12 GR1 makes key
     /// EQUALITY relation-condition equality, so equality tests use this too — an alphabet that equates two
     /// characters makes their keys EQUAL (Annex D.13.3).</summary>
     private int KeyCompare(int keyIndex, string a, string b) =>
         WeightsFor(keyIndex) is { } w ? CobolString.Compare(a, b, w) : string.CompareOrdinal(a, b);
     private bool KeyEquals(int keyIndex, string a, string b) => KeyCompare(keyIndex, a, b) == 0;

2. Replace at every site (this list is exhaustive for the file as it stands at HEAD — re-grep for
   `CompareOrdinal`, `StringComparer.Ordinal`, and `KeyOf(` equality before declaring done):

editionGating.behaviorByEdition: COBOL-85: REJECT. The 85 file control entry has no COLLATING SEQUENCE clause at all (its clause set is SELECT/ASSIGN/RESERVE/ORGANIZATION/PADDING CHARACTER/RECORD DELIMITER/ACCESS MODE/RECORD KEY/ALTERNATE RECORD KEY/RELATIVE KEY/FILE STATUS). Per the superset-grammar rule the clause still PARSES at --std 85; the ParseArm gate reports COBOLNET0900 on recognition (Constructs.FileCollating2002). A key-level (OF) clause at 85 reports COBOLNET0900 TWICE — once for the base clause, once for Constructs.FileCollatingKeyLevel2002 — the same double-report shape the sibling alphabet/PCS gates produce. || COBOL-2002 / COBOL-2014 / COBOL-2023: ACCEPT, identical semantics. No edition-differing behaviour is known within 2002..2023 — the clause is unchanged in the 2023 text and does not appear in the 2023 new-features annex (Annex E), and no VCR row exists for it. || --permissive: unchanged from strict for this construct — it is an INTRODUCTION gate, not a removal, so EditionSeverityPolicy leaves it an Error below 2002 (permissive downgrades removals, not introductions). || ⚠ The 2002-vs-2014 boundary for the FOR ALPHANUMERIC/FOR NATIONAL and the Format 2 (OF) sub-forms is asserted, not verified from a primary 2002/2014 text — see openQuestions (the D18 A1 acquisition trigger).

tests.covers: §12.4.5.7 Format 1 IS alphabet-name-1 + GR2 + §12.4.5.12 GR1 (weighted ORDERING and weighted EQUALITY of the prime key). This is the branch that proves the feature does something, not merely that it parses.
tests.sketch: SPECIAL-NAMES. ALPHABET FOLD IS "a" ALSO "A", "b" ALSO "B", "c" ALSO "C".  SELECT IXF ... ORGANIZATION INDEXED ACCESS DYNAMIC RECORD KEY IS IX-KEY COLLATING SEQUENCE IS FOLD.  OPEN OUTPUT, WRITE keys "abc","ABD" (both succeed), then WRITE "ABC" -> INVALID KEY, FILE STATUS '22' because "ABC" EQUALS "abc" under FOLD (Annex D.13.3's own worked claim). CLOSE, OPEN INPUT, READ NEXT twice and DISPLAY the keys -> the FOLD order, not the ordinal order (lowercase 'abc' sorts with 'ABD' by folded weight, whereas ordinally 'ABD' < 'abc'). Expected .out pins both the '22' and the two keys in FOLD order.

tests.covers: §12.4.5.2 GR6a — with NO clause the sequence is NATIVE, and crucially NOT the program collating sequence. The regression this catches is the easy mistake of defaulting to ctx.Data.Collating (the SORT default).
tests.sketch: OBJECT-COMPUTER. X PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS REV.  SPECIAL-NAMES. ALPHABET REV IS "Z" THRU "A".  An indexed file with NO COLLATING SEQUENCE clause; WRITE "A","B","C" sequentially in ORDER (which succeeds only if the file order is NATIVE — under REV it would be a '21' sequence error). READ NEXT x3 -> A B C. Expected .out: A B C, all statuses '00'.

tests.covers: §12.4.5.7 Format 2 + GR6 + GR2 interaction: a file-level clause governs the keys NOT named in a key-level clause, and the key-level clause wins for the key it names (this is Annex A.3 item 42's per-key-differing case, which the CONFORMANCE change now claims).
tests.sketch: Two alphabets FOLD and REV. SELECT with RECORD KEY IS IX-KEY, ALTERNATE RECORD KEY IS IX-ALT WITH DUPLICATES, `COLLATING SEQUENCE IS FOLD` and `COLLATING SEQUENCE OF IX-ALT IS REV`. Write records whose prime keys are distinguishable under FOLD and whose alternate keys order differently under REV vs native. READ NEXT over the prime path, then START KEY IS = IX-ALT + READ NEXT over the alternate path. Expected .out pins prime order under FOLD and alternate order under REV.

tests.covers: §12.4.5.7 Format 1 second option (FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1) — proves the collatingForPhrase reuse binds to the SAME slot as the bare IS form.
tests.sketch: Identical program to file_collating_format1 with the clause written `COLLATING SEQUENCE FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS FOLD`; the expected .out is byte-identical to file_collating_format1.out.

tests.sketch: Under FOLD, START KEY IS GREATER THAN IX-KEY with the key area holding "abc"; assert the record positioned is the one FOLD-ordering selects (not the ordinal one). risks: DFA/ambiguity — the Format 1 trailing `cobolWord?` (alphabet-name-2) is GREEDY. `COLLATING SEQUENCE IS A1` followed by a vendorFileControlClause (genericClause, IDENTIFIER-led) can have the vendor clause's leading word swallowed as alphabet-name-2. This hazard already exists verbatim in programCollatingSequenceClause and sortCollatingPhrase, so it is a known-accepted shape rather than a new one, but in fileControlClauses the IDENTIFIER-led vendor sink makes it REACHABLE for the first time. Mitigation: the new arm is placed before vendorFileControlClause, and a conformance case with `COLLATING SEQUENCE IS A1` immediately followed by an unrecognized vendor clause should be added if the batch's grammar smoke pass surfaces it. Do NOT 'fix' it by reordering — that would change PCS/SORT behaviour too.

Shared-rule over-fire (DEVLOG 736) — collatingForPhrase is now consumed by THREE rules. Any parse-arm or binder visitor that pattern-matches on collatingForPhrase generically (rather than via its parent context) will now also fire inside file control entries. Grep every use of CollatingForPhraseContext before committing; today the only consumers reach it through their specific parent, so the risk is that the IMPLEMENTER adds a generic visitor. Explicitly: do not add VisitCollatingForPhrase to ParseArm.

BinderDriver.cs:108 guard change (>= 2023 becomes >= 2002 with an inner 2023 guard) touches the VCR-15/18/31 external-file consistency path, which has goldens and a --permissive severity contract. This is the single highest-regression edit in the change set. Run the full battery (Conformance 3699 / unit 313 / char 33 / legacy 167) specifically after it, and diff the 1573/1575 diagnostics before/after.

The runtime comparator sweep is a PATTERN, not a site (feedback_scan_all_similar): missing even one `string.CompareOrdinal` / `StringComparer.Ordinal` / `KeyOf(...) == ...` in IndexedConnector.cs yields a file that orders correctly but detects duplicates wrongly (or vice versa) — a silent data-correctness bug. Re-grep the whole file after editing and assert zero remaining ordinal comparisons over key values. The lock-identity sites (LastReadRecordId / MutationTargetRecordId) are the deliberate exceptions and must be commented as such.

Weighted EQUALITY is the counterintuitive part and the most likely to be dropped as 'ordering only'. §12.4.5.12 GR1 and Annex D.13.3 both make it explicit; the '22'-on-fold-equal golden is the fence. Dropping it produces a compiler that passes every ordering test and still violates the standard.

CobolString.Compare(left, right, ushort[] weights) is currently exercised only by SORT/table paths; using it in the file layer widens its blast radius. Confirm its pad semantics (the `pad = ' '` overload at CobolString.cs:104 vs the weights overload at :124) match the key-slice padding IndexedConnector.KeyOf already applies (PadRight with space). If the weighted overload pads differently, keys of unequal slice length compare inconsistently — check before wiring.

Reserved-word collisions: NONE. COLLATING, SEQUENCE, OF, FOR, ALPHANUMERIC, NATIONAL, IS are all pre-existing lexer tokens (COLLATING at CobolLexer.g4:367). No lexer change, therefore no new reserved word and no legacy-guard exposure from the word list.

Legacy guard: CobolIO.g4 is a SHARED .g4 (both the greenfield and legacy parsers consume the Core fragments), so this change requires the FULL legacy conformance suite in the same change set, not just guard-fast (feedback_legacy_suite_on_shared_corpus). Adding an alternative to fileControlClauses can only widen the accepted language, so a legacy regression would indicate a DFA disturbance rather than a semantic change — treat any legacy red as a stop-the-line.

Emission size: an inline `new ushort[]{256 entries}` per key per file is emitted at registration. A file with a prime plus four alternates all naming distinct literal alphabets emits five 256-element arrays into the generated C#. Acceptable, and the __COLLATE reuse covers the common case, but if the batch cares about generated-source size, hoisting per-alphabet static fields is the obvious follow-on (do NOT do it in this change set — it changes ProgramEmitter's field layout).
openQuestions: 2002-vs-2014 boundary, UNVERIFIED. I can establish from the 2023 text that the clause is not a 2023 addition (no Annex E entry; no VCR row) and from the 85 clause inventory that it does not exist at 85 — hence 2002 as the introduction. But whether the FOR ALPHANUMERIC / FOR NATIONAL options and Format 2 (the OF key-level form) were present in ISO/IEC 1989:2002 or arrived in 2014 CANNOT be determined from specs/ISO_COBOL.md alone. I have registered all of it at 2002 (consistent with the sibling rows program-collating-national-2002 and sort-collating-national-2002, which place the whole national-class surface at 2002). If the D18 historical-standards acquisition (the A1 trigger) lands, re-check and, if needed, split file-collating-key-level-2002 into a 2014 row — that is a one-line constructs.json edit plus a regen, by design.

SPEC-INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY in Format 2. The normative Figure 2 (§12.4.5.7.2) shows `COLLATING SEQUENCE OF {data-name-1|record-key-name-1} … IS alphabet-name-3` with NO FOR phrase, but the standard's own Annex D.13.3 examples write `COLLATING SEQUENCE OF altkey_1 altkey_2 FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS Universal-order` and `COLLATING SEQUENCE OF prim-key FOR NATIONAL IS Universal-order`. I have specified the grammar to ACCEPT both (the FOR phrase as a permissive superset), because rejecting a form the standard itself writes would be indefensible, and because SR7 makes the class a consequence of the KEY's class, so the FOR word carries no independent meaning. If the owner prefers strict-to-Figure-2, the change is deleting `collatingForPhrase |` from the OF branch and adding a negative fixture — but I recommend accepting.

§12.4.5.7 GR1 'fixed file attribute … set upon the successful execution of an OPEN statement that creates the physical file' is STAGED, deliberately. The declared sequence is applied at every OPEN from the compiled-in declaration; it is not persisted with the physical file, so a second run declaring a DIFFERENT sequence over the same file is not detected as a §9.1.13.6 file-attribute conflict ('39'). REASON: RecordFraming's on-disk store has no attribute header and adding one re-baselines every existing indexed golden. There is no compile-time diagnostic for the staged part because the missed condition is a runtime I-O status — hence a named CONFORMANCE.md §3 row instead. Owner may want this promoted to a real work item; I have not created one.

The national leg (alphabet-name-2 / FOR NATIONAL / a national alphabet in Format 2) is resolved and class-validated but has no reachable consumer, because D-N2 refuses national leaves in FD/SD record descriptions so no national record key can be described (§12.4.5.12 SR2 permits them; our data model does not yet). I followed the SortBindCollating precedent (validate, do not carry) rather than minting a fourth diagnostic, on the reasoning that a provably-unreachable rule is VACUOUS, not SILENT. If the owner reads this as the 'silent semantics' class the ledger objects to, mint a fourth code (COBOLNET1581, file-collating-national-key-unsupported) and reject the national surface loudly instead — that is a strictly smaller change than what is specified here.

CONFORMANCE.md rows 41 and 42 are being UPGRADED from 'Not claimed' to 'Partial'. That is an owner-visible conformance-posture change (the D13 instrument), justified because the machinery genuinely supports literal-phrase alphabets and per-key differing sequences, and only the ISO/IEC 14651 cultural/LOCALE leg remains unsupported. Flagging it explicitly because posture upgrades should not be made silently by an implementer.

I did NOT verify whether PictureCategory.National is the exact enum spelling used for the SR7 class test in this tree (I inferred it from the surrounding binder code). The implementer should confirm the category accessor on DataItem before writing that line; it is the only place in this spec where I am naming a member I have not read.

The SUPPRESS WHEN design tracked in PHASE-13-wave-c-scout.md keys its equality test on 'the file's collating sequence'. Once this lands, that design has a real dependency to consume (FileModel.PerKeyCollating / KeyCollating). I have not checked whether the SUPPRESS WHEN work is ahead of or behind this item in the batch order — if it is ahead, it will need a follow-up to switch from ordinal to weighted equality.

citationErrors: ⛔ WRONG SECTION (ships into user-visible diagnostic text): the spec cites "§12.4.5.2 GR6" for the native default and "§12.4.5.2 SR1(g)" for the EXTERNAL consistency rule. §12.4.5.2 is **Syntax rules** and contains only SR1–SR13 (SR1 = "The SELECT clause shall be specified first in the file control entry..."; SR8 = "Format 1 shall be specified only for an indexed file"). It has NO general rules and NO rule with lettered subparts. Both cited rules actually live in **§12.4.5.3 General rules** (ISO_COBOL.md:15180-15231): GR1(a)–(m) is the external-file-connector consistency list — verbatim GR1(g) = "The same specification of COLLATING SEQUENCE clauses." — and GR6 (under the FORMAT 1 heading) = "If no COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is specified: a) the collating sequence for alphanumeric record keys, both primary and alternate, is the native alphanumeric collating sequence; b) ... national ...".

⛔ WRONG RULE TYPE: the external-consistency requirement is a GENERAL rule (§12.4.5.3 GR1(g)), not a SYNTAX rule. The spec calls it "SR1(g)" in the specCitations block, in the COBOLNET1580 diagnostic *message string*, in the BinderDriver code comment, in the diagnostics table's specSection field, in the negative-fixture description, and in the FileModel XML doc comment. That is six places emitting a citation that does not exist.

⛔ WRONG SECTION for §12.4.5.12.4 GR1 attribution: the quoted prime-key uniqueness text is correct and verbatim at ISO_COBOL.md:15721, but the spec's `semanticChanges` runtime block re-cites the SAME rule as "§12.4.5.12 GR1" in one place and "§12.4.5.12.4 GR1" in another. More importantly the ALTERNATE-key duplicate site has its own governing rule that is never cited: **§12.4.5.6.4 GR4** (ISO_COBOL.md:15372) — "The DUPLICATES phrase specifies that the value of the associated alternate record key may be equal ...
